config_keys.effect: Setting it to "mt_opd" is what enables this whole subsystem. Read and then DELETED from the rollout config so it never reaches the vLLM worker.
Must be > 0 under mt_opd or the step raises. Sets K, the last axis of every tensor these kernels touch.
Selects the reward formula in compute_distillation_reward. refresh_opd_advantage (M4) is only mathematically valid for only_stu (mt_opd.py:376-377) and nothing enforces it.

student_p | teacher_p | none - which log-probs form the softmax weight over K in the OPD reward. Must match actor_rollout_ref.actor.opd_reward_weight_mode or M4 rebuilds a different reward than rollout produced.
Ordered list whose index i names teacher i. Teacher 0 is reward_model, teacher i>=1 is mt_reward_model_{i}. Also the whitelist for target_gradient_shares.
How many mt_reward_model_{i} overlays to register and init. Must equal len(teacher_domains) - 1, otherwise the per-step arity check at 2121-2126 raises.
"uniform" averages all teachers' log-probs; ANY other string (including a typo) takes the one-hot routing path. Never validated.
Parallel lists giving the M1 target gradient share per domain. Preferred form because a dict-valued Hydra override fails to compose on the executor (comment at 671-673). Length mismatch raises.
Dict form of the same thing, used only when the two lists are absent. None means M1 is off and compute_domain_loss_weights returns None, leaving the loss bit-identical to plain MT.

M2 strength alpha. False -> 0 (off), True -> 1.0 (full), or a float in [0,2] for a partial correction (mag**alpha). Requires target_gradient_shares to be set, and requires rm_scores at call time. alpha=0 recovers M1 exactly.

mean | q75 | q90 | top10 - which statistic reads the per-domain reward magnitude. The quantile/top10 forms exist because per-token |reward| correlates with length at r=-0.87 (math) / -0.80 (code), so a plain mean reads math's scale ~3.4x too low (comment at mt_opd.py:250-254). Validated only inside the kernel, not at trainer init.

divide: scale /= mag**alpha (the original; comments at mt_opd.py:290-296 record it as measured harmful on 2026-08-04/06 - IF loss weight snowballed 27 -> 91, grad token share 57% vs a 33% target). multiply: scale *= clamp((mag/ref)**alpha, 0.05, 20), so the gradient budget follows the REMAINING teacher gap. Note the harmful option is still the default.

With multiply, uses the run's own first-step magnitudes as ref instead of a running batch mean, so step 1 is exactly M1 and only the DRIFT moves shares. Requires reward_scale_direction=multiply and reward_scale_stat=mean (both raise otherwise).
none | mask | consensus. Anything else raises at init. none is a genuine object-identity passthrough, so the default MT path is untouched.

Absolute spread threshold in nats above which a token is contested. Also the threshold for the pure-instrumentation contested_frac. Measured context: mean spread 0.131 nats, only 0.70% of tokens exceed 1.0, max 29.2 - so 1.0 contests almost nothing.

When set (strictly in (0,1)), pins the FRACTION of tokens treated as contested instead of guessing an absolute nats value; overrides conflict_nats. Note the truthiness parse at ray_trainer.py:758 means 0.0 becomes None rather than raising.

Per-teacher overlay merged over config.reward_model. The launcher sets .enable, .model.path, .model.input_tokenizer, .model.use_remove_padding, .model.fsdp_config.param_offload. A missing key raises a named error at init.
Enables M4. Also causes teacher_on_student_log_probs to be carried into the actor micro-batch. A no-op when strictly on-policy (single minibatch and ppo_epochs=1).
The reward_weight_mode M4 reproduces. Must be kept in sync with actor_rollout_ref.rollout.reward_weight_mode by hand - nothing cross-checks them.

Not read by mt_opd.py, but the entire M1 premise assumes it: under token-mean each token contributes equally, so gradient share == token share. The measured divergence it corrects is IF holding 20% of prompts and 0.9% of tokens.

config_keys.default: must be "token_reward_direct" for the MT recipe
config_keys.effect: The estimator whose output refresh_opd_advantage reproduces (advantages = rm_scores * response_mask). Any other estimator makes M4's step-0 identity claim false.

entrypoints.signature: build_domain_weights(domains: Sequence[str] | np.ndarray | None, domain_order: list[str], device: torch.device | str, weighting: str = "domain_routing") -> torch.Tensor
entrypoints.what_it_does: Builds the [B, N] per-sample teacher weight matrix (B = batch, N = len(domain_order)). weighting=='uniform' or domains is None -> torch.full((b, n), 1/n) (lines 51-52). Otherwise a zeros [B,N] matrix with a single 1.0 at column domain_to_idx[str(d)] (one-hot routing, lines 54-59); a sample whose label is absent from domain_order falls back to a uniform 1/N row (lines 60-61). Returns float32 on `device`. Callers: ray_trainer.py:2128-2133; tests test_mt_opd_domain_metrics.py:173, test_mt_opd_batch_routing.py:225.

Contracts N teacher tensors of [B,T,K] against the [B,N] weight matrix: stacked = torch.stack(teacher_logprobs, dim=0) -> [N,B,T,K]; w = domain_weights.transpose(0,1).reshape(N,-1,1,1); return (w*stacked).sum(dim=0) -> [B,T,K] (lines 84-87). One-hot rows select exactly one teacher per sample; uniform rows produce the arithmetic mean of LOG-probs (a normalised geometric mean of probabilities, NOT a distribution mixture). Validates domain_weights.shape[-1]==N (76-79) and teacher_logprobs[0].dim()==3 (81-82). Allocates a new tensor, so teacher_logprobs[0] stays intact - the invariant test_mt_opd_domain_metrics.py:160-186 exists to protect. Callers: ray_trainer.py:2134-2136; two tests.

entrypoints.signature: compute_domain_share_metrics(domains: Sequence[str] | np.ndarray | None, response_mask: torch.Tensor, rm_scores: torch.Tensor | None = None) -> dict[str, float]
entrypoints.what_it_does: Flat metric dict, 4 or 5 keys per distinct domain, prefix `mt_opd/domain/{dom}/`. per_seq_tokens = mask.sum(-1); total_tokens = clamp(sum, min=1). prompt_share = n_d/B; token_share = tokens_d/total_tokens; prompt_count = n_d; mean_response_length = tokens_d/max(n_d,1). If rm_scores given: r is reduced with r.sum(dim=-1) when 3-D (lines 134-135, so signed cancellation over K happens BEFORE abs), reward_per_seq = (r.abs()*mask).sum(-1), and reward_abs_mean = sum over the domain's sequences / clamp(tokens_d,1) - i.e. mean |per-token reward| for that domain. Returns {} when domains is None or empty (116-117). Raises ValueError on response_mask.shape[0] != len(domains) (119-123). Caller: ray_trainer.py:2170-2176.

entrypoints.signature: compute_domain_loss_weights(domains, response_mask: torch.Tensor, target_shares: dict[str, float] | None = None, rm_scores: torch.Tensor | None = None, normalize_reward_scale: bool | float = False, reward_scale_stat: str = "mean", reward_scale_direction: str = "divide", reward_anchor: dict[str, float] | None = None) -> torch.Tensor | None
entrypoints.what_it_does: M1+M2. Returns a [B] float32 per-sequence loss weight, or None (leave the loss alone) when target_shares is None or domains is None/empty (207-208). M1: observed_d = tokens_d / total_tokens (this batch, self-calibrating); target_d = target_shares restricted to the domains present and renormalised to sum 1 (225-229; all-zero targets fall back to an equal 1/len(present)); scale_d = target_d / observed_d (line 288). M2 (alpha = 1.0 if normalize_reward_scale is True else float(...), must lie in [0,2]): mag_d = per-domain reward magnitude - reward_scale_stat 'mean' gives sum(|sum_K r| * mask)/tokens_d (262, 276-277), 'q75'/'q90' gives torch.quantile over that domain's strictly-positive real-token magnitudes (286-287), 'top10' gives the mean of the top numel//10 (282-284). direction 'divide': scale_d /= mag_d**alpha, skipped when mag_d <= 1e-8 (316-321, no upper clamp). direction 'multiply': fac = clamp((mag_d/ref_d)**alpha, 0.05, 20); scale_d *= fac (322-325), where ref_d = reward_anchor[d] when anchored, else a single scalar equal to the M1-scale-weighted mean magnitude sum(scale*mag)/sum(scale) (307-312). Final normalisation to token-weighted mean 1: weights *= total_tokens / sum(weights*per_seq) (333-334), so the overall loss scale (hence effective learning rate) is preserved and only relative shares move. Caller: ray_trainer.py:2202-2215.

entrypoints.signature: refresh_opd_advantage(student_top_k_log_probs: torch.Tensor, teacher_on_student_log_probs: torch.Tensor, response_mask: torch.Tensor, reward_weight_mode: str = "student_p") -> torch.Tensor
entrypoints.what_it_does: M4 (AsyncOPD-style). Rebuilds the OPD advantage from the CURRENT student's top-k log-probs, so the reward stops describing a student that no longer exists after an inner update. s = student.detach(); t = teacher.to(s.dtype); logits = s ('student_p') | t ('teacher_p') | zeros_like(s) ('none'); weights = exp(logits - logsumexp(logits, -1, keepdim)) i.e. a softmax over the K axis, nan_to_num'd; rm_scores = -(s - t) * weights; return rm_scores * response_mask.unsqueeze(-1). Shapes [B,T,K] in -> [B,T,K] out. This is exactly dp_actor.compute_distillation_reward's only_stu branch (dp_actor.py:710-714; valid_mask is all-ones there so the -inf masking at 696 is a no-op) followed by core_algos.compute_token_reward_direct_advantage (core_algos.py:897-899) - the documented step-0 identity. Costs zero extra forward passes because topk_log_probs was already computed for the gradient. Raises ValueError on shape mismatch (380-384) or unknown reward_weight_mode (394-395). Caller: dp_actor.py:1100-1107. NOT listed in __all__ (lines 14-21). No test file anywhere in the repo.

entrypoints.signature: apply_teacher_conflict_policy(routed_logprobs: torch.Tensor, teacher_logprobs: list[torch.Tensor], response_mask: torch.Tensor, policy: str = "none", conflict_nats: float = 1.0, conflict_quantile: float | None = None) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor | None, dict[str, float]]
entrypoints.what_it_does: M3. Turns cross-teacher agreement (which routing otherwise discards) into either a mask or a consensus target. spread = max_over_teachers(top1) - min_over_teachers(top1) per token, where top1 = stacked[..., 0].float() - index 0 of the K axis, the student's own top-1 candidate (449-450). Threshold = conflict_nats, overridden by torch.quantile(spread[mask.bool()], conflict_quantile) when the quantile is given (460-468). agree = spread <= thresh. policy 'none' (or fewer than 2 teachers): returns (routed_logprobs, None, {}) with the SAME object - a bit-identical passthrough (440-441). policy 'mask': target unchanged, token_weight = agree.to(dtype) rescaled by denom/kept so the total loss (and effective LR) is preserved (477-482). policy 'consensus': target = where(agree, stacked.mean(dim=0), routed_logprobs) - the across-teacher log-prob mean on agreeing tokens, routed teacher on contested ones (486-489); weight None. Metrics: mt_opd/conflict/policy_agree_frac, /policy_threshold_nats, plus /mask_rescale (mask) or /consensus_frac (consensus). Raises on unknown policy (438-439), bad quantile (461-465), teacher/routed shape mismatch (444-448). Caller: ray_trainer.py:2140-2147.

entrypoints.signature: compute_teacher_conflict_metrics(teacher_logprobs: list[torch.Tensor], response_mask: torch.Tensor, domains: Sequence[str] | np.ndarray | None = None, conflict_nats: float = 1.0) -> dict[str, float]
entrypoints.what_it_does: Pure instrumentation, same spread definition as the policy. Returns mt_opd/conflict/spread_mean = masked mean of spread, /contested_frac = masked mean of (spread > conflict_nats), /spread_max = (spread*mask).max(). When domains is supplied and len(domains)==B, adds mt_opd/conflict/{dom}/spread_mean and /{dom}/contested_frac per distinct domain (546-561). Returns {} for fewer than 2 teachers (525-526), since disagreement is undefined for one. Raises if stacking does not yield a 4-D tensor (530-533). Caller: ray_trainer.py:2177-2183.

files.role: The subsystem itself. 7 module-level functions, no classes, no state. Imports only numpy + torch + typing.Sequence. Docstrings carry measured numbers from real runs (response lengths math 11570 / code 9032 / IF 364; mean teacher spread 0.131 nats, max 29.2; IF gradient share 0.9%).

Only production caller of build_domain_weights / select_routed_teacher_logprobs / apply_teacher_conflict_policy / compute_domain_share_metrics / compute_teacher_conflict_metrics / compute_domain_loss_weights. Imports them at lines 76-83; parses every mt_opd.* Hydra key at 660-777; registers the extra teacher worker groups at 1427-1440 and 1492-1496; the whole MT-OPD reward block is 2100-2230.

Only caller of refresh_opd_advantage (import line 46, call line 1100). Also the only consumer of the tensor mt_opd.py produces for M1/M3: selects `domain_loss_weight` into the actor micro-batch (975-976) and multiplies it into `advantages` (1128-1132). Reference implementation of the OPD reward that refresh_opd_advantage must reproduce: compute_distillation_reward, lines 601-774 (only_stu branch 710-714).

`token_reward_direct` advantage estimator (lines 876-902): advantages = token_level_rewards * response_mask.unsqueeze(-1). This is the second half of the step-0 identity refresh_opd_advantage claims to reproduce.
Dataclass declaring the two M4 config keys: opd_refresh_advantage: bool = False (line 128), opd_reward_weight_mode: str = "student_p" (line 129).

M1 unit tests for compute_domain_loss_weights: exact target hit, unnormalised ratios, the token-weighted-mean-1 invariant, absent-domain renormalisation, numpy labels, and the advantage-scaling == mask-scaling equivalence the dp_actor implementation relies on (lines 132-155).

Tests compute_domain_share_metrics + compute_teacher_conflict_metrics + the routing pair. Lines 160-186 pin the aliasing bug: routing must not mutate teacher_logps[0], or conflict would compare a teacher to itself.
M2 (reward-scale) and M3 (conflict policy) tests, including the alpha=0 == M1 and anchored-at-current == M1 equivalences, the [0.05, 20] clamp, and the quantile-vs-absolute-threshold argument.

End-to-end check that non_tensor_batch['domain'] survives _get_gen_batch / repeat / union, then that build_domain_weights + select_routed_teacher_logprobs pick teacher 0 for math and teacher 1 for code (lines 210-237).

Released launcher. Sets ONLY reward_mode=mt_opd, +mt_opd.teacher_domains, +mt_opd.n_additional_teachers, and +mt_reward_model_i.*. None of the M1/M2/M3/M4 keys appear here - they must be passed through LOCAL_EXTRA_OVERRIDES.

gotchas: M3 'mask' does NOT mask tokens in the loss. apply_teacher_conflict_policy returns a [B, T] per-token weight and its docstring says it 'multiplies the per-token loss' (mt_opd.py:435-437), but the only production caller immediately collapses it to a per-sequence scalar: per_seq = (conflict_token_weight * response_mask).sum(-1) / response_mask.sum(-1).clamp(min=1.0) at ray_trainer.py:2218-2221, then folds it into domain_loss_weight. The realised effect is that a sequence is down-weighted in proportion to its fraction of agreeing tokens, while contested tokens inside a kept sequence still contribute their full gradient. The kernel's unit tests (test_mt_opd_m2_m3.py:260-294) verify the per-token contract that the integration never exercises.

Composing M1 and M3-mask silently changes the total loss scale. Each factor alone has token-weighted mean exactly 1 (dom_w by mt_opd.py:333-334; per_seq because sum_i per_seq_i*n_i = sum(weight*mask) = denom = total after the mask_rescale at 480-481). Their elementwise PRODUCT at ray_trainer.py:2222 is not re-normalised, so sum_i(dom_w_i * per_seq_i * n_i) / total != 1 in general and the effective learning rate drifts. Both docstrings advertise LR preservation as an invariant.

torch.quantile hard-fails above 2^24 elements. Verified on the installed torch 2.5.1: torch.quantile on a 17,000,000-element tensor raises RuntimeError('quantile() input tensor is too large'). Two reachable call sites: (a) mt_opd.py:468, real = spread[mask.bool()] over ALL real response tokens of the GLOBAL training batch (this runs on the driver, not a micro-batch) whenever conflict_quantile is set; (b) mt_opd.py:287, one domain's strictly-positive token magnitudes when reward_scale_stat is q75/q90. With the docstrings' own measured math response length of 11570 tokens, ~1450 math sequences in a batch cross the limit. 'top10' (lines 282-284, torch.topk) has no such limit.

Nothing enforces refresh_opd_advantage's only_stu precondition. The docstring states 'Only valid for top_k_strategy=only_stu' (mt_opd.py:376-377) and the softmax deliberately skips -inf masking on that basis (397-398), but dp_actor.py:1095-1099 gates the call on opd_refresh_advantage + key presence only. Under top_k_strategy='intersection' the shapes still match ([B,T,K] vs [B,T,K]) so the call succeeds and silently drops the overlap_mask that dp_actor.py:724-728 applies, producing a wrong reward. 'only_tch' is likewise shape-compatible and wrong. 'union'/'union-intersection' would at least trip the shape check at mt_opd.py:380-384 (student side is 2K, teacher side K).

M2 'divide' is documented as measured-harmful yet remains the default. The comment block at mt_opd.py:290-296 records that dividing by the current magnitude snowballs onto the fastest-learning domain as its gap collapses (IF loss weight 27 -> 91, gradient token share 57% against a 33% target, dated 2026-08-04/06), and ray_trainer.py:719-721 defaults reward_scale_direction to exactly that. Turning on mt_opd.normalize_reward_scale without also setting reward_scale_direction=multiply selects the path the authors' own measurements reject.

'divide' has no upper clamp; 'multiply' does. divide guards only against a vanishing magnitude (if m <= 1e-8: continue, mt_opd.py:319-320), so mag=1e-6 with alpha=1 multiplies the scale by 1e6 unclamped. multiply clamps the factor to [0.05, 20] (line 324). The M2 test suite only covers the divide case with mag exactly 0.0 (test_mt_opd_m2_m3.py:78-88), which takes the skip branch.

M2 breaks M1's exact-target guarantee by design. compute_domain_loss_weights only hits target_shares exactly when alpha == 0 or the anchor equals the current magnitudes (pinned by test_mt_opd_m2_m3.py:127-139 and 142-158). Reading mt_opd/domain/{dom}/token_share and expecting it to equal the configured target is wrong whenever normalize_reward_scale is on.

mt_opd.reward_scale_stat is validated only at first use, not at init. ray_trainer.py:718 reads it with no check, unlike reward_scale_direction (722-726) and conflict_policy (749-753). A typo therefore surfaces as a ValueError from mt_opd.py:239-240 during the first training step, after every model and worker group has been initialised. Related asymmetry: the non-mt_opd else branch (ray_trainer.py:766-777) sets every other mt_* attribute but omits self.mt_reward_scale_stat - currently unreachable because it is only read inside the mt_opd branch, but a latent AttributeError.

mt_opd.domain_weighting is never validated. mt_opd.py:51 treats any value other than the literal 'uniform' as one-hot routing, and ray_trainer.py:664 passes the raw string through. 'Uniform', 'uniform_avg', or a typo silently select routing.

Unknown domain labels fail silently, not loudly. A sample whose 'domain' string is absent from mt_opd.teacher_domains gets a uniform 1/N row (mt_opd.py:60-61) - i.e. an averaged teacher instead of a routed one - with no warning and no metric. The only visible trace is an extra mt_opd/domain/{unknown_label}/* metric group.

The M2 anchor is not checkpointed. self._mt_reward_anchor is created at ray_trainer.py:739 and populated once at 2197-2201; grep across the repo shows no save/load path (its only occurrences are lines 739, 774, 2191, 2197, 2211). Resuming a run re-anchors at the resume step's magnitudes, so the 'anchored' semantics ('step 1 is exactly M1, only the drift moves shares') silently restart from a different baseline.

The anchor is read out of the metrics dict, not recomputed. ray_trainer.py:2197-2201 pulls mt_opd/domain/{d}/reward_abs_mean by string key, which is why reward_scale_anchored hard-requires reward_scale_stat='mean' (checked at 734-738). Any change to compute_domain_share_metrics' key naming or its abs/sum ordering silently changes M2's reference. I verified the two computations are numerically identical today (mt_opd.py:137+153-155 vs 262+276-277).

A 3-D rm_scores is reduced sum-over-K BEFORE abs, in both consumers (mt_opd.py:134-135 and 259-260). So the magnitude is |sum_k r_k|, not sum_k |r_k| - signed cancellation across the K candidates happens first. Deliberate (it matches mt_opd/rm_scores_mean at ray_trainer.py:2156-2158 and is pinned by test_mt_opd_domain_metrics.py:79-84), but the opposite of what 'reward magnitude' usually means.

Averaging log-probs is not averaging distributions. Both the uniform-weighting path (mt_opd.py:87) and consensus (line 486) take the arithmetic mean over teachers of LOG-probabilities, i.e. an unnormalised geometric mean of probabilities. The result is not a normalised distribution over the K candidates, so a 'consensus target' does not correspond to any single teacher policy. compute_distillation_reward then consumes it as if it were a log-prob (dp_actor.py:711).

mt_opd/domain/{dom}/loss_weight logs one sample, not the domain. ray_trainer.py:2229 reads dom_w[sel[0]] - the first index belonging to that domain. Under M1/M2 alone every sample in a domain shares a weight so this is exact; once M3-mask folds a per-sequence factor in (2222), weights vary within a domain and the metric becomes an arbitrary representative.

M4 is a no-op in the default configuration. dp_actor.py:1016 defines on_policy = len(mini_batches) == 1 and ppo_epochs == 1, and 1095-1097 gates the refresh on `not on_policy`. With one minibatch per step and ppo_epochs=1, mt_opd/m4_advantage_refreshed never appears even with opd_refresh_advantage=True; it also requires advantages.dim() == 3 (line 1071).

refresh_opd_advantage is absent from __all__ (mt_opd.py:14-21) even though it is the single symbol dp_actor.py:46 imports. The explicit import works, but `from verl.workers.actor.mt_opd import *` would not pick it up. It is also the one function with no test anywhere in the repo (grep finds it only in mt_opd.py and dp_actor.py).

refresh_opd_advantage silently changes reward semantics if the two weight-mode keys disagree. actor_rollout_ref.rollout.reward_weight_mode (used at rollout, ray_trainer.py:1971/1984) and actor_rollout_ref.actor.opd_reward_weight_mode (used by M4, dp_actor.py:235-237) are independent config keys with the same default and no cross-check; the docstring only says 'must match the rollout-time setting' (mt_opd.py:374).

build_domain_weights(domains=None) returns shape [1, N], not [B, N] (b = 1 at mt_opd.py:49). It happens to work downstream because select_routed_teacher_logprobs reshapes to [N,1,1,1] and broadcasts over B, yielding a uniform teacher average. Unreachable from the trainer, which raises first at ray_trainer.py:2110-2114 - but any new caller can hit it. Similarly select_routed_teacher_logprobs would IndexError on an empty teacher list (line 80) rather than raise a named error.

No step-0 sanity assertions exist in mt_opd.py. The step-0 invariants are documented claims and pytest checks, not runtime assertions: refresh_opd_advantage's 'identical in construction to compute_distillation_reward + token_reward_direct at step 0' (mt_opd.py:377-378), alpha=0 == M1 and anchored-at-current == M1 (test_mt_opd_m2_m3.py:127-158), policy='none' returns the identical object (mt_opd.py:440-441, test at 233-240). Nothing verifies any of them at runtime, so a divergence between refresh_opd_advantage and compute_distillation_reward would go unnoticed.

conflict_quantile=0.0 is parsed to None rather than rejected. ray_trainer.py:758 uses `float(_q) if _q else None`, so 0.0 (and any falsy value) silently disables the quantile and falls back to conflict_nats, even though mt_opd.py:461-465 would have raised for 0.0. The trainer's own validation at 759-765 is therefore unreachable for 0.0.

MT-OPD is FSDP-only. grep for domain_loss_weight / mt_opd / refresh_opd in /data/ycfeng/Open-MOPD/training/verl/verl/workers/actor/megatron_actor.py returns nothing, so a Megatron actor silently ignores M1/M2/M3's per-sequence weight and M4 entirely while the trainer-side routing and metrics still run.

compute_domain_share_metrics and compute_domain_loss_weights build a Python index list per domain in an O(B) loop over labels (mt_opd.py:142-144, 270), and the conflict metrics build a torch.Tensor of indices per domain (549-553). Fine at B in the hundreds; it is per-step driver-side work that scales linearly with batch and domain count.

inputs.name: domains
inputs.shape_or_schema: numpy object array of str, length B, one label per sequence. Values must match mt_opd.teacher_domains entries for routing to hit (e.g. 'math'|'code'|'if'); str(d) is applied everywhere, and any label absent from domain_order silently falls back to a uniform 1/N teacher row.
inputs.source: batch.non_tensor_batch['domain'], originating from the training parquet column and explicitly preserved through _get_gen_batch (ray_trainer.py:1149-1151) and batch.repeat/union. Read at ray_trainer.py:2109; a missing key raises at 2110-2114.

inputs.name: response_mask
inputs.shape_or_schema: [B, T] float/bool, 1 on real response tokens. Padding must be 0 or every share, quantile and threshold is wrong.
inputs.source: batch.batch['response_mask'], created at ray_trainer.py:1943-1944 if absent.

inputs.name: teacher_logprobs / teacher_logps
inputs.shape_or_schema: list of N tensors, each [B, T, K]. Element 0 is teacher 0; elements 1..N-1 come from the renamed mt_teacher_{i}_on_student_log_probs keys. Index 0 of the K axis is treated as the student's top-1 candidate by both conflict functions.

inputs.name: rm_scores
inputs.shape_or_schema: [B, T] or [B, T, K]. A 3-D tensor is reduced with sum(dim=-1) BEFORE abs() in both consumers (mt_opd.py:134-135 and 259-260), matching mt_opd/rm_scores_mean at ray_trainer.py:2156-2158.
inputs.source: batch.batch['rm_scores'] returned by compute_distillation_reward (dp_actor.py:773). Passed to compute_domain_share_metrics (ray_trainer.py:2174) and compute_domain_loss_weights (2206).

inputs.name: target_shares
inputs.shape_or_schema: dict[str, float]; need not sum to 1 (ratios like {'math':2,'code':2,'if':1} work - renormalised at mt_opd.py:228-229). Domains absent from the batch are dropped and the rest renormalised. All-zero falls back to an equal split (226-227).
inputs.source: self.mt_target_gradient_shares, built from either mt_opd.target_share_domains + mt_opd.target_share_values (parallel lists, ray_trainer.py:675-688) or mt_opd.target_gradient_shares (dict, 689-695).

inputs.name: reward_anchor
inputs.shape_or_schema: dict[str, float], one entry per domain present in the batch (missing entries raise at mt_opd.py:245-248). Semantically the run's own first-step per-domain reward_abs_mean.
inputs.source: self._mt_reward_anchor, captured once from the metrics dict at ray_trainer.py:2197-2201. Driver-local, not persisted.

inputs.name: student_top_k_log_probs (M4)
inputs.shape_or_schema: [B, T, K] from the CURRENT weights on the same student_top_k_ids. Must be detached - the docstring (mt_opd.py:368-370) says so explicitly and .detach() is applied defensively at line 385, because this is a reward and gradient through it would change the objective.
inputs.source: topk_log_probs, the 4th return of dp_actor._forward_micro_batch, passed at dp_actor.py:1101.

inputs.name: teacher_on_student_log_probs (M4)
inputs.shape_or_schema: [B, T, K] frozen-teacher log-probs on the same ids. Cacheable forever, which is why the refresh costs no extra forward pass. In MT mode this is the ROUTED (and possibly consensus-substituted) tensor, because ray_trainer.py:2149 overwrote the key.
inputs.source: model_inputs['teacher_on_student_log_probs'], selected into the actor micro-batch at dp_actor.py:985-986.

inputs.name: conflict_nats / conflict_quantile
inputs.shape_or_schema: float; the quantile must lie strictly in (0,1), and when given it OVERRIDES conflict_nats entirely (mt_opd.py:460-468).
inputs.source: mt_opd.conflict_nats / mt_opd.conflict_quantile via ray_trainer.py:754-765, passed at 2145-2146.

open_mopd_specific.what: The entire file mt_opd.py (562 lines, 7 functions) is an Open-MOPD addition.
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Module docstring names MT-OPD and domain routing; every symbol matches the Open-MOPD naming signals (mt_opd/*, teacher_domains, domain_weighting, target_gradient_shares); and it is not re-exported from verl/workers/actor/__init__.py, whose __all__ lists only BasePPOActor and DataParallelPPOActor (lines 15-18) - a bolt-on module upstream's package surface does not know about.

open_mopd_specific.what: reward_mode='mt_opd' branch in the trainer's reward stage, and the mt_rm_wgs multi-teacher worker-group fan-out.
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Upstream verl has one reward model role. This adds N extra RewardModel-class worker groups keyed mt_rm_{i} from mt_reward_model_{i} config overlays, renames each one's teacher_on_student_log_probs into mt_teacher_{i}_on_student_log_probs, and overwrites the canonical teacher key with the routed mix at line 2149.

open_mopd_specific.what: domain_loss_weight as a first-class actor batch key.
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: A per-sequence loss scaler with no upstream analogue. The comments explicitly justify applying it to `advantages` rather than `response_mask` because response_mask is also the averaging mask for ppo_kl and pg_clipfrac - an upstream-verl-specific constraint the patch had to work around. Absent from megatron_actor.py entirely, so MT-OPD is FSDP-only.

open_mopd_specific.what: refresh_opd_advantage (M4) wired into the actor inner loop.
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Reward-staleness correction has no upstream equivalent (upstream corrects sampling-distribution staleness with importance sampling only). The docstring argues explicitly that IS cannot repair a stale reward, and cites AsyncOPD's 1.6-3.8x throughput at matched accuracy.

open_mopd_specific.what: Cross-teacher conflict as a signal (M3), presented as the recipe's structural advantage over a single mixed-reward run.
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Only exists because the MT path already pays for every teacher to score every student token. The docstrings state the claim twice (lines 415-418, 502-505): MixRL sees one scalar per domain, never N opinions on the same token.

open_mopd_specific.what: domain label plumbed through generation so post-rollout routing is possible.
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: 'domain' is added to the reward_model_keys set that _get_gen_batch refuses to pop, with a comment naming MT-OPD as the reason. Regression-tested in test_mt_opd_batch_routing.py:46-58 and 210-237.

open_mopd_specific.what: Per-domain quota preservation inside dynamic filtering.
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: _take_complete_groups / _has_complete_groups take a hardcoded domain_order ('math','code','if') and enforce exact per-domain quotas, raising when unavailable. Upstream only trims to k unique uids. Adjacent to this subsystem: it is what keeps every domain present in the batch, which compute_domain_loss_weights' present-domain renormalisation depends on.

outputs.consumer: select_routed_teacher_logprobs at ray_trainer.py:2134-2136. Not written to the batch.
outputs.name: domain_weights
outputs.shape_or_schema: [B, N] float32 on the teacher tensors' device; rows are one-hot (routing) or 1/N (uniform / unknown label).

outputs.consumer: Written over batch.batch['teacher_on_student_log_probs'] at ray_trainer.py:2149, then read by compute_distillation_reward (dp_actor.py:663) and, when M4 is on, by refresh_opd_advantage.
outputs.name: routed teacher target
outputs.shape_or_schema: [B, T, K], same dtype as the stacked teacher tensors.

outputs.consumer: ray_trainer.py:2218-2222, where it is averaged per sequence and multiplied into dom_w. Never reaches the loss as a per-token tensor.
outputs.name: conflict_token_weight
outputs.shape_or_schema: [B, T] in routed_logprobs' dtype, or None. 0 on contested tokens, denom/kept (>= 1) on agreeing ones; padding positions are NOT zeroed. None for policy none/consensus or fewer than 2 teachers.

outputs.consumer: batch.batch['domain_loss_weight'] (ray_trainer.py:2224) -> dp_actor.py:975-976 select_keys -> dp_actor.py:1128-1132 advantages *= weight.view(-1,1,1).
outputs.name: domain_loss_weight
outputs.shape_or_schema: [B] float32, token-weighted mean exactly 1 when M1 alone or M3-mask alone; see gotchas for the composed case.

outputs.consumer: Local variable `advantages` in dp_actor.update_policy (1100-1107), then M1 weighting (1128-1132), then the policy loss.
outputs.name: refreshed advantages
outputs.shape_or_schema: [B, T, K], response-masked. Numerically equal to compute_distillation_reward(only_stu) + token_reward_direct evaluated at the current weights.

outputs.consumer: metrics dict at ray_trainer.py:2170-2176 -> the swanlab/console logger; reward_abs_mean is additionally consumed programmatically as the M2 anchor at 2197-2201.
outputs.name: mt_opd/domain/{dom}/{prompt_share,token_share,prompt_count,mean_response_length,reward_abs_mean}
outputs.shape_or_schema: flat dict[str, float], 5 keys per distinct domain label in the batch (4 without rm_scores).

outputs.consumer: metrics at ray_trainer.py:2177-2183.
outputs.name: mt_opd/conflict/{spread_mean,contested_frac,spread_max} and mt_opd/conflict/{dom}/{spread_mean,contested_frac}
outputs.shape_or_schema: flat dict[str, float]; {} when fewer than 2 teachers.

outputs.consumer: metrics.update(_cm) at ray_trainer.py:2148.
outputs.name: mt_opd/conflict/{policy_agree_frac,policy_threshold_nats,mask_rescale,consensus_frac}
outputs.shape_or_schema: flat dict[str, float]; mask_rescale only for policy=mask, consensus_frac only for policy=consensus (a duplicate of policy_agree_frac, mt_opd.py:490); {} for policy=none.

outputs.consumer: ray_trainer.py:2156-2162 and 2225-2230; dp_actor.py:1108.
outputs.name: mt_opd/rm_scores_mean, mt_opd/teacher_entropy, mt_opd/domain/{dom}/loss_weight, mt_opd/m4_advantage_refreshed
outputs.shape_or_schema: floats emitted by the callers, not by mt_opd.py.

report.purpose: A dependency-light, side-effect-free numeric library (numpy + torch only, no verl imports) holding the five mechanisms that turn N single-domain RL teachers into one distillation target and one loss weighting. It (a) routes each sample to the teacher matching non_tensor_batch["domain"], (b) instruments per-domain prompt/token/length/reward-magnitude shares under mt_opd/domain/*, (c) computes per-sequence loss weights that force a requested *gradient* share per domain (M1), optionally scaled by per-domain reward magnitude (M2), (d) turns cross-teacher disagreement into either a token mask or a consensus target (M3), and (e) rebuilds the OPD advantage from the current student inside the inner update loop (M4). Every function is pure: tensors and labels in, tensors or flat float metric dicts out; it never touches DataProto, config, or Ray. All state and all DataProto plumbing live in the two callers - ray_trainer.py for routing + M1/M2/M3, dp_actor.py for M4.
report.subsystem: mt_opd_kernels — /data/ycfeng/Open-MOPD/training/verl/verl/workers/actor/mt_opd.py (Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation math kernels: domain routing, per-domain instrumentation, gradient-share rebalancing, teacher-conflict policy, off-policy advantage refresh)
uncertain: I could not diff against a pristine verl 0.7.0.dev tree - the repo has only two commits ('release Open-MOPD open recipe', 'add Open-MOPD arXiv citation') and no upstream remote or vendored reference copy. The upstream/Open-MOPD split above rests on naming signals, the module's absence from verl/workers/actor/__init__.py's __all__, and the MT-OPD-specific docstrings, not on a mechanical diff.

The measured numbers quoted throughout the docstrings (response lengths 11570/9032/364; mean teacher spread 0.131 nats and max 29.2; the divide-direction failure IF loss weight 27 -> 91 and grad token share 57% vs 33%; math weight 0.697 -> 1.326 at alpha=1; per-token |reward| vs length correlation r=-0.87/-0.80) come from run logs not present in this repo. I could not verify any of them against data.

No released config or shell script sets any M1/M2/M3/M4 key. scripts/local/mt_opd.sh only passes teacher_domains, n_additional_teachers, and the mt_reward_model_i overlays; there is no YAML anywhere under training/ containing an mt_opd block (grep over *.yaml/*.yml returns nothing). Which of divide/multiply, anchored/unanchored, mean/q75/q90/top10, none/mask/consensus was actually used for the paper's headline runs is not recoverable from the repo.

I did not execute the test suites (test_mt_opd_domain_metrics.py, test_mt_opd_gradient_share.py, test_mt_opd_m2_m3.py, test_mt_opd_batch_routing.py); the reported behaviour comes from reading the assertions alongside the implementation, plus one direct experiment confirming the torch.quantile size limit on torch 2.5.1.

Whether the torch.quantile size limit is actually hit in practice depends on train_batch_size x rollout.n x mean response length, which no committed config pins down. I established that the limit is real on the installed torch and that the code path passes the whole global batch through it; I did not establish that any historical run crossed 2^24 tokens.

The 'M2 length-dilution fix' comment (mt_opd.py:250-254) and the q75/q90/top10 statistics are implemented and validated inside the kernel, but no test in the repo exercises reward_scale_stat other than the default 'mean' - grep over the three test files shows reward_scale_stat is never passed. Those three branches (mt_opd.py:279-287) are untested.

I did not trace how batch.non_tensor_batch['domain'] is originally produced by the dataset layer - grep for 'domain' in verl/utils/dataset/rl_dataset.py returns nothing, so it appears to flow straight through DataProto.from_single_dict from a parquet column of that name. The on-disk dataset schema requirement is therefore inferred, not read from code.

corrections.claim: mt_opd.conflict_nats is "Also the threshold for the pure-instrumentation contested_frac" (config_keys entry, citing ray_trainer.py:754-756, 2145 and mt_opd.py:521-524, 538).
corrections.why_wrong: The trainer passes conflict_nats ONLY to apply_teacher_conflict_policy (ray_trainer.py:2145). The compute_teacher_conflict_metrics call passes exactly three kwargs — teacher_logprobs, response_mask, domains — and no conflict_nats, so the parameter falls back to its signature default of 1.0 for the entire instrumentation path.
corrections.correct_fact: mt_opd/conflict/contested_frac and mt_opd/conflict/{dom}/contested_frac are hard-pinned at a 1.0-nat threshold and do NOT follow mt_opd.conflict_nats. Setting mt_opd.conflict_nats moves only the policy path (policy_agree_frac / policy_threshold_nats / mask / consensus). The two thresholds silently diverge whenever conflict_nats != 1.0, which is the exact case the docstring at mt_opd.py:521-524 says an operator will want.
corrections.evidence: /data/ycfeng/Open-MOPD/training/verl/verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py:2177-2183 — `metrics.update(compute_teacher_conflict_metrics(teacher_logprobs=teacher_logps, response_mask=response_mask, domains=domains,))`, no conflict_nats kwarg; contrast ray_trainer.py:2145 `conflict_nats=self.mt_conflict_nats,`. Default lives at /data/ycfeng/Open-MOPD/training/verl/verl/workers/actor/mt_opd.py:498 `conflict_nats: float = 1.0` and is consumed at mt_opd.py:538.

corrections.claim: "M4 is a no-op in the default configuration. ... With one minibatch per step and ppo_epochs=1, mt_opd/m4_advantage_refreshed never appears even with opd_refresh_advantage=True."
corrections.why_wrong: The shipped defaults are off-policy, not on-policy. train_batch_size=1024 and ppo_mini_batch_size=256 give 4 minibatches per step (the *=rollout.n / //=dp_size normalisation cancels, leaving train_batch_size/ppo_mini_batch_size), so on_policy is False and the refresh at dp_actor.py:1100 DOES fire.
corrections.correct_fact: M4 is a no-op only for a strictly on-policy configuration, i.e. when a run sets ppo_mini_batch_size equal to the effective train batch (which scripts/local/mt_opd.sh incidentally does via TRAIN_BATCH_SIZE=1 against the 256 default). Under verl's own defaults M4 is active whenever opd_refresh_advantage=True and advantages.dim()==3.

corrections.claim: "MT-OPD is FSDP-only ... so a Megatron actor silently ignores M1/M2/M3's per-sequence weight and M4 entirely while the trainer-side routing and metrics still run."
corrections.why_wrong: The failure is loud, not silent, and it happens before most of the block. compute_distillation_reward is registered only on the FSDP ActorRolloutRefWorker; megatron_workers.py has no such method (grep returns nothing), so ray_trainer.py:2152 `self.actor_rollout_wg.compute_distillation_reward(batch)` raises. That line sits before rm_scores_mean (2156), the share metrics (2170), the anchor (2197) and M1 (2202).
corrections.correct_fact: Under a Megatron actor the mt_opd step hard-fails at ray_trainer.py:2152. Only build_domain_weights / select_routed_teacher_logprobs (2128-2136), the M3 policy plus its metrics (2140-2148) and the teacher-key overwrite (2149) execute first; the share metrics, the M2 anchor and the whole M1 path never run at all.
corrections.evidence: Registration only at /data/ycfeng/Open-MOPD/training/verl/verl/workers/fsdp_workers.py:1091-1093 (`@register(...)` + `def compute_distillation_reward`); implementation at /data/ycfeng/Open-MOPD/training/verl/verl/workers/actor/dp_actor.py:601. `grep -rn compute_distillation_reward` over verl/ hits only mt_opd.py, ray_trainer.py, dp_actor.py, fsdp_workers.py — megatron_workers.py has only compute_rm_score (megatron_workers.py:1268). Call site: ray_trainer.py:2152.

corrections.claim: config key actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_top_k has "default: 0", cited to ray_trainer.py:1968.
corrections.why_wrong: ray_trainer.py:1968 is a local `.get(..., 0)` fallback, not the key's declared default. The declared default is 256 in the RolloutConfig dataclass that fsdp_workers.py:610 builds from config.rollout. Separately, no YAML in the repo declares the key at all (grep for `log_prob_top_k:` over every *.yaml/*.yml returns nothing), so the trainer and the rollout worker can legitimately see different values for the same Hydra path.
corrections.correct_fact: The declared default is `log_prob_top_k: int = 256` (workers/config/rollout.py:154). Because rollout.yaml never declares it, the trainer-side DictConfig lookup at ray_trainer.py:1968 yields 0 unless the user passes `+actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_top_k=K`, while fsdp_workers.py:610's dataclass conversion yields 256. The report presents only half of that split as "the default".
corrections.evidence: /data/ycfeng/Open-MOPD/training/verl/verl/workers/config/rollout.py:154 `log_prob_top_k: int = 256`; /data/ycfeng/Open-MOPD/training/verl/verl/workers/fsdp_workers.py:610 `rollout_config: RolloutConfig = omega_conf_to_dataclass(self.config.rollout)`; `grep -rn "log_prob_top_k:" --include=*.yaml --include=*.yml` over /data/ycfeng/Open-MOPD returns nothing; second `.get(...,0)` fallback at fsdp_workers.py:1022.

corrections.claim: "advantages = advantages * domain_loss_weight.view(-1, 1, 1)" at dp_actor.py:1128-1132 (repeated in outputs as `advantages *= weight.view(-1,1,1)`).
corrections.why_wrong: The literal code uses a rank-generic view and an explicit dtype cast, neither of which the report reproduces. `.view(-1, 1, 1)` would raise on the 2-D advantage path; the real code works there.
corrections.correct_fact: The code is `_dw = model_inputs["domain_loss_weight"].to(advantages.dtype)` then `advantages = advantages * _dw.view(-1, *([1] * (advantages.dim() - 1)))`. Consequence: M1 also applies on the non-topk (2-D advantage) branch, not only inside the dim()==3 branch, and the weight is cast to the advantage dtype (bf16 in practice) before multiplying.

corrections.claim: open_mopd_specific: "domain label plumbed through generation so post-rollout routing is possible."
corrections.why_wrong: The mechanism is the opposite of "plumbed through generation": in sync mode `domain` is deliberately kept OUT of gen_batch and left ON the training batch. The report's own cited regression test asserts exactly that.
corrections.correct_fact: _get_gen_batch keeps `domain` in the reward_model_keys set that is excluded from the non-tensor pop, so it stays on `batch` and is absent from gen_batch in sync mode; it reappears in gen_batch only in async mode via the `gen_batch.non_tensor_batch.update(batch.non_tensor_batch)` at ray_trainer.py:1162. The report's own citation, ray_trainer.py:1059, is also mis-attributed: that line is the rollout-dump key tuple ("request_id","uid","data_source","domain") in _log_rollout_data, unrelated to generation plumbing.
corrections.evidence: /data/ycfeng/Open-MOPD/training/verl/verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py:1145-1163; test assertion /data/ycfeng/Open-MOPD/training/verl/tests/trainer/ppo/test_mt_opd_batch_routing.py:58 `assert "domain" not in gen_batch.non_tensor_batch`; ray_trainer.py:1059 `for key in ("request_id", "uid", "data_source", "domain"):` inside the dump path.

report.purpose: Single-controller Ray driver that owns the whole RL/distillation dataflow: it validates the Open-MOPD `reward_mode` family (`opd_kl` | `delta_opd` | `exopd` | `mt_opd`) plus the `mt_opd.*` knobs in `__init__`, spawns the actor/ref/critic worker groups **and one reward-model worker group per teacher** (`rm` = teacher 0, `teacher_ref_rm`, `mt_rm_1..N`), then runs `fit()`: dataloader batch -> rollout -> student top-k log-probs -> teacher scoring -> per-domain teacher routing -> distillation reward -> rule reward -> DAPO dynamic sampling -> advantage -> actor update -> validation/checkpoint. All light-weight math (advantage, domain routing/weighting, teacher-conflict policy, ~600 metric keys) happens on the driver; every forward pass is an RPC to a worker group. This file is where MT-OPD's per-row `non_tensor_batch["domain"]` becomes a teacher choice and a per-sequence loss weight.

MT-OPD uses token_reward_direct: advantages = token_level_rewards * response_mask.unsqueeze(-1) -> [B,T,K] (core_algos.py:896-899); token_reward_direct_plus_grpo additionally writes token_level_advantage_direct and grpo_outcome_sampled_frac into batch.batch.

~660 lines emitting val-topk/* and val-extrema/* (global + per-1024-token chunk) split by strategy (union / only_tch / only_stu+intersection). Entire block is wrapped in `try/except Exception` that prints a traceback and continues (3290-3293).

Optional is_plot SwanLab scatter/line plots (3295-3474), _dump_data_proto(stage='post_advantage') pickling the whole DataProto (3476), then pops teacher_on_student_log_probs, teacher_top_k_ids, teacher_top_k_log_probs, teacher_entropy, overlap_mask, teacher_in_student_mask, student_log_probs_on_teacher_ids (3479-3490). student_top_k_ids / student_top_k_log_probs / rm_scores / domain_loss_weight are deliberately kept for the actor update.

update_critic (3493-3497). Then, gated by trainer.critic_warmup <= global_steps: sets meta_info['multi_turn'], optionally retunes actor.kl_loss_coef from metrics[actor.adaptive_kl_loss_reward_key] via update_kl_loss_coef_from_reward (3505-3523), sets meta_info['actor_kl_loss_coef'], and calls `self.actor_rollout_wg.update_actor(batch)` (3527). The actor reads domain_loss_weight, advantages, student_top_k_log_probs, old_log_probs, response_mask, format_mask. reduce_metrics(actor_output.meta_info['metrics']) is merged.

should_save_ckpt_esi + trainer.save_freq > 0 and (is_last_step or step % save_freq == 0 or esi_close_to_expiration) -> _save_checkpoint (1512-1558): <default_local_dir>/global_step_<N>/actor, /critic, /data.pt, plus latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt. Teacher/RM worker groups are never checkpointed.
can_validate and trainer.test_freq > 0 and (is_last_step or step % test_freq == 0) -> _validate() merged into metrics under val-core/* and val-aux/*.

profiling stop, training/global_step, training/epoch, compute_data_metrics, compute_timing_metrics, compute_throughout_metrics(n_gpus=resource_pool_manager.get_n_gpus()), logger.log(metrics, step=global_steps) (3600), global_steps += 1 (3603), optional dump_memory_snapshot, return on is_last_step, dataset.on_batch_end hook.

open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Exists to change FSDP world size between MixSFT/RL stages, since the native per-rank checkpoint format cannot load 64-shard weights on 32 ranks (comment 1714-1717).

gotchas: `reward_mode` is NOT declared in verl/trainer/config/rollout/rollout.yaml or in RolloutConfig, yet scripts/local/mt_opd.sh:87 and scripts/local/opd.sh:66 pass it as a plain (non-`+`) Hydra override. I could not execute Hydra in this environment to confirm whether that composes. If it does not, the key silently defaults to 'opd_kl' (ray_trainer.py:88) and the whole MT-OPD path is skipped without any error.

There is NO whitelist on reward_mode. A typo ('mtopd', 'mt-opd', 'MT_OPD') falls through every branch to `elif top_k > 0:` at 2232 and trains as plain opd_kl with a single teacher — no ValueError, no warning. The three extra teacher worker groups are still spawned only if use_mt_opd is True, so a typo also silently disables them.

mt_opd requires non_tensor_batch['domain'] as a TOP-LEVEL parquet column, not extra_info['domain']. `_get_gen_batch` keeps it via the hard-coded keep-set at ray_trainer.py:1150; anything not in that set is popped off the training batch and lost. ValueError at 2110-2114 if absent.

A domain label that is not in mt_opd.teacher_domains does NOT raise. build_domain_weights silently assigns uniform 1/N weights (mt_opd.py:57-61), so a mislabelled row is distilled from the AVERAGE of all three teachers. This is the one place in the MT-OPD path that swallows a data error.

len(mt_opd.teacher_domains) must equal 1 + mt_opd.n_additional_teachers, and the ORDER must match the order of teacher paths (teacher 0 = reward_model.model.path, teacher i = mt_reward_model_{i}.model.path). Nothing cross-checks the model paths against the domain names — a swapped pair routes math prompts to the code teacher silently. The count mismatch does raise (2121-2126).

MT-OPD routing replaces ONLY `teacher_on_student_log_probs` (2149). teacher_top_k_ids, teacher_top_k_log_probs, overlap_mask and teacher_in_student_mask still belong to teacher 0. So any top_k_strategy other than `only_stu` mixes teacher 0's candidate ids with the routed teacher's log-probs. Only only_stu is safe under mt_opd.

`extra_raw.batch['teacher_on_student_log_probs']` at 2106 is a bare dict access — a KeyError, not a ValueError, if an extra teacher returns nothing (e.g. because log_prob_top_k resolved to 0 for that worker). Contrast the teacher_ref branch, which does raise an explicit ValueError at 2020-2023.

`self.mt_reward_scale_stat` is assigned only inside the `if self.use_mt_opd:` branch (718). The else-branch at 766-777 initialises ten sibling attributes but not this one, so `trainer.mt_reward_scale_stat` raises AttributeError on any non-mt_opd trainer. Harmless today because it is read only at 2208 inside the mt_opd branch, but it is a latent asymmetry.

`mt_reward_scale_anchored` captures self._mt_reward_anchor from the FIRST mt_opd batch only, keyed by the domains present in that batch (2197-2201). If a later batch contains a domain that was missing from step 1, compute_domain_loss_weights raises ValueError "reward_anchor missing domains present in batch" (mt_opd.py:245-248) mid-run.

`domain_loss_weight` is computed on the FULL pre-filter generation batch and normalised to token-weighted mean 1 there (mt_opd.py:332-335). DAPO dynamic sampling then trims to train_batch_size (2563/2565) and can concatenate rounds that were each normalised separately, so the mean-1 invariant — the thing that keeps the effective learning rate unchanged — does not hold exactly in the batch that reaches update_actor.

The dynamic-sampling `continue` at 2556 re-enters the dataloader loop, which re-initialises `metrics` and `timing_raw` at 1872-1873. Every metric computed in a discarded generation round (including that round's mt_opd/* domain and conflict metrics) is thrown away and never logged.
`exopd_lambda` is read as `OmegaConf.select(...) or 1.0` (649-651), so an explicit 0.0 becomes 1.0. Same shape of bug in `mt_opd.conflict_nats` (`float(... or 1.0)`, 754-756).

apply_kl_penalty (409-448) assumes 2D token_level_scores and 2D old_log_probs/ref_log_prob. With the dense top-k OPD reward token_level_scores is [B,T,K], so `algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=True` together with log_prob_top_k>0 will broadcast-mismatch at line 437. Nothing validates this combination.

should_reuse_inline_reward returns False whenever use_rm is True (reward.py:110-113), so an OPD/MT-OPD training step ALWAYS goes through the reward manager, which then hands back batch['rm_scores'] unchanged (naive.py:126-131). The rule score is diagnostic only during training; `acc` reaching the metrics comes from reward_extra_info, not from the training reward.

`_validate` returns {} early (1223-1224) when reward_model.enable is True and the first row's reward_model dict declares style=='model'. Combined with `assert val_metrics` at 1739 that turns into an assertion failure before the first training step rather than a readable error.

The Top-K metrics block (2635-3293) and both plot blocks (2241-2327, 3295-3474) are wrapped in bare `except Exception` that only print. A genuine shape bug in the reward tensors can therefore hide behind "Error computing Top-K metrics: ..." while training continues on wrong data.

All mt_rm_{i} groups share Role.RewardModel's resource pool, which main_ppo.py:226-229 maps to 'global_pool' by default. With N=3 teachers that means four full teacher/RM models colocated with the actor and rollout engine on the same GPUs; only reward_model.enable_resource_pool moves them off.

`algorithm.filter_groups.domain_weights` is read via `.get` (1791) but is not a field of FilterGroupsConfig (verl/trainer/config/algorithm.py:43-56), so it needs a `+` override; a plain override would be rejected and a typo silently leaves the {math:1, code:1, if:1} default.

The domain-balanced trim hard-codes the tuple ('math','code','if') at 1820/1863 and domain_weighted_sampler.DOMAIN_ORDER. A fourth domain in teacher_domains would be dropped by _take_complete_groups (2 filters at 1826 and 1866 skip unknown domains) even though routing handles it.

compute_rm_score on the teacher reads batch['old_log_probs'] (fsdp_workers.py:2673), so the student forward at 1961 must run first. That forward sits INSIDE the `if self.use_rm and 'rm_scores' not in batch.batch` guard (1957) — if a future path pre-populates rm_scores, old_log_probs would be missing and the assert at 2445 fires instead of a useful message.

_save_checkpoint persists only actor, critic and the dataloader state. The teacher / teacher_ref / mt_rm worker groups are frozen and never saved, so a resumed run silently depends on the teacher paths in the config still pointing at the same weights.
uncertain: Whether `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.reward_mode=<x>` composes under Hydra as a plain override. The key is absent from verl/trainer/config/rollout/rollout.yaml and from RolloutConfig (verl/workers/config/rollout.py), and both launch scripts pass it without a `+`. No hydra/omegaconf is installed in this environment (`python -c 'import hydra'` -> ModuleNotFoundError) and there is no conda env, so I could not execute the composition to settle it. Same question applies to `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.kl_estimator` (read with .get at 1970, also undeclared) and `algorithm.filter_groups.domain_weights`.

The upstream-vs-Open-MOPD split is inferred from naming signals plus in-file comments that cite this project's own measurements. The repo has only two commits (a8d1f7f, 4809a96) and the vendored verl was committed already patched, so there is no upstream baseline in git to diff against and no network access to fetch verl 0.7.0.dev. Items like the `mask_truncated_samples` / `clip_advantages` / `overlong_filter` parameters of compute_advantage, and the exact boundary of the DAPO port, could not be diffed line-by-line.

Whether `mt_opd.domain_weighting='uniform'` is ever exercised. It bypasses domain routing entirely (averaging all N teachers per token) but nothing in scripts/ or experiments/ sets it, and no test covers it. Its interaction with conflict_policy='consensus' (which also averages) is untested as far as I can see.

`refresh_opd_advantage` (mt_opd.py:338-402, labelled M4) is imported nowhere in ray_trainer.py — the driver imports only the other six symbols (76-83). It is reached from dp_actor.py (the mt_opd/m4_advantage_refreshed metric at dp_actor.py:1108), so it is live, but the config key that enables it is outside this subsystem and I did not trace it.

Whether the `_dyn_enable` path was ever exercised together with reward_mode=mt_opd in a real run. The interaction (domain_loss_weight normalised pre-trim, metrics discarded on `continue`) is a code-reading conclusion; I found no log or test that covers the combination.

`compute_advantage`'s `num_repeat` parameter is accepted (474) and passed from fit (2625) but is never used in the body. Looks like dead plumbing rather than a bug, but I did not confirm against upstream.

call_chain.step: Hydra config selects the estimator by string
call_chain.detail: `AlgoConfig.adv_estimator: str = "gae"`. Open-MOPD scripts override it: `algorithm.adv_estimator=token_reward_direct` (scripts/local/mt_opd.sh:77) or `${ADV_ESTIMATOR:-token_reward_direct}` (scripts/local/opd.sh:42,56).

call_chain.step: fit() loop calls compute_advantage on the driver
call_chain.detail: Passes adv_estimator=self.config.algorithm.adv_estimator (a plain str), gamma, lam, num_repeat=rollout.n, norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo, mask_truncated_samples, clip_advantages, config=self.config.algorithm, overlong_filter.

call_chain.step: compute_advantage dispatches: GAE and GRPO are hard-coded, everything else goes through the registry
call_chain.detail: `if adv_estimator == AdvantageEstimator.GAE ... elif == AdvantageEstimator.GRPO ... else: adv_estimator_fn = core_algos.get_adv_estimator_fn(adv_estimator)`. Because AdvantageEstimator subclasses `str`, the `==` on a raw string works; "token_reward_direct" matches no enum member and therefore lands in the registry `else` branch.

`get_adv_estimator_fn` reads ADV_ESTIMATOR_REGISTRY (populated by the `@register_adv_est(name)` decorator at lines 113-131). OPD estimators are registered by *string* only — they are NOT added to the AdvantageEstimator enum (lines 88-107).

Always: token_level_rewards, response_mask, config. Conditionally: index=non_tensor_batch['uid'], true_reward_score, reward_baselines, student_top_k_ids, responses (all from data.batch). The last three `if ... in data.batch` blocks for true_reward_score / student_top_k_ids / responses are Open-MOPD additions.

`res = adv_estimator_fn(**adv_kwargs)`; `len(res)==3` unpacks `(advantages, returns, extra_metrics)` and writes every extra key straight into `data.batch[k]`. This 3-tuple path exists only for token_reward_direct_plus_grpo.
Under torch.no_grad: if rewards are 3D, mask is unsqueezed to (bs, L, 1); advantages = token_level_rewards * response_mask; returns = advantages.clone().

direct_adv from token_reward_direct; grpo_adv from compute_grpo_outcome_advantage on `true_reward_score` (falls back to token_level_rewards); combined = direct + config.grpo_outcome_weight * grpo_adv; returns extra dict.

call_chain.step: 3D dense top-k path scatters the outcome scalar onto the sampled candidate
call_chain.detail: _scatter_outcome_adv_onto_sampled_topk builds sampled_mask = (student_top_k_ids == responses.unsqueeze(-1)) and torch.where(sampled_mask, grpo_adv.unsqueeze(-1), 0). Also returns per-sequence coverage `sampled_frac`.
`if clip_advantages: data.batch['advantages'] = torch.clamp(..., -1, 1)` — applies to the 3D dense OPD advantage too.

3D advantages get critic/advantages/mean_sum_over_k and mean_overall; the extra key token_level_advantage_direct produces critic/advantages/direct_{mean,max,min} and per-1k-position variants (lines 223-253).

call_chain.step: Actor consumes the advantage; 3D triggers a top-k forward
call_chain.detail: `if advantages.dim() == 3: top_k = advantages.shape[-1]`, forward with student_top_k_ids/union_top_k_ids, log_prob_for_loss = topk_log_probs. Off-policy + opd_refresh_advantage rebuilds the advantage via refresh_opd_advantage (mt_opd.py:338-402).

call_chain.step: MT-OPD domain weighting multiplies the advantage
call_chain.detail: `advantages = advantages * domain_loss_weight.view(-1, 1[,1])`. Applied to the advantage rather than response_mask so ppo_kl/pg_clipfrac stay unweighted.

loss_mode = config.policy_loss.get('loss_mode', 'vanilla'); get_policy_loss_fn(loss_mode); called with old_log_prob, log_prob=log_prob_for_loss (3D for top-k), advantages, response_mask, loss_agg_mode, config, rollout_is_weights, format_mask.

Dual-clip PPO computed elementwise on (bs, L, K), then `pg_losses = torch.sum(pg_losses, dim=-1)` (line 1240, comment `[MOD] for wings`). pg_clipfrac_lower is a hard-coded 0.0 placeholder in this branch (line 1251).

call_chain.step: Loss aggregation, optionally masked by format_mask
call_chain.detail: `if format_mask is not None: agg_loss(loss_mask=response_mask * format_mask.unsqueeze(-1))` else plain response_mask.

config_keys.effect: Selects the advantage estimator. Any value other than "gae"/"grpo" is resolved by string through ADV_ESTIMATOR_REGISTRY. Valid OPD values: token_reward_direct, token_reward_direct_plus_grpo (token_grpo is registered but broken — see gotchas).

Scalar multiplier on the GRPO outcome advantage inside token_reward_direct_plus_grpo: adv = direct + weight * grpo. Read as an attribute (`config.grpo_outcome_weight`), so it must exist on the config object. Open-MOPD addition (absent from upstream 0.6.0/0.7.0 AlgoConfig).

Inside the hybrid estimator, controls whether the outcome term is (R-mean)/std (GRPO) or R-mean (Dr.GRPO). Read from `config.norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo`, NOT from the `norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo` argument that compute_advantage was given.

Excludes zero-reward full-length (truncated) samples from GRPO group statistics and pins their advantage to 0. Reaches compute_grpo_outcome_advantage only via the hard-coded GRPO branch (ray_trainer.py:533); it is NOT forwarded through the registry path, so it is inert for token_reward_direct_plus_grpo.
DAPO Overlong Filtering: drops every full-length sample from group stats regardless of reward. Same forwarding limitation as mask_truncated_samples — inert for the hybrid OPD estimator.
Clamps the final advantages tensor to [-1, 1] after the estimator returns, including 3D dense OPD advantages.

When True, apply_kl_penalty sets token_level_rewards = token_level_scores - beta * kl(old_log_probs, ref_log_prob). beta comes from the KL controller. Incompatible with 3D dense OPD rewards (shape broadcast failure) — see gotchas.
Estimator string passed to core_algos.kl_penalty: kl/k1, abs, mse/k2, low_var_kl/k3, or any of those with a trailing '+' for the straight-through k2-gradient trick. Byte-identical to upstream.
get_kl_controller returns FixedKLController(kl_coef) or AdaptiveKLController(kl_coef, target_kl, horizon). Only used for the in-reward KL penalty (self.kl_ctrl_in_reward). Upstream, unmodified.

Selects the policy loss from POLICY_LOSS_REGISTRY. OPD runs stay on "vanilla", which is the only registered loss with the 3D top-k branch and the only one that accepts format_mask. No OPD-specific loss is registered.

config_keys.default: (see actor config) / used as kl_penalty type / float
config_keys.effect: Adds kl_loss = agg_loss(kl_penalty(log_prob, ref_log_prob, kl_loss_type)) * effective_coef to the policy loss. NOTE the KL loss uses the 2D `log_prob`, never the 3D `log_prob_for_loss`, so it is a token-level anchor to the reference model and is independent of the top-k distillation term.

Open-MOPD reward-driven KL-loss controller: each step, kl_loss_coef is multiplied by (1-eps) when the tracked reward mean is negative and (1+eps) when positive, clamped to [min,max], then shipped to the actor as meta_info['actor_kl_loss_coef'].

MT-OPD M4. When off-policy, rebuilds the 3D advantage from the current student's top-k log-probs inside update_policy via refresh_opd_advantage, bypassing whatever token_reward_direct produced on the driver.

Decide whether token_level_rewards is 3D and its K: only_stu/only_tch/intersection give K=log_prob_top_k, union / union-intersection give 2K. reward_weight_mode picks the softmax weight w over the K candidates in the OPD reward.

Chooses which dense reward fills rm_scores -> token_level_rewards: opd_kl (compute_distillation_reward), delta_opd, exopd, mt_opd. All produce a 3D tensor, so all reach the 3D paths of the OPD estimators.

entrypoints.what_it_does: Decorator; writes fn into module-global ADV_ESTIMATOR_REGISTRY[name]. Raises ValueError on a duplicate name bound to a different function. Accepts a bare string, which is how both OPD estimators register without touching the AdvantageEstimator enum.
Registry lookup; raises `ValueError(f"Unknown advantage estimator simply: {name}")` when absent. Sole consumer is compute_advantage's else-branch.

gotchas: `token_grpo` (core_algos.py:352-450) is effectively dead code. Its signature has no `**kwargs`, but compute_advantage always passes `true_reward_score` (ray_trainer.py:2487 sets it unconditionally, 548-549 forwards it) and `responses` (557-558), so selecting `algorithm.adv_estimator=token_grpo` raises `TypeError: compute_grpo_process_advantage() got an unexpected keyword argument 'true_reward_score'`. Nothing else in the repo references it. The same forwarding change also breaks upstream `grpo_vectorized` (core_algos.py:454-461, also no **kwargs).

`algorithm.mask_truncated_samples` and `algorithm.overlong_filter` are silently ignored under the OPD estimators. compute_advantage forwards them only inside the hard-coded `adv_estimator == GRPO` branch (ray_trainer.py:533-534); the registry path (541-558) does not include them, and token_reward_direct_plus_grpo calls compute_grpo_outcome_advantage without them (core_algos.py:933-937).

Likewise `compute_advantage(norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo=...)` is dead for the hybrid estimator: the value used is `config.norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo` read off AlgoConfig inside the estimator (core_algos.py:932). The two happen to agree at the call site (ray_trainer.py:2617-2625) but an in-code override of the argument would have no effect.

token_reward_direct_plus_grpo with 3D rewards requires a 2D `true_reward_score` in data.batch. If it were absent, `rewards_for_grpo` would be the 3D tensor and compute_grpo_outcome_advantage's final `scores.unsqueeze(-1) * response_mask` would be a (bs,L,1)*(bs,L) broadcast failure, plus `response_length = token_level_rewards.shape[-1]` would read K instead of L (core_algos.py:306,348). In practice ray_trainer.py:2476-2487 always populates true_reward_score, and naive.py:280 makes it the 2D rule-based verifier reward — the invariant holds but is not asserted anywhere.

Hybrid estimator + union / union-intersection top-k strategy is unsupported and fails loudly: direct_adv has K'=2K (dp_actor.py:735-742 concatenates student and teacher ids) while compute_advantage only forwards `student_top_k_ids` (ray_trainer.py:555-556, K columns), so _scatter_outcome_adv_onto_sampled_topk raises `student_top_k_ids has K=... but advantages have K=...` (core_algos.py:999-1003).

`grpo_outcome_sampled_frac` measures real coverage loss, not a diagnostic nicety. A sampled token whose id is not in the student's top-k receives *no* outcome advantage (core_algos.py:1009-1013). The top-k set comes from a separate forward pass than the vLLM sample, so a miss is expected with small log_prob_top_k, and the outcome term is then applied to a biased subset of positions.

`algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=True` is incompatible with dense OPD rewards. apply_kl_penalty computes `token_level_scores - beta * kld` with kld of shape (bs, L) (ray_trainer.py:430-438) while token_level_scores is the 3D rm_scores, giving a broadcast error unless K == L. Default is False, so this only bites if someone enables it.

The 3D branch of compute_policy_loss_vanilla reports `pg_clipfrac_lower` as a hard-coded 0.0 (core_algos.py:1251) and `ppo_kl` as the K-summed KL (line 1245), so those two metrics are not comparable with 2D runs. It also `print(f"Advantages shape: ...")` on every micro-batch (line 1215).

The docstring/comment block above the 3D branch (core_algos.py:1206-1213) describes a memory-efficient `L = -sum_x A(x) log pi(x)` formulation, but the code actually below it builds the full 3D ratio and does dual-clip PPO (1219-1240). The comment does not describe the implementation.

token_reward_direct_plus_grpo's type annotation says `-> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]` while it always returns a 3-tuple (core_algos.py:912, 967). The trainer copes via the `len(res) == 3` branch (ray_trainer.py:564-567), but any other caller typed against the annotation would break.

`returns` is never a real return for either OPD estimator — it is a clone of `advantages` (core_algos.py:900, 965). Enabling a critic (GAE) with these estimators would train the value head against the advantage, not a discounted return. utils.py:89-93 disables the critic whenever adv_estimator != gae, which keeps this from firing.

The advantage the actor optimizes is not always the advantage the driver computed and logged. dp_actor.py:1095-1107 can overwrite it entirely (MT-OPD M4 refresh, off-policy only) and 1128-1132 rescales it per domain, both after metric_utils has already recorded critic/advantages/*.

compute_advantage writes every key of the `extra` dict into data.batch with no name validation (ray_trainer.py:565-567), so an estimator can silently shadow an existing batch key. Currently only `token_level_advantage_direct` and `grpo_outcome_sampled_frac` are produced.

report.purpose: This subsystem is the advantage-estimation layer of the vendored verl PPO stack plus the two Open-MOPD estimators that turn a dense per-token teacher reward into an advantage. `token_reward_direct` is the pure on-policy-distillation estimator: it passes the teacher-vs-student KL reward through as the advantage with no baseline, no group normalization and no whitening, and it is the estimator both OPD launch scripts select. `token_reward_direct_plus_grpo` is the hybrid: it adds a group-normalized verifiable outcome advantage on top of the dense distillation advantage, and in the dense top-k case it places that scalar outcome term on the single top-k slot the rollout actually sampled instead of broadcasting it over all K candidates. Selection happens purely by string through `register_adv_est` / `ADV_ESTIMATOR_REGISTRY` — neither estimator is added to the `AdvantageEstimator` enum.
report.subsystem: core_algos_adv — advantage estimators (Open-MOPD token_reward_direct family), the register_adv_est registry, and the policy-loss / KL helpers OPD depends on
uncertain: Provenance of `compute_policy_loss_with_rollout_correction` + `register_policy_loss("rollout_correction")` (core_algos.py:1872-2083). The vendored tree says version 0.7.0.dev, and I could only obtain the released 0.6.0 and 0.7.0 wheels, not the exact fork-point snapshot. Upstream 0.7.0 has the same capability under different names (compute_policy_loss_reinforce, register_policy_loss('bypass_mode')) and also ships rollout_corr_helper.py, so this is most likely fork-point upstream code rather than an Open-MOPD addition — but I cannot prove it from the artifacts available offline.

Same caveat for the `agg_loss` signature difference (vendored takes 3 args; upstream 0.7.0 takes 7 with dp_size/global_batch_info). That reads as upstream drift after the fork rather than an Open-MOPD edit, since it is a mechanical parallelism-invariance refactor with no OPD-related naming.

Whether `token_grpo` was ever functional. It is coherent code with a clear formula, but there is no config, script, test, or doc referencing it anywhere in the repo, and via compute_advantage it now TypeErrors. I cannot tell whether it predates the true_reward_score/responses kwargs additions or was written and never run.

Whether `grpo_outcome_sampled_frac` is meant to be logged. It is written into data.batch but grep finds no metrics code reading it; the docstring says only that carrying it "keeps it inspectable in the saved DataProto". Cannot tell from source whether a logging step is missing or intentionally omitted.

The exact real-run value of `algorithm.grpo_outcome_weight` for published Open-MOPD hybrid runs. Neither scripts/local/*.sh nor experiments/ set it, and no experiment config in the repo selects token_reward_direct_plus_grpo at all — so the hybrid estimator has no launcher in the released recipe, only the unit test.

Output dict: teacher_on_student_log_probs, teacher_top_k_ids, teacher_top_k_log_probs, teacher_entropy, teacher_valid_counts, overlap_mask, teacher_in_student_mask (+ rm_scores only on the top_k==0 path).

call_chain.detail: if reward_mode in ('delta_opd','exopd'): teacher-ref scorer path (:1993-2099). elif reward_mode=='mt_opd': extra-teacher routing then standard OPD (:2100-2230). elif top_k > 0: plain opd_kl -> compute_distillation_reward (:2232-2238). opd_kl with top_k==0 hits no branch and keeps the scalar rm_scores from the RM worker.

call_chain.step: opd_kl: teacher forward becomes a dense per-token reward
call_chain.detail: For strategy only_stu: kl_val = S_logp - T_on_S; valid_mask all-ones; norm_weights = softmax over K of S_logp (reward_weight_mode student_p) / T_on_S (teacher_p) / uniform (none) (:672-706); rm_scores = -kl_val * norm_weights, shape [B,T,K] (:711-714). Returned as DataProto {rm_scores, plus union_* keys for union strategies} (:773-774).

call_chain.step: mt_opd: score every extra teacher, route by domain, then reuse the opd_kl reward
call_chain.detail: Each mt_rm_{i}.compute_rm_score -> mt_teacher_{i}_on_student_log_probs (:2102-2107). domain labels required (:2109-2114). build_domain_weights one-hot [B,N] (mt_opd.py:24-62), select_routed_teacher_logprobs weighted sum over teachers (mt_opd.py:65-87), apply_teacher_conflict_policy (mt_opd.py:405-491), then batch['teacher_on_student_log_probs'] is OVERWRITTEN with the routed tensor (:2149) and compute_distillation_reward runs unchanged (:2151-2153).

call_chain.detail: compute_domain_loss_weights returns [B] weights = target_share/observed_token_share (optionally times/over per-domain |reward| magnitude), token-weighted-mean-normalised to 1; written to batch['domain_loss_weight'] (:2224) and applied to advantages in dp_actor.py:1128-1132.

Then compute_exopd_reward (:2039) or compute_delta_opd_reward (:2055). _compute_delta_opd_rm_scores: delta = T_rl - T_ref, rm_scores = softmax(detached S_logp) * delta (dp_actor.py:109-148). _compute_exopd_rm_scores: opd + (lambda-1)*delta, exact identity at lambda==1 (dp_actor.py:151-191).

Divides the teacher logits before log_softmax/top-k, in place, on both the rmpad and dense paths.
Extrapolation strength for reward_mode=exopd: rm = opd + (lambda-1)*delta. Exactly identity (early return) at 1.0; must be finite and >= 0.
