The teacher forward pass. Runs the teacher LM over the student's own input_ids and returns per-candidate teacher log-probs plus overlap bookkeeping. Returns rm_scores ONLY when top_k == 0 (scalar reverse KL); with top_k > 0 it deliberately returns no rm_scores. The kl_estimator argument is never used in the body.

entrypoints.signature: _forward_micro_batch(self, micro_batch, student_top_k_ids=None, compute_entropy=False, top_k=0, strategy="only_stu", teacher_temperature=1.0, top_p_intersec_p=0.99) -> tuple[8 tensors]
entrypoints.what_it_does: Returns (rm_log_probs[B,T], teacher_on_student_log_probs[B,T,K], teacher_top_k_ids[B,T,K], teacher_top_k_log_probs[B,T,K], teacher_entropy[B,T], teacher_valid_counts[B,T], teacher_overlap_mask[B,T,K], teacher_in_student_mask[B,T,K]). Handles remove-padding + Ulysses re-slicing of the externally supplied student ids.

entrypoints.signature: _compute_teacher_top_k_log_probs(self, logits, student_ids, top_k, strategy="only_stu", chunk_size=1024, top_p_intersec_p=0.99) -> tuple[6 tensors]
entrypoints.what_it_does: This is where top_k actually does its work. Per 1024-token chunk: teacher's own topk ids/log-probs, teacher log-probs at the student's ids (gather - logsumexp), and the K_s x K_t match matrix from which overlap_mask (student-in-teacher) and teacher_in_student are reduced. For intersection strategy it instead max-reduces the teacher's top-k values onto matching student slots, leaving -inf where there is no match.
Nucleus variant of the overlap mask: marks which student top-k ids fall in the teacher's top-p set. Always keeps the argmax.

Ray-dispatched wrapper (mesh_name="actor"). Injects micro_batch_size / max_token_len / use_dynamic_bsz / temperature from rollout config, then delegates to DataParallelPPOActor.compute_distillation_reward.

Turns the teacher log-probs into the dense reward. For only_tch/intersection/union/union-intersection it first runs a second student forward on teacher_top_k_ids to get S_on_T. Then per strategy: rm_scores = -(S - T) * normalized_weights, shape [B,T,K] (or [B,T,2K] for union).
Returns {rm_scores, delta_log_ratio}: student-prob-weighted (T_rl - T_ref) gap. No model forward -- pure tensor algebra on three cached log-prob tensors.
Returns {rm_scores, delta_log_ratio, exopd_delta_rm_scores}. Requires opd_rm_scores already in the batch, else ValueError.
delta = T_rl.detach() - T_ref.detach() (0 outside valid_mask); rm_scores = softmax(masked detached student_logp) * delta. Enforces identical [B,T,K] shapes.
opd + (lambda - 1) * delta, with an explicit early return at lambda == 1.0 so opd_kl is bit-reproducible.

entrypoints.signature: _forward_micro_batch(self, micro_batch, temperature, calculate_entropy=False, top_k=0, student_top_k_ids=None) -> (entropy, log_probs, topk_ids, topk_log_probs)
entrypoints.what_it_does: Single student forward. With top_k > 0 it computes log_softmax once and gathers both the sampled-token log-probs and the K candidate log-probs. If student_top_k_ids is supplied it gathers at those ids instead of running torch.topk (this is how S_on_T is produced).

entrypoints.signature: build_domain_weights(domains, domain_order, device, weighting="domain_routing") -> Tensor[B,N]; select_routed_teacher_logprobs(teacher_logprobs: list[Tensor[B,T,K]], domain_weights) -> Tensor[B,T,K]
entrypoints.what_it_does: Per-sample one-hot (or uniform) teacher weights, then a weighted sum over the stacked teacher log-prob tensors. Domains absent from domain_order silently fall back to uniform.

entrypoints.signature: apply_teacher_conflict_policy(routed_logprobs, teacher_logprobs, response_mask, policy="none", conflict_nats=1.0, conflict_quantile=None) -> (target_logprobs, token_weight|None, metrics)
entrypoints.what_it_does: Measures cross-teacher spread on the top-1 candidate; mask zeroes (and renormalises) contested tokens' loss weight, consensus swaps in the teacher mean on agreeing tokens.

entrypoints.signature: compute_domain_loss_weights(domains, response_mask, target_shares=None, rm_scores=None, normalize_reward_scale=False, reward_scale_stat="mean", reward_scale_direction="divide", reward_anchor=None) -> Tensor[B]|None
entrypoints.what_it_does: Per-sequence loss weights hitting a target per-domain gradient share, token-weighted-mean normalised to 1. Returns None (leave the loss alone) when target_shares is None.
Rebuilds the only_stu OPD reward from the current student inside the inner update loop. Only valid for only_stu.
Registered as adv_est "token_reward_direct". Multiplies the reward by the response mask (unsqueezing the mask to [B,T,1] for 3D dense rewards) and returns it as both advantage and return.

Unit test pinning _pop_direct_opd_rollout_options behaviour (:133-138) and the delta-OPD metric math.

gotchas: reward_mode is declared NOWHERE in the config schema. It is absent from RolloutConfig (/data/ycfeng/Open-MOPD/training/verl/verl/workers/config/rollout.py:98-213) and from trainer/config/rollout/rollout.yaml (326 lines, grep for reward_mode returns nothing), yet scripts/local/opd.sh:66 and scripts/local/mt_opd.sh:87 pass it as a plain override without Hydra's '+' prefix -- while every other Open-MOPD-only key in the very same arrays does use '+' (mt_opd.sh:92-93, :105-112). Under normal Hydra semantics a plain override of an undeclared key is an error. I could not execute Hydra here to confirm (no hydra module in the reachable interpreter), so this is flagged as a strong static discrepancy rather than a confirmed crash. The Python side tolerates absence: rollout.get("reward_mode", "opd_kl") at ray_trainer.py:88.

_pop_direct_opd_rollout_options MUTATES the config: it deletes rollout.reward_mode under open_dict (ray_trainer.py:89-91). That delete is required -- RolloutConfig would reject the unknown field when config.actor_rollout_ref is handed to the worker at :1388 -- but it also means (a) nothing downstream can read rollout.reward_mode, only self.reward_mode, and (b) a second call returns the "opd_kl" default silently.

reward_mode is never validated against a set of legal values. Only three equality tests exist (:643, :644, :648). A typo such as 'delta-opd' or 'mt-opd' falls through to the `elif top_k > 0` branch at :2232 and trains plain opd_kl with no warning. There is no registry/enum for these modes despite four of them.

batch.meta_info["reward_mode"] is written at ray_trainer.py:1986 and read by nothing in the tree (verified by grep for both meta_info["reward_mode"] and meta_info.get("reward_mode")). Informational only; the actor decides what to do purely from which RPC the trainer calls.

kl_estimator is dead. ray_trainer.py:1970 reads actor_rollout_ref.rollout.kl_estimator (a key that does not exist in RolloutConfig or rollout.yaml, so it is always "k1"), forwards it at :1983, and dp_actor.py:614 assigns it to a local that is never used in compute_distillation_reward. RewardModelWorker.compute_rm_score also takes a kl_estimator parameter (fsdp_workers.py:2664) that its body ignores.

top_k_strategy=top_p_intersec has NO branch in DataParallelPPOActor.compute_distillation_reward. The strategy chain at dp_actor.py:710-771 covers only only_stu / only_tch / intersection / union / union-intersection, so rm_scores stays unbound and line 773 (res_tensors["rm_scores"] = rm_scores) raises UnboundLocalError. It is reachable with reward_mode=opd_kl or mt_opd (which both call compute_distillation_reward) and with reward_mode=exopd (ray_trainer.py:2007). Only reward_mode=delta_opd handles it, at dp_actor.py:785. The unit test that exercises top_p_intersec pairs it with delta_opd (tests/test_delta_opd_reward.py:124-125).

The top_k > 0 guard is asymmetric. ray_trainer.py:1973-1974 raises only for delta_opd and mt_opd. reward_mode=exopd with log_prob_top_k=0 passes the guard, then compute_distillation_reward hits KeyError on data.batch["student_top_k_ids"] (dp_actor.py:661) because compute_log_prob only emits that key when top_k > 0 (fsdp_workers.py:1031-1034). reward_mode=opd_kl with top_k=0 silently degrades to the scalar reverse-KL reward computed inside the RM worker (fsdp_workers.py:2831-2834), a [B,T] tensor instead of [B,T,K].

MT-OPD M4 (actor.opd_refresh_advantage) appears unreachable through RayPPOTrainer.fit. dp_actor.py:985 and :1098 both require teacher_on_student_log_probs to be present in the DataProto handed to update_policy, but ray_trainer.py:3478-3490 pops exactly that key (along with teacher_top_k_*, teacher_entropy, overlap_mask, teacher_in_student_mask) unconditionally, and update_actor is only invoked afterwards at :3502. No other code path re-adds the key. Either the pop needs to be conditional on the flag, or M4 is dead.

reward_mode is meaningless without reward_model.enable=True. use_rm is derived from Role.RewardModel membership (ray_trainer.py:640 -> trainer/ppo/utils.py:78-81), and main_ppo.py:206 only registers that role when reward_model.enable. delta_opd/exopd/mt_opd raise a clear error in that case (:653-658), but opd_kl silently skips the entire teacher block at :1957 and trains on whatever the rule reward manager returns.

Megatron cannot run any OPD reward_mode. verl/workers/megatron_workers.py:1105-1275 is the untouched upstream scalar-value RM: compute_rm_score just calls MegatronRewardModel.compute_reward and returns to CPU (:1268-1275). No top_k, no student_top_k_ids, no teacher_on_student_log_probs anywhere in the file (grep confirms zero hits). Setting reward_model.strategy=megatron therefore yields a batch with no teacher_on_student_log_probs and the mode branches fail.

trainer.use_legacy_worker_impl=disable is broken for reward models: main_ppo.py:216 imports RewardModelWorker from verl.workers.roles, and that package contains only actor.py, critic.py, hybrid_engine.py, utils/ -- no reward_model module.

The FSDP RewardModelWorker docstring still claims "subclass of AutoModelForTokenClassification" (fsdp_workers.py:1737) but _build_model loads AutoModelForCausalLM (:1837-1843). The Open-MOPD teacher is a full LM whose logits are the reward source, not a scalar head.

Student and teacher temperatures are independent and unchecked. The student's log-probs are computed at rollout.temperature (fsdp_workers.py:1021) while the teacher's logits are divided by rollout.teacher_temperature (fsdp_workers.py:2122, :2357). A mismatch silently changes the KL that the reward measures; nothing validates the pair.

mt_opd requires non_tensor_batch["domain"] on every training row (ray_trainer.py:2109-2114 raises otherwise). "domain" is one of the non-tensor keys explicitly retained across the generation pop (:1149-1150). Teacher count must equal len(mt_opd.teacher_domains) or :2121-2126 raises.

mt_opd OVERWRITES batch["teacher_on_student_log_probs"] in place with the routed tensor (ray_trainer.py:2149) so that the unmodified opd_kl reward kernel can be reused. Teacher 0 (rm_wg) is implicitly domain index 0; the extra teachers are indexed 1..N by the mt_reward_model_{i} key number.

exopd cannot union its two rewards under one name: DataProto.union asserts equality on duplicate keys, so the standard OPD reward is stashed as opd_rm_scores (ray_trainer.py:2013-2017) and compute_exopd_reward raises a named ValueError if it is missing (dp_actor.py:809-813).

The teacher's overlap tensor is renamed on the way out: internally teacher_overlap_mask, exported as "overlap_mask" (fsdp_workers.py:2857-2858). Consumers key on "overlap_mask" (dp_actor.py:669, :786, :819; ray_trainer.py:2635).

The teacher reward reaches the loss only because NaiveRewardManager passes rm_scores through (naive.py:126-131 / :275-287). should_reuse_inline_reward deliberately returns False for training when use_rm (reward.py:110-112), so the manager is always invoked; if a recipe swaps in a manager without that passthrough (e.g. mixed.py:48-53), the dense OPD reward would be discarded.

open_mopd_specific.what: reward_mode itself: the option dict, the pop-and-delete, the four mode flags and their validation
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Names opd_kl / delta_opd / mt_opd / exopd, references config.teacher_ref_reward_model and mt_opd.*, and exists solely to smuggle a key past the upstream RolloutConfig dataclass. No upstream verl concept.

open_mopd_specific.what: The entire four-way reward dispatch inside fit(), including the extra teacher RPCs and every delta_opd / exopd / mt_opd metric
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Upstream verl's reward step is a single rm_wg.compute_rm_score followed by the reward manager. Here the block orchestrates a student top-k forward, 1..N teacher forwards, an optional reference-teacher forward, and three distinct reward kernels.

open_mopd_specific.what: teacher_ref_rm and mt_rm_{i} worker-group registration by config-key merge
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Uses OmegaConf.merge(config.reward_model, config.teacher_ref_reward_model) and config.mt_reward_model_{i}; both key names are Open-MOPD signals, and spawning multiple RM groups under one resource pool has no upstream counterpart.

open_mopd_specific.what: RewardModelWorker rewritten from a scalar value model into a teacher log-prob server
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Loads AutoModelForCausalLM while the class docstring still says AutoModelForTokenClassification (:1737); returns teacher_on_student_log_probs / teacher_top_k_* / teacher_entropy / overlap_mask / teacher_in_student_mask; and returns rm_scores=None when top_k>0 (:2825-2829) -- an upstream RM always returns a score.

open_mopd_specific.what: Dense top-k distillation reward kernels on the actor
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Upstream DataParallelPPOActor has no reward-producing method at all. rm_scores here is [B,T,K] rather than [B,T].

open_mopd_specific.what: top_k plumbing through the student forward, including remove-padding/Ulysses re-alignment of externally supplied candidate ids
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: compute_log_prob's 4-tuple return (entropy, log_probs, topk_ids, topk_log_probs) and the student_top_k_ids argument are additions; upstream returns log_probs (+ entropy).

open_mopd_specific.what: verl/workers/actor/mt_opd.py in full
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Module docstring names MT-OPD; every symbol (build_domain_weights, select_routed_teacher_logprobs, compute_domain_loss_weights, apply_teacher_conflict_policy, refresh_opd_advantage, compute_domain_share_metrics, compute_teacher_conflict_metrics) is exclusive to this recipe and emits mt_opd/* metrics.

open_mopd_specific.what: OPD knobs added to the RolloutConfig dataclass
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: log_prob_top_k, top_k_strategy, top_p_intersec_p, reward_weight_mode, teacher_temperature, exopd_lambda -- the exopd_lambda comment explicitly says "for reward_mode=exopd". They are in the dataclass but absent from rollout.yaml, so they are dataclass-only additions.

open_mopd_specific.what: opd_refresh_advantage / opd_reward_weight_mode on ActorConfig, and the adaptive-KL default keyed to a delta_opd metric
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: adaptive_kl_loss_reward_key defaults to "delta_opd/weighted_reward_mean", a metric produced only by ray_trainer.py:196-234.

open_mopd_specific.what: token_reward_direct and token_reward_direct_plus_grpo advantage estimators
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Both are 3D-reward aware, and _scatter_outcome_adv_onto_sampled_topk exists purely to reconcile a per-sequence outcome advantage with the dense top-k axis. Chinese-language docstring at :884 also marks it as fork code.

open_mopd_specific.what: rm_scores passthrough with the rule reward demoted to a diagnostic true_reward_score
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: The comment states outright that OPD's learning signal is the dense teacher-KL rm_scores and rule scoring is diagnostic only. compute_true_reward is a fork-added constructor flag.

open_mopd_specific.what: should_reuse_inline_reward gating that reserves training rm_scores for the teacher
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Docstring explicitly says "OPD must reserve its training rm_scores for teacher distillation"; agent_loop.py:392 comments on reward_model.enable=True being OPD's teacher KL reward.

open_mopd_specific.what: OPD validation reward dispatcher
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Header names reward_mode=opd_kl/mt_opd and explains that training reward never routes through it -- written to fix math-only scoring of mixed MT-OPD validation sets.

report.purpose: rollout reward_mode is the single switch that selects which flavour of on-policy-distillation reward Open-MOPD computes for a training batch: opd_kl (student-teacher reverse KL over dense top-k candidates), delta_opd (the RL-teacher vs pre-RL-teacher log-prob gap), exopd (a lambda-weighted combination of those two), or mt_opd (per-domain routing across N RL teachers, then the opd_kl kernel). It is read exactly once, in RayPPOTrainer.__init__, and immediately deleted from the rollout config node; from there it lives only as trainer boolean flags that pick which worker RPCs the fit loop issues. The actual reward tensor is produced in two halves: the FSDP RewardModelWorker turns a frozen teacher's logits into per-candidate log-probs at the student's own top-k token ids, and the actor worker turns those log-probs plus the student's log-probs into a dense [B, T, K] rm_scores tensor that the naive reward manager passes through verbatim to become the advantage under adv_estimator=token_reward_direct.
report.subsystem: rollout_reward_mode (reward_mode plumbing, teacher log-prob computation, and dense top-k KL reward construction)

Someone with the training env should run `python -m verl.trainer.main_ppo actor_rollout_ref.rollout.reward_mode=opd_kl --cfg job` to settle it.

call_chain.step: CLI launch: build Hydra overrides for N teachers
call_chain.detail: Emits `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.reward_mode=mt_opd`, `reward_model.enable=True`, `reward_model.model.path=<teacher_0>`, `+mt_opd.teacher_domains=[math,code,if]`, `+mt_opd.n_additional_teachers=<count-1>`, and for i=1..N-1 a `+mt_reward_model_{i}.{enable,model.path,model.input_tokenizer,model.use_remove_padding,model.fsdp_config.param_offload}` block. Shell-side check at :58-60 forces len(domains)==len(teacher paths).

call_chain.step: Register RewardModelWorker class + resource pool for Role.RewardModel
call_chain.detail: `config.reward_model.enable=True` -> imports `verl.workers.fsdp_workers.RewardModelWorker` for strategy fsdp/fsdp2 (megatron path imports the megatron one), wraps in `ray.remote`, and maps Role.RewardModel to "reward_pool" when `reward_model.enable_resource_pool` else "global_pool". This is the ONLY worker class used for every teacher.

call_chain.step: Parse mt_opd config, validate, pop reward_mode
call_chain.detail: `_pop_direct_opd_rollout_options` (:86-92) reads `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.reward_mode` (default "opd_kl") and DELETES the key from the rollout node. `use_mt_opd = reward_mode=='mt_opd'`. Then reads mt_opd.teacher_domains / n_additional_teachers / domain_weighting / target_share_* / normalize_reward_scale / reward_scale_* / conflict_*. Raises if teacher_domains empty or use_rm False.

call_chain.step: Register N teacher RayClassWithInitArgs into one resource pool's class_dict
call_chain.detail: resource_pool = get_resource_pool(Role.RewardModel). Key str(Role.RewardModel)=='rm' gets config.reward_model. Optional key 'teacher_ref_rm' gets OmegaConf.merge(reward_model, teacher_ref_reward_model) (delta_opd/exopd only). Then for i in 1..mt_n_additional: key f'mt_rm_{i}' gets OmegaConf.merge(config.reward_model, config.mt_reward_model_{i}); a missing `mt_reward_model_{i}` key raises ValueError at :1431-1435. ALL teachers land in the SAME resource_pool dict.

call_chain.step: Create one colocated Ray actor class holding every role, spawn per-prefix WorkerGroups
call_chain.detail: `create_colocated_worker_cls(class_dict)` builds a `WorkerDict(Worker)` whose __init__ instantiates EVERY class in class_dict inside the same Ray actor process (DISABLE_WORKER_INIT=1), then `_bind_workers_method_to_parent` (base.py:681-726) copies each @register-decorated method onto WorkerDict under name `{key}_{method}` (e.g. `rm_compute_rm_score`, `mt_rm_1_compute_rm_score`) carrying the same MAGIC_ATTR. `RayWorkerGroup.__init__` (base.py:325-326) binds all of those onto the group; `spawn(prefix_set)` (base.py:479-512) makes one shallow WorkerGroup per prefix sharing the SAME actor handles and strips the `{prefix}_` prefix so each group exposes plain `compute_rm_score` / `init_model`.

call_chain.step: Ray placement: one bundle per GPU, STRICT_PACK per node, 1 actor per bundle
call_chain.detail: RayResourcePool built with max_colocate_count=1 (ray_trainer.py:375-377), so bundle={'CPU':1,'GPU':1}, one placement group per node with n_gpus_per_node bundles, strategy STRICT_PACK (bin_pack=True default). Each worker gets num_gpus=1/max_colocate_count=1 and env WORLD_SIZE/RANK/MASTER_ADDR/MASTER_PORT. Consequence: all N teacher models are FSDP-sharded over the same world_size and live in the same processes as the actor/rollout.

call_chain.step: init_model per teacher group: load each teacher as a causal LM
call_chain.detail: rm_wg=all_wg['rm'].init_model(); optional teacher_ref_rm_wg=all_wg['teacher_ref_rm']; then for i=1..N-1 `all_wg[f'mt_rm_{i}'].init_model()` and appended IN ASCENDING i to `self.mt_rm_wgs`. `_build_model` uses AutoModelForCausalLM (NOT a token/sequence-classification head), attn_implementation='flash_attention_2', dtype from `reward_model.model.dtype` (default 'bf16'), FSDP1 with `CPUOffload(offload_params=True)` hardcoded, or FSDP2 with CPUOffloadPolicy(pin_memory=True).

call_chain.step: Per step: student forward for top-k ids/log-probs, then set teacher meta_info
call_chain.detail: `actor_rollout_wg.compute_log_prob(batch)` adds old_log_probs / student_top_k_ids / student_top_k_log_probs. Then meta_info gets global_steps, is_plot, log_prob_top_k, top_k_strategy, kl_estimator, reward_weight_mode, teacher_temperature, reward_mode, top_p_intersec_p. Raises if reward_mode in {delta_opd, mt_opd} and log_prob_top_k <= 0 (:1973-1974).

`teacher_data = self.rm_wg.compute_rm_score(batch)`; `batch = batch.union(teacher_data)` -> installs teacher_on_student_log_probs, teacher_top_k_ids, teacher_top_k_log_probs, teacher_entropy, teacher_valid_counts, overlap_mask, teacher_in_student_mask (rm_scores is absent because top_k>0).

call_chain.step: WorkerGroup dispatch of compute_rm_score down to the worker
call_chain.detail: compute_rm_score is decorated `@register(dispatch_mode=make_nd_compute_dataproto_dispatch_fn(mesh_name='reward'))` (fsdp_workers.py:2662). That is a dict dispatch mode, so `_bind_worker_method` wires dispatch_fn=partial(dispatch_lazy_compute_data_proto,'reward'), collect_fn=partial(collect_lazy_compute_data_proto,'reward'), execute_fn=WorkerGroup.execute_all. `func_generator`'s Functor: dispatch_fn splits the DataProto into dp_size chunks (dp_size from `_query_dispatch_info('reward')`, a ONE_TO_ALL call answered per rank from `_register_dispatch_collect_info('reward', ...)` at fsdp_workers.py:1785-1791), ray.put's them (parallel_put), fans out one chunk per global rank via dp_rank_mapping, `execute_all` calls the actor method (which is WorkerDict.mt_rm_i_compute_rm_score -> self.worker_dict['mt_rm_i'].compute_rm_score), ray.get, then collect_fn keeps only ranks with is_collect=True and DataProto.concat's them.

`for i, extra_wg in enumerate(self.mt_rm_wgs, start=1): extra_raw = extra_wg.compute_rm_score(batch)` then unions ONLY `{f'mt_teacher_{i}_on_student_log_probs': extra_raw.batch['teacher_on_student_log_probs']}`. The rename is mandatory because DataProto.union asserts tensor equality on duplicate keys (protocol.py:113-119). All other teacher-i outputs (entropy, top-k ids, overlap masks) are DISCARDED.

call_chain.step: Assemble ordered teacher list and enforce count
call_chain.detail: `domains = batch.non_tensor_batch['domain']` (raises if absent). teacher_logps = [batch['teacher_on_student_log_probs']] then a `while f'mt_teacher_{i}_on_student_log_probs' in batch.batch` loop i=1,2,3,... -> strictly ascending index order. Raises if len(teacher_logps) != len(mt_opd.teacher_domains).

call_chain.step: Route per-sample to its domain teacher
call_chain.detail: `build_domain_weights(domains, domain_order=mt_teacher_domains, weighting='domain_routing')` -> [B,N] one-hot via `{d: i for i, d in enumerate(domain_order)}`; unknown domain falls back to uniform 1/N. `select_routed_teacher_logprobs` stacks to [N,B,T,K] and contracts with the weights. Then `apply_teacher_conflict_policy` (mt_opd.py:405-491) may replace the target with the cross-teacher mean or emit a [B,T] token weight. Result overwrites `batch.batch['teacher_on_student_log_probs']` IN PLACE.

call_chain.step: Standard OPD reward on the routed teacher target
call_chain.detail: `actor_rollout_wg.compute_distillation_reward(batch)` reads student_top_k_ids, student_top_k_log_probs, teacher_on_student_log_probs (+ teacher_top_k_ids / overlap_mask for non-only_stu strategies) and returns rm_scores ([B,T,K] for top_k>0).

compute_domain_share_metrics, compute_teacher_conflict_metrics, compute_domain_loss_weights -> optional `batch.batch['domain_loss_weight']` ([B] float, token-weighted mean 1). M3 mask policy folds its [B,T] weight into the same per-sequence channel.

config_keys.default: "opd_kl" (NOT declared in rollout.yaml nor in RolloutConfig)
config_keys.effect: Central switch. 'mt_opd' turns on the multi-teacher path; 'delta_opd'/'exopd' turn on teacher_ref_rm; 'opd_kl' is the single-teacher default. Read then DELETED from the rollout node via open_dict.
Ordered domain list; index i names the domain served by teacher i (teacher 0 = reward_model, teacher i>=1 = mt_reward_model_i). Consumed as `domain_order` in build_domain_weights.
How many `mt_reward_model_{i}` worker groups to create (i = 1..N). Should be len(teacher_domains)-1 but that is NOT validated at construction.
"domain_routing" = one-hot per-sample teacher selection; "uniform" = average all teachers' log-probs. No shipped script sets it.

Per-teacher overlay merged ON TOP of config.reward_model via OmegaConf.merge, becoming the whole config of that RewardModelWorker. mt_opd.sh sets enable, model.path, model.input_tokenizer=null, model.use_remove_padding=True, model.fsdp_config.param_offload=True.
Teacher 0's checkpoint. Loaded with AutoModelForCausalLM, so it must be a causal LM, not an RM head.

Non-null enables `_do_switch_chat_template=True` -> `_switch_chat_template_token_level` decode/re-encode with LEFT padding. null skips it and feeds raw input_ids/attention_mask/position_ids/responses.
Teacher weight dtype via PrecisionType.to_dtype; the module is also .to(model_dtype) after monkey patch. Not declared in dp_reward_model.yaml.
Selects the unpad/pack + ulysses branch of `_forward_micro_batch` vs the dense padded branch. Both produce the same output tuple.

Fused-kernel log_probs shortcut, taken only when no logits are needed (student_top_k_ids is None and compute_entropy False). Because compute_rm_score hardcodes compute_entropy=True, this shortcut is unreachable on the OPD path.
>1 builds an (dp, sp) device mesh, registers dispatch info with dp_rank from the dp mesh and is_collect only on sp-local-rank 0, and switches the pad-back path to gather_outputs_and_unpad.
FSDP shape for each teacher. NOTE: FSDP1 path hardcodes `CPUOffload(offload_params=True)` regardless of param_offload; only FSDP2 honours a CPUOffloadPolicy.
Micro-batching inside compute_rm_score. Dynamic path reorders rows (rearrange_micro_batches) and undoes it with get_reverse_idx over EVERY returned teacher tensor.

When True a separate 'reward_pool' is created and Role.RewardModel maps to it. Since teachers all fetch get_resource_pool(Role.RewardModel), every teacher shares that one pool; per-teacher pools are impossible.

K for the student top-k candidate set; forwarded as meta_info['log_prob_top_k']. Must be >0 for mt_opd, else ValueError. In the worker top_k>0 makes compute_rm_score return rm_scores=None and defer reward math to the actor.

Chooses how teacher log-probs are gathered onto student ids inside `_compute_teacher_top_k_log_probs`: only_stu/union/union-intersection/top_p_intersec gather from the full teacher distribution; 'intersection' masks to the teacher top-k and yields -inf outside.
Teacher logits are divided in place by this before log_softmax / entropy / top-k. Applied identically to every teacher because it comes from meta_info, not from the per-teacher config.
Nucleus cutoff for the top_p_intersec overlap mask in `_compute_student_topk_in_teacher_top_p_mask`.
Target per-domain GRADIENT share. Two parallel lists are accepted because a dict-valued Hydra override fails to compose; a dict form is also accepted. Names outside teacher_domains raise.
M2: folds per-domain reward magnitude into the share correction (alpha in [0,2]). Requires target_gradient_shares; anchored requires direction=multiply and stat=mean.
M3: none|mask|consensus on tokens where teachers disagree by more than the threshold (absolute nats or a self-calibrating quantile of the spread).

config_keys.default: none (required for delta_opd/exopd, unused for mt_opd)
config_keys.effect: Overlay merged onto reward_model to build the extra 'teacher_ref_rm' worker group, whose teacher_on_student_log_probs becomes teacher_ref_on_student_log_probs.
Makes the [B,T,K] rm_scores be used directly as the token-level advantage (the reward the teacher path produces is already an advantage).

entrypoints.what_it_does: The single class used for EVERY teacher (teacher 0, teacher_ref, and each mt_reward_model_i). Sets up NCCL, an FSDP device mesh, an optional Ulysses (dp, sp) mesh, and registers dispatch/collect info under mesh_name='reward'. Docstring still claims AutoModelForTokenClassification; the implementation loads a causal LM.
Imports external libs then `self.reward_module = self._build_model(config=self.config)`. Called once per teacher worker group from ray_trainer._init_workers.

OPEN-MOPD CORE PATCH: loads the teacher with `AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(..., attn_implementation='flash_attention_2')` so the worker can emit full-vocabulary logits, applies apply_monkey_patch for remove_padding/ulysses, then wraps in FSDP1 (CPUOffload(offload_params=True) hardcoded, ZeRO-3 sharding) or FSDP2.

entrypoints.signature: @register(dispatch_mode=make_nd_compute_dataproto_dispatch_fn(mesh_name='reward')) @DistProfiler.annotate(color='brown') def compute_rm_score(self, data: DataProto, kl_estimator='k1') -> DataProto
entrypoints.what_it_does: The teacher-LM entrypoint. Returns a DataProto whose tensors are a SUBSET of {rm_scores, teacher_on_student_log_probs, teacher_top_k_ids, teacher_top_k_log_probs, teacher_entropy, teacher_valid_counts, overlap_mask, teacher_in_student_mask}. When log_prob_top_k>0 it deliberately returns rm_scores=None (reward math is deferred to the actor); when top_k==0 it returns the scalar-per-token rm_scores = -(student_logp - teacher_logp). Output stays on GPU (the `.to('cpu')` is commented out at :2870).

entrypoints.signature: def _forward_micro_batch(self, micro_batch, student_top_k_ids=None, compute_entropy=False, top_k=0, strategy='only_stu', teacher_temperature=1.0, top_p_intersec_p=0.99) -> tuple of 8
entrypoints.what_it_does: Returns (rm_log_probs, teacher_on_student_log_probs, teacher_top_k_ids, teacher_top_k_log_probs, teacher_entropy, teacher_valid_counts, teacher_overlap_mask, teacher_in_student_mask). Divides logits by teacher_temperature, slices [-response_length-1:-1] so teacher logits at position t align with the student token at t+1.

entrypoints.signature: def _compute_teacher_top_k_log_probs(self, logits, student_ids, top_k, strategy='only_stu', chunk_size=1024, top_p_intersec_p=0.99) -> 6-tuple
entrypoints.what_it_does: Chunked (1024 rows) evaluation of the teacher distribution on the student's K candidate ids plus the teacher's own top-K, returning (log_probs_on_student_ids [N,K_s], valid_counts [N], overlap_mask S_in_T [N,K_s], teacher_top_k_ids [N,K_t], teacher_top_k_log_probs [N,K_t], teacher_in_student T_in_S [N,K_t]).

OPEN-MOPD addition beside upstream's right-padding `_switch_chat_template`: re-applies the teacher's chat template with LEFT padding so the response remains at the end of the sequence and `[-response_length-1:-1]` still indexes it. Requires actor and teacher to share a vocabulary; prints a per-token match diagnostic on rank 0.

entrypoints.signature: build_domain_weights(domains, domain_order: list[str], device, weighting='domain_routing') -> Tensor[B, N]
entrypoints.what_it_does: THE ordering contract. Builds `{d: i for i, d in enumerate(domain_order)}` and one-hots each sample onto teacher index i. Unknown domain -> uniform 1/N (silent).

entrypoints.signature: select_routed_teacher_logprobs(teacher_logprobs: list[Tensor], domain_weights: Tensor) -> Tensor[B, T, K]
entrypoints.what_it_does: Stacks the N per-teacher [B,T,K] tensors to [N,B,T,K] and contracts with the [B,N] weight matrix. Raises if the weight width != N or if the tensors are not 3-D.

entrypoints.signature: apply_teacher_conflict_policy(routed_logprobs, teacher_logprobs, response_mask, policy='none', conflict_nats=1.0, conflict_quantile=None) -> (Tensor, Tensor|None, dict)
entrypoints.what_it_does: Measures cross-teacher spread on the student's top-1 candidate (index 0 of K) and either masks contested tokens (with a rescale so the total loss magnitude is preserved) or substitutes the across-teacher mean on agreeing tokens.

entrypoints.signature: compute_domain_loss_weights(domains, response_mask, target_shares=None, rm_scores=None, normalize_reward_scale=False, reward_scale_stat='mean', reward_scale_direction='divide', reward_anchor=None) -> Tensor[B] | None
entrypoints.what_it_does: Turns a target per-domain gradient share into a per-sequence weight target_d/observed_d (observed = this batch's token share), optionally folded with per-domain reward magnitude, token-weighted-mean-normalised to 1.

Creates one facade WorkerGroup per class_dict key, all sharing the same Ray actor handles, and strips the `{prefix}_` from the bound method names. This is how `all_wg['mt_rm_1'].compute_rm_score` reaches `WorkerDict.mt_rm_1_compute_rm_score`.
Builds the WorkerDict Ray actor that instantiates every registered role (actor_rollout + rm + teacher_ref_rm + mt_rm_1..N) inside ONE process, and monkey-patches prefixed delegating methods onto it.

files.role: Contains RewardModelWorker (line 1735), the teacher-LM worker. Open-MOPD rewrote _build_model to load AutoModelForCausalLM, added _compute_entropy_safe, _compute_teacher_top_k_log_probs, _switch_chat_template_token_level, and rewrote compute_rm_score to return teacher log-probs instead of a scalar reward. Also holds ActorRolloutRefWorker's compute_distillation_reward / compute_delta_opd_reward / compute_exopd_reward / compute_log_probs_for_ids.

Builds the N teacher worker groups from +mt_reward_model_{i} (1413-1440, 1482-1496), parses and validates all mt_opd.* config (641-777), and drives the per-step teacher scoring + routing loop (2100-2230).

Pure-function MT-OPD library: domain->teacher weight matrix, routed log-prob selection, per-domain share metrics, per-domain loss weights (M1/M2), cross-teacher conflict metrics and policy (M3), and refresh_opd_advantage (M4).

Upstream megatron RewardModelWorker (line 1105). UNTOUCHED by Open-MOPD: compute_rm_score (1268-1275) just calls self.rm.compute_reward and returns a scalar-style DataProto on CPU. No teacher log-prob path, so mt_opd requires reward_model.strategy in {fsdp, fsdp2}.

Ray plumbing: RayResourcePool placement groups (91-139), RayWorkerGroup construction/binding (262-330, 362-444), spawn/prefix rebinding (479-512), func_generator dispatch Functor (41-59), create_colocated_worker_cls + _bind_workers_method_to_parent (681-790).
@register decorator, Dispatch enum, and the mesh-aware dispatch/collect functions. make_nd_compute_dataproto_dispatch_fn('reward') (311-315) is what compute_rm_score uses.
WorkerGroup._bind_worker_method (185-253): reads MAGIC_ATTR off each @register-ed method, resolves dispatch_fn/collect_fn/execute_fn and setattr's the generated Functor onto the group.

Worker base: _register_dispatch_collect_info / _query_dispatch_info / _query_collect_info (86-131), the per-instance mesh->dp_rank registry that makes mesh_name='reward' dispatch work per teacher instance.
Registers Role.RewardModel -> fsdp/megatron RewardModelWorker and its resource pool (202-226); builds the global_pool / optional reward_pool spec (177-200).
Role enum and str(Role) mapping. str(Role.RewardModel) == 'rm', which is the class_dict key / spawn prefix for teacher 0.
RolloutConfig dataclass; declares log_prob_top_k=256, top_k_strategy, top_p_intersec_p, reward_weight_mode, teacher_temperature, exopd_lambda (149-162). reward_mode is NOT declared here.

Base reward_model Hydra group: enable, enable_resource_pool, n_gpus_per_node/nnodes, strategy, model.{input_tokenizer,path,external_lib,trust_remote_code}, micro_batch_size*, max_length, use_dynamic_bsz, forward_max_token_len_per_gpu, profiler. Does NOT declare dtype/log_prob_top_k/teacher_temperature.
FSDP overlay: strategy=fsdp, model.use_shm/use_remove_padding/use_fused_kernels, model.fsdp_config.*, ulysses_sequence_parallel_size=1.

The only shipped launcher that constructs the multi-teacher override set: teacher_domains list, n_additional_teachers, and one +mt_reward_model_{i} block per extra teacher. Enforces len(domains)==len(teacher paths) at :58-60.

gotchas: The teacher index -> domain binding is POSITIONAL AND UNCHECKED. teacher 0 is always `reward_model.model.path`, teacher i is `mt_reward_model_{i}.model.path`, and `mt_opd.teacher_domains[i]` names the domain. Nothing in the code verifies that the checkpoint at index i is actually the domain-i teacher (ray_trainer.py:2116-2133, mt_opd.py:55-59). Swap two --teacher paths and training silently routes math prompts to the code teacher. The ONLY guard is the count check at ray_trainer.py:2121-2126, and it fires at step 1 AFTER all N teachers have been loaded onto GPUs.

`mt_opd.n_additional_teachers` and `len(mt_opd.teacher_domains)` are parsed independently at ray_trainer.py:662-663 with NO consistency check at construction time. A mismatch costs a full worker-group spin-up before the runtime ValueError.

A domain label that is not in `teacher_domains` does NOT raise; `build_domain_weights` silently falls back to uniform 1/N weighting for that sample (mt_opd.py:57-61). A typo in the dataset's `domain` column therefore averages all three teachers instead of failing loudly.

All N teachers share ONE resource pool and ONE set of Ray actors. `create_colocated_worker_cls` instantiates every role inside the same WorkerDict process (ray/base.py:769-781) and `spawn` hands out facade WorkerGroups over the SAME actor handles (ray/base.py:501-511). So N teacher models + the actor + rollout engine are co-resident per GPU; per-teacher parallelism or per-teacher placement is not expressible. `reward_model.enable_resource_pool` moves ALL teachers together because every teacher fetches get_resource_pool(Role.RewardModel) (ray_trainer.py:1415).

The FSDP1 branch hardcodes `cpu_offload=CPUOffload(offload_params=True)` (fsdp_workers.py:1867) and ignores `model.fsdp_config.param_offload`. Every teacher's shard therefore sits in pinned/host RAM; N teachers multiply host memory, not just device memory.

The megatron RewardModelWorker was NOT patched. megatron_workers.py:1268-1275 returns `self.rm.compute_reward(data)` with no teacher_on_student_log_probs, so `reward_model.strategy=megatron` + `reward_mode=mt_opd` would fail on the missing key at ray_trainer.py:2106 rather than at config validation.

compute_rm_score deliberately returns NO `rm_scores` key when log_prob_top_k > 0 (fsdp_workers.py:2825-2828). Any caller that expects a reward tensor from the teacher worker gets only log-probs; the reward is computed later by `actor_rollout_wg.compute_distillation_reward`. That is why ray_trainer raises if log_prob_top_k <= 0 under mt_opd (ray_trainer.py:1973-1974).

Only `teacher_on_student_log_probs` is kept from teachers 1..N (ray_trainer.py:2105-2107). Their teacher_entropy, teacher_top_k_ids, teacher_top_k_log_probs, overlap_mask and teacher_in_student_mask are computed on GPU and then thrown away, and `compute_entropy=True` is hardcoded at fsdp_workers.py:2685 so the full-vocab entropy pass is paid for every teacher every step.

The rename in ray_trainer.py:2105-2107 is mandatory, not cosmetic: `DataProto.union` asserts tensor equality on duplicate keys (protocol.py:113-119), so unioning teacher i's `teacher_on_student_log_probs` directly would abort.

`batch.batch['teacher_on_student_log_probs']` is OVERWRITTEN in place with the routed tensor (ray_trainer.py:2149). After that line, teacher 0's raw target is unrecoverable from the batch, while `teacher_logps[0]` (the local Python list) still holds it - that is what the conflict metrics use.

The whole `batch` (including every tensor teacher 0 already produced) is passed to each subsequent teacher's compute_rm_score (ray_trainer.py:2104). Those tensors are chunked, ray.put'd and shipped to every rank even though the worker reads only old_log_probs / student_top_k_ids / student_top_k_log_probs / response_mask / input_ids / attention_mask / position_ids / responses.

Teacher 0 and teachers 1..N get DIFFERENT preprocessing in the shipped launcher. `reward_model.model.input_tokenizer` defaults to ${actor_rollout_ref.model.path} (reward_model.yaml:33) and mt_opd.sh does not override it for teacher 0, so teacher 0 goes through `_switch_chat_template_token_level` (decode -> re-apply chat template -> re-tokenize -> left-pad/truncate), while mt_opd.sh:109 sets `input_tokenizer=null` for teachers 1..N so they consume the raw input_ids. Same prompt, two different token streams.

`_switch_chat_template_token_level` force-fits the re-tokenized response to the original `response_length` by truncating or right-padding with pad_token_id (fsdp_workers.py:2612-2627). Any tokenizer drift shifts teacher log-probs off the student's tokens with no error raised - only a rank-0 debug print of the match count.

`reward_mode` is not declared in rollout.yaml nor in the RolloutConfig dataclass, yet both scripts/local/mt_opd.sh:87 and scripts/local/opd.sh:66 pass it WITHOUT a leading `+`. `_pop_direct_opd_rollout_options` defends against absence (`rollout.get('reward_mode', 'opd_kl')`, `if 'reward_mode' in rollout: del`), which is consistent with the key sometimes not existing.

`domain` must be present in non_tensor_batch or step 1 raises (ray_trainer.py:2109-2114). It is a dataset column produced by experiments/data/build_mix_rl_union.py:108; it must survive batch.repeat and _balance_batch reordering. The M1 loss weight is deliberately materialised as a [B] TENSOR (`domain_loss_weight`) because a numpy string array would not survive the dynamic-batch reordering downstream (comment at ray_trainer.py:2185-2188).

`_register_dispatch_collect_info` raises on a duplicate mesh_name (worker.py:97-98). Multiple colocated RewardModelWorkers all register mesh 'reward' and only avoid the clash because each is a separate Python object with its own name-mangled `_Worker__dispatch_dp_rank` dict; WorkerDict's own (empty) registry is shadowed by `_rebind_actor_methods` stripping the prefix. This is load-bearing but implicit.

`teacher_temperature`, `log_prob_top_k`, `top_k_strategy`, `top_p_intersec_p` all reach the worker through `data.meta_info` set once from `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.*` (ray_trainer.py:1981-1987), so they are GLOBAL across teachers. The per-teacher config fallbacks (`self.config.get(...)` at fsdp_workers.py:2720-2725) are dead on this path.

The `use_fused_kernels` fast path in _forward_micro_batch is unreachable on the OPD path: it requires `not need_logits`, but compute_rm_score hardcodes `compute_entropy = True` (fsdp_workers.py:2685), which forces need_logits True (fsdp_workers.py:2052).

open_mopd_specific.what: RewardModelWorker loads a full causal LM instead of a reward head
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: The docstring still says 'we only implement the reward model that is subclass of AutoModelForTokenClassification' while the code calls AutoModelForCausalLM. Upstream verl's FSDP RewardModelWorker uses a classification head and returns one scalar per sequence. The stale docstring is direct evidence of an in-place patch.

open_mopd_specific.what: compute_rm_score returns teacher log-probs, not a reward
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: For log_prob_top_k>0 it sets `rm_scores = None` with the comment 'Reward calculation is moved to ray_trainer for top_k > 0' and instead emits teacher_on_student_log_probs / teacher_top_k_ids / teacher_top_k_log_probs / teacher_entropy / teacher_valid_counts / overlap_mask / teacher_in_student_mask. Upstream returns `rm_scores` expanded to token level via _expand_to_token_level. Note _expand_to_token_level (:2401-2417) is still present but is no longer called from compute_rm_score - effectively dead on this path.

open_mopd_specific.what: _compute_teacher_top_k_log_probs and _compute_student_topk_in_teacher_top_p_mask
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Chunked S_in_T / T_in_S overlap computation over the student's top-K candidate set with strategy switches only_stu / union / union-intersection / intersection / top_p_intersec. Nothing in upstream verl needs a student candidate set inside the reward model.

open_mopd_specific.what: _compute_entropy_safe
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Chunked full-vocabulary entropy of the teacher distribution, logged as teacher_entropy. A scalar reward model has no distribution to take entropy of.

open_mopd_specific.what: _switch_chat_template_token_level (left-padded variant)
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Explicit contrast in its own docstring: 'Unlike _switch_chat_template (which uses right-padding for sequence-level RM), this function uses LEFT-padding so that the response stays at the end'. Upstream's right-padded version is still present at :2418-2477.

open_mopd_specific.what: N teacher worker-group registration from +mt_reward_model_{i}
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Comment 'MT-OPD: register additional RL teacher workers (teachers 1..N, teacher_0 = rm_wg)'. Upstream verl registers exactly one Role.RewardModel entry; there is no notion of extra RM worker groups keyed `mt_rm_{i}` nor of a `self.mt_rm_wgs` list.

open_mopd_specific.what: teacher_ref_rm worker group
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: A second RewardModelWorker built from OmegaConf.merge(reward_model, teacher_ref_reward_model) to score the teacher's pre-RL base for delta_opd/exopd. Uses the same class as a teacher but plays the reference role.

open_mopd_specific.what: The whole mt_opd config surface
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: teacher_domains, n_additional_teachers, domain_weighting, target_share_domains/values, target_gradient_shares, normalize_reward_scale, reward_scale_stat/direction/anchored, conflict_policy/nats/quantile. None of these keys exist in any Hydra yaml or dataclass in verl/trainer/config or verl/workers/config - they are all `+`-injected trees, confirming they are additions rather than upstream schema.

open_mopd_specific.what: verl/workers/actor/mt_opd.py in its entirety
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Module docstring: 'Multi-Teacher OPD (MT-OPD) utilities. Domain-routing helpers for regular OPD'. Exports build_domain_weights / select_routed_teacher_logprobs / compute_domain_share_metrics / compute_teacher_conflict_metrics / compute_domain_loss_weights / apply_teacher_conflict_policy, plus refresh_opd_advantage (M4).

open_mopd_specific.why_specific: `_pop_direct_opd_rollout_options` reads actor_rollout_ref.rollout.reward_mode then deletes it under open_dict so the downstream RolloutConfig dataclass (which has no such field, see workers/config/rollout.py) still instantiates. report.purpose: The teacher/reward-model worker layer repurposes verl's RewardModelWorker from a scalar reward scorer into a frozen teacher language model that returns per-token log-probabilities over the student's own top-K candidate ids. Open-MOPD patched the FSDP variant to load the teacher with AutoModelForCausalLM (not a classification head) and to emit teacher_on_student_log_probs plus overlap/entropy diagnostics instead of rm_scores, deferring the actual reward math to the actor. ray_trainer then instantiates N of these identical workers (teacher 0 from config.reward_model, teachers 1..N-1 from +mt_reward_model_{i}), all co-resident in one Ray placement group, calls compute_rm_score on each, and routes the per-sample teacher choice by matching non_tensor_batch['domain'] against the positional list mt_opd.teacher_domains. Dispatch reaches the worker through the mesh-aware DataProto dispatch mode registered under mesh_name='reward'.
report.subsystem: teacher_workers (RewardModelWorker-as-teacher-LM, N-teacher worker-group construction, ray placement, and WorkerGroup dispatch)
uncertain: Whether `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.reward_mode=mt_opd` (no leading `+`) as written in scripts/local/mt_opd.sh:87 and scripts/local/opd.sh:66 actually composes under Hydra. I could not find `reward_mode` declared in verl/trainer/config/rollout/rollout.yaml or in the RolloutConfig dataclass (verl/workers/config/rollout.py), and Hydra normally rejects overriding an undeclared key in struct mode. The defensive `rollout.get('reward_mode', 'opd_kl')` + conditional `del` in _pop_direct_opd_rollout_options (ray_trainer.py:86-92) suggests the key is sometimes absent. I did not execute the launcher, so I cannot say whether the shipped script runs as-is or whether the real experiment runs used `+`.

The vendored verl is squashed into 2 commits (a8d1f7f, 4809a96) with no upstream remote in this checkout, so I could not `git diff` against upstream verl 0.7.0.dev. My upstream-vs-Open-MOPD attribution rests on in-file evidence (stale docstrings, MT-OPD comments, keys absent from every config schema, and the untouched megatron twin), not on a diff.
Whether `mt_opd.domain_weighting='uniform'` is ever exercised. No shipped script or config sets it, and I found no test referencing it; it may be reachable-but-unused.

`refresh_opd_advantage` (mt_opd.py:338-402, the M4/AsyncOPD advantage refresh) is exported by name in mt_opd.py's docstring context but is NOT in `__all__` (mt_opd.py:14-21) and I found no caller in ray_trainer.py. It may be dead in the released recipe or wired from dp_actor.update_policy; I did not exhaustively trace dp_actor.

Exactly how the `domain` column travels from the parquet through RLHFDataset/collate_fn into non_tensor_batch. I confirmed the producer (build_mix_rl_union.py:108) and the consumer (ray_trainer.py:2109) but did not read the dataset/collate code, so I cannot state whether it arrives as a top-level column or via extra_info.

corrections.claim: `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_top_k` default is "256 (RolloutConfig)"; K for the student top-k candidate set; "Must be >0 for mt_opd, else ValueError" — implying the shipped mt_opd.sh produces a working run.
corrections.why_wrong: The 256 in the dataclass never reaches either read site. `rollout.yaml` (326 lines) does not declare `log_prob_top_k` at all, and both consumers read it off the raw Hydra DictConfig with an explicit fallback of 0. OmegaConf `DictConfig.get(key, default)` returns the default for a missing key even in struct mode, so both resolve to 0. `RolloutConfig` is only materialized as a *local* (`rollout_config`) for the vLLM engine and never written back onto `self.config.rollout`. Consequence: `scripts/local/mt_opd.sh`, which never sets `log_prob_top_k`, raises `ValueError: reward_mode=mt_opd requires actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_top_k > 0` before any teacher is even called. The user must add `+actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_top_k=<K>` (with a leading `+`, since the key is undeclared).
corrections.correct_fact: Effective default of `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_top_k` as seen by the trainer and the actor worker is 0, not 256. The dataclass default 256 only affects the rollout-engine construction.

call_chain.detail: Builds `python3 -m verl.trainer.main_ppo <override>...`. Plain `key=value` for existing keys, `+key=value` for new ones. local_run_command (common.sh:226) prints it; execs only with --run.

defaults order: actor@actor_rollout_ref.actor=dp_actor, data@data=legacy_data, ref@actor_rollout_ref.ref=dp_ref, rollout@actor_rollout_ref.rollout=rollout, model@actor_rollout_ref.model=hf_model, critic@critic=dp_critic, reward_model@reward_model=dp_reward_model, algorithm@@algorithm.rollout_correction=rollout_correction, then _self_. CLI overrides last.

Reads ray_kwargs.ray_init, transfer_queue.enable (injects TRANSFER_QUEUE_ENABLE=1), global_profiler.tool/steps (nsys runtime_env), ray_kwargs.timeline_json_file; then ray.get(TaskRunner.run.remote(config)).

OmegaConf.resolve(config) in place. Registers Role.Critic from critic.strategy, Role.RewardModel only when reward_model.enable is True (routed to 'reward_pool' when enable_resource_pool), Role.RefPolicy when algorithm.use_kl_in_reward or actor.use_kl_loss.

call_chain.detail: n_gpus = trainer.n_gpus_per_node * trainer.nnodes. Instantiates FSDPActorConfig via omega_conf_to_dataclass(config.actor_rollout_ref.actor) at line 151 - where ActorConfig.__post_init__ and .validate() fire.

config_keys.default: none; empty raises ValueError('reward_mode=mt_opd requires mt_opd.teacher_domains to be set')

Number of extra RM worker groups (i=1..N). Each needs a mt_reward_model_{i} key or init_workers raises at 1432. mt_opd.sh sets teacher_count-1.

Legal: domain_routing (one-hot per sample) or uniform (1/N average). NOT validated anywhere; build_domain_weights only special-cases the exact string 'uniform' (mt_opd.py:51), so a typo silently means domain_routing.

Parallel-list form of target_gradient_shares (domain names). Must match len(target_share_values) or 681 raises. Exists because a dict-valued Hydra override 'fails to compose on the executor' (comment 671-673). Takes precedence - the dict form is read only in the else branch.
Parallel float list matching target_share_domains; both must be non-None to be used.

config_keys.default: None (leave the loss untouched, bit-identical to the pre-M1 path)
config_keys.effect: M1. dict domain->desired gradient share. A key not in teacher_domains raises at 699. Normalized over domains present in the batch (mt_opd.py:223-229). Produces batch['domain_loss_weight'].
M2. False/None = off, True = alpha 1.0, or a float alpha validated to [0,2] at 713-717 (again mt_opd.py:237). Requires target_gradient_shares or 741 raises. alpha=0 recovers M1 exactly.
Legal mean|q75|q90|top10, NOT checked in ray_trainer - the only raise is mt_opd.py:239-240, so a bad value fails at the first MT step rather than startup.

Legal divide|multiply, validated 722-726. 'divide' is the original and documented as measured harmful (mt_opd.py:290-296: IF loss weight 27->91, grad token share 57% vs target 33%). 'multiply' makes budget follow the remaining teacher gap.

M2v2. Anchors per-domain magnitude at this run's first batch (captured from mt_opd/domain/{d}/reward_abs_mean, 2189-2201) so step 1 is exactly M1 and only drift moves shares. Requires direction=multiply (730) and stat=mean (734).

M3. Legal none|mask|consensus, validated 749-753 (again mt_opd.py:438). mask zeroes per-token loss weight where teachers disagree and rescales to preserve total loss; consensus swaps in the cross-teacher mean on agreeing tokens. Silent no-op with <2 teachers.

Absolute nats threshold for disagreement on the student's top-1 candidate; ignored when conflict_quantile is set. Docstring records mean spread 0.131 nats and only 0.70% of tokens above 1.0, so the default catches almost nothing.
Self-calibrating alternative to conflict_nats; must be in (0,1) exclusive or 762 raises. Pins the contested-token fraction instead of a drifting absolute threshold.

config_keys.default: none; missing raises ValueError("reward_mode=mt_opd: expected config key 'mt_reward_model_{i}' for teacher {i} but it is missing")
config_keys.effect: Per-teacher overlay merged over config.reward_model. mt_opd.sh supplies enable, model.path, model.input_tokenizer=null, model.use_remove_padding=True, model.fsdp_config.param_offload=True - all mirroring real reward_model keys (reward_model.yaml:33, dp_reward_model.yaml:24,42); only the top-level group is new.

config_keys.effect: Pre-RL base-teacher overlay merged over config.reward_model; only for reward_mode in {delta_opd, exopd}. No launcher and no YAML provides it, so those modes are append-only.

Selects the reward path: opd_kl | delta_opd | mt_opd | exopd. No whitelist - any other string falls through to the generic `elif top_k > 0` branch at 2232 and silently behaves like opd_kl. Deleted from the config right after being read.

config_keys.default: TWO conflicting defaults: 0 at every DictConfig read (ray_trainer.py:1968, fsdp_workers.py:1022,2720) vs 256 in the RolloutConfig dataclass (workers/config/rollout.py:154). Undeclared in YAML so both stay live.

gotchas: mt_opd.* keys are NOT declared in any YAML - all 13 require a Hydra append: `+mt_opd.teacher_domains=[math,code,if]`, `+mt_opd.n_additional_teachers=2`, `+mt_opd.domain_weighting=domain_routing|uniform`, `+mt_opd.target_share_domains=[...]`, `+mt_opd.target_share_values=[...]`, `+mt_opd.target_gradient_shares={...}`, `+mt_opd.normalize_reward_scale=<bool|float in [0,2]>`, `+mt_opd.reward_scale_stat=mean|q75|q90|top10`, `+mt_opd.reward_scale_direction=divide|multiply`, `+mt_opd.reward_scale_anchored=<bool>`, `+mt_opd.conflict_policy=none|mask|consensus`, `+mt_opd.conflict_nats=<float>`, `+mt_opd.conflict_quantile=<float in (0,1)>`. mt_opd.sh supplies only the first two (lines 92-93), so M1/M2/M3 are all OFF in the shipped launcher.

Same append-only status outside the mt_opd group: `+mt_reward_model_{i}.*`, `+teacher_ref_reward_model.*`, `+actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_top_k`, `+...top_k_strategy`, `+...top_p_intersec_p`, `+...reward_weight_mode`, `+...teacher_temperature`, `+...exopd_lambda`, `+actor_rollout_ref.actor.opd_refresh_advantage`, `+actor_rollout_ref.actor.opd_reward_weight_mode`, `+data.gen_batch_size`, `+data.domain_weights.*`, `+trainer.val_only`.

LIKELY BROKEN LAUNCHERS: `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.reward_mode` is written WITHOUT a leading `+` at opd.sh:66 and mt_opd.sh:87, but `grep -c reward_mode training/verl/verl/trainer/config/rollout/rollout.yaml` returns 0 and it is not a RolloutConfig field either. A Hydra `key=value` override on a key absent from the composed config raises ConfigCompositionException ('Could not override ... To append to your config use +...'). I could not execute this - hydra is not importable here (ModuleNotFoundError) - and the repo's own launcher test cannot catch it because it substitutes /bin/echo for the Python binary (experiments/tests/test_local_shell_entrypoints.py:56-57). The paired `+mt_opd.teacher_domains` and `+mt_reward_model_1.enable` appends on adjacent lines show the author knew the distinction, which makes the missing `+` look like an oversight rather than a declared key I failed to find.

Two live defaults for one key: log_prob_top_k is 256 in the RolloutConfig dataclass (workers/config/rollout.py:154) but 0 at all three DictConfig read sites (ray_trainer.py:1968, fsdp_workers.py:1022, 2720). With no YAML declaration the dataclass value is used only where the dataclass is consulted (the vLLM engine) while the OPD reward path sees 0 - and reward_mode in {delta_opd, mt_opd} then dies at 1974 with 'requires actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_top_k > 0'. MT-OPD cannot run without appending this key.

`actor_rollout_ref.rollout.kl_estimator` is unreachable. Read at 1970 with default 'k1', but in neither rollout.yaml nor RolloutConfig, so appending it with `+` would break omega_conf_to_dataclass(self.config.rollout) at fsdp_workers.py:610 (hydra instantiate, unexpected kwarg). Permanently 'k1'. This is the mirror image of reward_mode, which needed an explicit `del` to survive.

Suspicious defaults-list entry: ppo_trainer.yaml:34 reads `- algorithm@@algorithm.rollout_correction: rollout_correction` with a DOUBLE `@`, while ppo_megatron_trainer.yaml:19 reads `- algorithm@algorithm: rollout_correction` (single `@`) and rollout_correction.yaml:2 documents the intended CLI path as `algorithm.rollout_correction.rollout_is=...`. If Hydra splits on the first `@`, the package becomes the literal '@algorithm.rollout_correction' and the group lands under a stray top-level `@algorithm` key, leaving algorithm.rollout_correction absent. That would be silent: ray_trainer.py:2387 reads it with `.get(..., None)`, maybe_apply_rollout_correction treats None as 'no bypass', and rollout_correction.yaml is all-null anyway - so disabled-by-accident and disabled-by-default look identical at runtime. I could not execute Hydra to resolve it.

Validation errors the shipped launchers hit even after the reward_mode issue: with defaults actor.use_dynamic_bsz=false and both actor.ppo_micro_batch_size and ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu are null, so ActorConfig.__post_init__ asserts (workers/config/actor.py:143). The launchers set data.train_batch_size=1 while actor.ppo_mini_batch_size is 256, so ActorConfig.validate raises 'train_batch_size (1) must be >= actor.ppo_mini_batch_size (256)' (actor.py:160). And reward_model.enable=True with reward_model.use_dynamic_bsz resolving false (via ${critic.use_dynamic_bsz} -> ${oc.select:actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz,false}) trips 'Please set at least one of reward_model.micro_batch_size or ...per_gpu' (utils/config.py:171-174). All three need `--extra` overrides the launchers do not supply.

`or`-fallback truthiness traps: `OmegaConf.select(...) or <default>` discards an explicitly configured falsy value. `+mt_opd.conflict_nats=0` silently becomes 1.0 (754-756); `+mt_opd.conflict_quantile=0` becomes None (757-758); `+actor_rollout_ref.rollout.exopd_lambda=0` becomes 1.0 (649-651). Only normalize_reward_scale uses an explicit None/False/True ladder (706-712).

Validation is split across two files and two moments. ray_trainer validates conflict_policy (749), reward_scale_direction (722), reward_scale_anchored's two preconditions (730,734), normalize_reward_scale's range (713) and its target_gradient_shares dependency (740), target_gradient_shares' domain membership (697), the parallel-list length match (680) and conflict_quantile's range (759) - all at __init__. reward_scale_stat is NOT checked at __init__; its only raise is mt_opd.py:239, reached during the first MT step. domain_weighting is never validated at all.

MT-OPD hard-requires a top-level `domain` column in the training parquet - ray_trainer.py:2111 raises "reward_mode=mt_opd requires non_tensor_batch['domain']". Nothing in the data config declares or checks it; RLHFDataset just passes every parquet column through (rl_dataset.py:338). A label not in mt_opd.teacher_domains does not error - it silently gets uniform weighting across all teachers (mt_opd.py:56-61).

Two independent domain registries can disagree: mt_opd.teacher_domains is configurable, but DomainWeightedSampler hard-codes DOMAIN_ORDER = ('math','code','if') (domain_weighted_sampler.py:16) and raises on any empty pool among exactly those three (line 66). A different teacher domain set plus the weighted sampler is not consistently supported.

Teacher count is asserted twice at different sites: n_additional_teachers drives worker-group creation (missing mt_reward_model_{i} raises at 1432) while len(teacher_domains) is checked against the returned logprob tensor count at 2121-2126. mt_opd.sh derives n_additional_teachers = teacher_count-1 and separately validates domain count == teacher path count (58-60), so they only line up if you go through the launcher.

reward_mode has no whitelist: anything other than delta_opd / mt_opd / exopd falls through to the generic `elif top_k > 0` branch at 2232, so a typo like 'mtopd' silently trains plain opd_kl instead of failing.

sft.sh targets sft_trainer_engine.yaml, not sft_trainer.yaml (sft_trainer.py:378 sets config_name='sft_trainer_engine'). The legacy sft_trainer.yaml uses model.partial_pretrain (34) and has no data.use_dynamic_bsz, so sft.sh's `model.path=` and `data.use_dynamic_bsz=True` would fail against it. SFT config edits must go to sft_trainer_engine.yaml.

BaseConfig instances are frozen after construction (base_config.py:33-38). Escape hatches: ActorConfig allows ppo_mini_batch_size / ppo_micro_batch_size / ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu / ppo_infer_micro_batch_size_per_gpu (actor.py:86-91); RolloutConfig allows max_model_len and load_format (rollout.py:99); MultiTurnConfig allows max_assistant_turns / max_user_turns (rollout.py:48). Runtime code mutating anything else must work on the DictConfig.

RolloutConfig declares `skip_tokenizer_init` twice - True at workers/config/rollout.py:103 and False at 213. Dataclasses keep the last definition, so the effective dataclass default is False, contradicting both the earlier line and rollout.yaml:301 which sets True. The YAML wins in practice, but reading the dataclass alone gives the wrong answer.

`algorithm._target_: verl.trainer.config.AlgoConfig` (ppo_trainer.yaml:69) is decorative in the RayPPOTrainer path - AlgoConfig is only a type annotation in core_algos.py, never instantiated by the trainer. Its field list is documentation, not an enforced schema, and `+algorithm.foo=1` would not be rejected.

Undeclared keys are fatal only where a dataclass conversion happens (utils/config.py:42-64). Converted: actor_rollout_ref.actor, .rollout, .model, .ref.fsdp_config, critic. NOT converted: algorithm, trainer, data, and the whole mt_opd surface - which is precisely why the mt_opd group can be a free-form append.
trainer/config/npu_profile/npu_profile.yaml is dead in this tree: no YAML defaults entry mounts it and the only Python reference is commented out (recipe/fully_async_policy/ray_trainer.py:97).
common.sh's local_die uses `return 2` rather than `exit` (38-41), so validation failures depend on `set -e` propagating out of the calling context.

The Megatron option files (actor/megatron_actor, ref/megatron_ref, reward_model/megatron_reward_model, critic/megatron_critic, optim/megatron, engine/megatron) are unreachable from ppo_trainer.yaml and selected only by ppo_megatron_trainer.yaml, which no Open-MOPD launcher invokes. None of the MT-OPD wiring has a Megatron path.

open_mopd_specific.why_specific: adaptive_kl_loss_reward_key defaults to the literal 'delta_opd/weighted_reward_mean' - the delta_opd signal hard-coded as a config default. It is also the only block in actor.yaml violating that file's own 'comment above each field / blank line between fields' CI rule.

report.purpose: Defines the entire Hydra config tree consumed by `verl.trainer.main_ppo` (config_name=`ppo_trainer`) and `verl.trainer.sft_trainer` (config_name=`sft_trainer_engine`), composed from per-component group YAMLs under `training/verl/verl/trainer/config/{actor,rollout,ref,reward_model,data,algorithm,model,optim,engine,critic}/`. A parallel dataclass layer (`BaseConfig` subclasses in `verl/trainer/config/*.py` and `verl/workers/config/*.py`) is instantiated from those DictConfigs via `omega_conf_to_dataclass` and carries the real type/validation surface (`__post_init__`, `validate()`), with `validate_config()` handling cross-section consistency. Open-MOPD's knobs are split unevenly across this layer: some are declared in YAML (`actor.adaptive_kl_loss_*`), some only in dataclasses (`rollout.log_prob_top_k`, `actor.opd_refresh_advantage`), and the whole `mt_opd.*` / `mt_reward_model_N.*` / `teacher_ref_reward_model` surface is declared nowhere and is reachable only through Hydra `+key=value` appends.
report.subsystem: config_schema (Hydra/OmegaConf configuration for Open-MOPD's vendored verl 0.7.0.dev)
uncertain: Whether `- algorithm@@algorithm.rollout_correction: rollout_correction` (ppo_trainer.yaml:34) composes at all, and if so whether the group lands at algorithm.rollout_correction or under a stray '@algorithm' node. hydra is not installed here (`import hydra` -> ModuleNotFoundError) and raw.githubusercontent.com is blocked, so I could neither execute the composition nor diff against upstream verl v0.7.0. The single-`@` form in the Megatron sibling and the CLI path documented at rollout_correction.yaml:2 both point at a typo, but I am not asserting it.

Whether Hydra at this repo's pin actually rejects `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.reward_mode=mt_opd` without a `+`. My conclusion rests on documented Hydra 1.x override semantics plus confirmation that the key exists in no YAML and in no dataclass; I could not run the launcher end to end. If the pinned Hydra behaves differently, opd.sh and mt_opd.sh are fine as written.

Which upstream verl v0.7.0.dev commit this tree was vendored from. Git history is unusable for the upstream/fork split - the whole tree arrives in one commit (a8d1f7f 'release Open-MOPD open recipe') and the only other commit adds a citation. My upstream-vs-Open-MOPD attributions therefore rest on the naming signals given in the task plus internal evidence (docstrings citing measured Open-MOPD numbers, dates like 2026-08-04, MT-OPD domain references), not on a diff.

The exact on-disk parquet schema beyond the fact that a top-level `domain` column is required and that all columns pass through RLHFDataset. Column dtypes and the full expected set belong to the data subsystem; I did not trace training/scripts/.

Whether any out-of-tree config supplies the mt_opd.* / mt_reward_model_N / teacher_ref_reward_model values used for the published runs. Nothing in this repository does, so how the paper's M1/M2/M3 settings were passed is not recoverable here. The comment at ray_trainer.py:671-673 mentions 'what the builder emits' and 'a dict-valued Hydra override fails to compose on the executor', implying an external launch builder not part of this release.

Whether trainer.data_proto_dump.stages accepts values beyond the default ['post_advantage']. I read the declaration and the enable/dir guards but did not enumerate the stage names the dump implementation recognizes.

Whether the `algorithm@algorithm: rollout_correction` form at ppo_megatron_trainer.yaml:19 is itself viable: it would merge rollout_is/rollout_rs/etc. flat into `algorithm`, and AlgoConfig has no such fields. Since AlgoConfig is never instantiated in the trainer path this may be harmless, but I did not trace the Megatron entrypoint.
Exact line counts for dp_actor.py and domain_weighted_sampler.py - I read only the relevant regions of those two, so those two numbers are approximate. All other line counts came from `wc -l`.

Then self.messages = df[messages_key], self.tools = df['tools'] if present, self.enable_thinking = df['enable_thinking'] if present.

EngineRegistry.new(model_type='language_model', backend=engine.strategy) -> FSDPEngineWithLMHead. DistributedSampler(shuffle=True, num_replicas=dp_size, rank=dp_rank, drop_last=True); train_batch_size_per_dp = data.train_batch_size // dp_size; StatefulDataLoader(collate_fn=SFTTensorCollator(data.pad_mode), num_workers=8, pin_memory=True, drop_last=True).

total_training_steps = trainer.total_training_steps or len(train_dataloader) * trainer.total_epochs; optimizer_config.total_training_steps patched; save_freq/test_freq accept the literal string 'after_each_epoch' which is replaced by steps_per_epoch.

resume_mode 'auto' reads latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt under default_local_dir (checkpoint_manager.py:183-192); 'resume_path' requires an existing path containing 'global_step_'; 'disable' returns 0. engine.load_checkpoint(path) then per-dp-rank data_{dp_rank}.pt restores the StatefulDataLoader iterator.

meta_info = {use_remove_padding, use_dynamic_bsz, max_token_len_per_gpu, micro_batch_size_per_gpu, temperature=1.0, global_batch_size, pad_mode, pad_token_id}; data = tu.get_tensordict(tensor_dict=collated_batch, non_tensor_dict=meta_info).

engine.train_batch: optimizer_zero_grad -> forward_backward_batch (assigns sp_size, all-reduce SUM of loss_mask into batch_num_tokens, assigns dp_size, prepare_micro_batches, per-micro-batch forward_step + loss.backward()) -> optimizer_step (clip to optim.clip_grad, skips the step when grad_norm is non-finite) -> metrics['grad_norm'].

prepare_model_inputs asserts pad_mode==no_padding (:727). With model.use_remove_padding=False (the hf_model.yaml default) the nested batch is converted to padded tensors using meta_info pad_token_id, attention_mask is rebuilt as ones over each real sequence, labels = roll(input_ids.values(), -1), and log_probs are returned as a jagged nested tensor keyed 'log_probs'.
loss = -masked_sum(log_prob.values(), roll(loss_mask.values(), -1)) / batch_num_tokens * dp_size, so the accumulated backward equals a global token-mean cross-entropy over the whole DP batch.

metrics['loss'] is the list of per-micro-batch losses; torch.SUM over it (:277) then all_reduce(AVG) over the dp group. Emits train/loss, train/grad_norm, train/lr, train/global_tokens, train/total_tokens(B), train/mfu (FlopsCounter.estimate_flops / world_size). Logged only from dp_rank 0 via Tracking(trainer.project_name, trainer.experiment_name, trainer.logger).

Runs when (is_last_step and val_dataloader is not None) or (test_freq > 0 and global_step % test_freq == 0): engine.infer_batch under eval_mode over the whole val_dataloader, mean of per-micro-batch losses, all_reduce(AVG), logged as val/loss.

Fires when is_last_step or (save_freq > 0 and global_step % save_freq == 0). Writes <default_local_dir>/global_step_{N}/{model,optim,extra_state}_world_size_{W}_rank_{R}.pt, huggingface/ (config + tokenizer + generation_config), fsdp_config.json, data_{dp_rank}.pt, and updates <default_local_dir>/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt atomically.

`python -m verl.model_merger merge --backend fsdp --local_dir global_step_N --target_dir OUT [--trust-remote-code]` produces the HF directory that scripts/local/rl.sh / opd.sh / mt_opd.sh take as --model.

[--generation-bos-token TOK] [--generation-pad-token TOK] [--qwen-preserve-assistant-content] [--smollm3-preserve-system-think-tags] [--smollm3-fix-system-boundary] [--fixed-date STR]
entrypoints.what_it_does: Copies the template tokenizer's chat_template onto the Base tokenizer (vocab untouched), applies the requested Jinja rewrites (raising if the expected block is absent), sets eos/pad, saves tokenizer + generation_config.json, then reloads and asserts get_vocab() is byte-identical to the Base vocab and that chat_template survived.

Per tokenizer: asserts tokenizer.eos_token_id is inside generation_config.eos_token_id, checks turn-boundary markers, asserts every assistant content string appears verbatim in the rendered text, asserts <think>/</think> counts are unchanged, builds MultiTurnSFTDataset(pad_mode=no_padding, truncation=right) and asserts loss_mask.sum()>0 for every row, and asserts SFTTensorCollator('no_padding') yields nested tensors. Prints 'NAME: PASS rows=... length=[min,max] trained_tokens=[min,max]'.

Requires CHECKPOINT_DIR/fsdp_config.json, rejects '://' URIs, runs `python -m verl.model_merger merge --backend fsdp --local_dir IN --target_dir OUT [--trust-remote-code]`, then asserts OUT/config.json exists. Default OUT = dirname(IN)/merged_hf/basename(IN).
