gotchas: sft.sh does NOT use sft_trainer.yaml. `-m verl.trainer.sft_trainer` (sft.sh:48) resolves to the Hydra config `sft_trainer_engine` (sft_trainer.py:378). sft_trainer.yaml belongs exclusively to the legacy `verl.trainer.fsdp_sft_trainer` (fsdp_sft_trainer.py:833), which no script in this repo launches. The two configs are mutually incompatible: engine path uses `model.path`, legacy path uses `model.partial_pretrain`; engine path has `checkpoint.*` at top level, legacy has `trainer.checkpoint.*`; engine default lr is 1e-3 (optim/fsdp.yaml:12) vs 1e-5 in sft_trainer.yaml:51.

Only `data.pad_mode=no_padding` works on the sft.sh path. transformer_impl.py:727 asserts `pad_mode == DatasetPadMode.NO_PADDING` in prepare_model_inputs, and engine/utils.py:70 asserts it again in postprocess_batch_func. The whole right-padding branch of MultiTurnSFTDataset (multiturn_sft_dataset.py:369-404) and the `response_mask` branch of sft_loss (losses.py:49-51) are unreachable from verl.trainer.sft_trainer; the latter would also KeyError because the SFT dataset never emits `response_mask`.

`data.truncation=error` set by sft.sh:52 is silently ignored. In no_padding mode MultiTurnSFTDataset unconditionally right-truncates to max_length (multiturn_sft_dataset.py:406-409) without consulting self.truncation. Over-long conversations are quietly cut mid-assistant-turn instead of raising. The truncation setting only matters in the unreachable right-pad branch (:380-392).

sft.sh defaults TRAIN_BATCH_SIZE=1 (sft.sh:29) while NUM_TRAINERS defaults to GPUS. verl.trainer.sft_trainer computes `train_batch_size_per_dp = global_batch_size // dp_size` (sft_trainer.py:173) with no divisibility assertion, so GPUS>1 with the default batch size yields batch_size=0 for the DataLoader. The legacy trainer does assert divisibility (fsdp_sft_trainer.py:141-147); the engine trainer does not. Always set TRAIN_BATCH_SIZE to a multiple of the GPU count.

The flat keys `data.messages_key`, `data.tools_key`, `data.enable_thinking_key` in sft_trainer_engine.yaml:25-27 are dead. MultiTurnSFTDataset reads them from the nested `config['multiturn']` block (multiturn_sft_dataset.py:63-66), which that YAML does not define, so the hardcoded defaults always win. Renaming the messages column requires `+data.multiturn.messages_key=<col>`.

MultiTurnSFTDataset enforces a rigid opening turn order AFTER tokenization: messages[0] must be 'system' or 'user' (else ValueError), and if it is 'system' then messages[1] must be 'user' and messages[2] must be 'assistant' (multiturn_sft_dataset.py:359-365). A system+user pair with no assistant turn raises IndexError rather than a clear error. A 'system' message anywhere other than index 0 raises ValueError at :331-332.

Turn-by-turn tokenization can disagree with whole-conversation tokenization. When it does, the code logs a warning and silently uses the concatenated token stream (multiturn_sft_dataset.py:262-275). Chat templates that rewrite earlier turns based on later context (Qwen's reasoning extraction, SmolLM3's /think substring rewrite) trigger this on every row, which is exactly why prepare_posttrain_tokenizer.py patches those template blocks and raises if the expected block is missing (:84-85, :97-99, :112-113).

Assistant supervision boundary: the generation-prompt tokens of an assistant turn get loss_mask 0 and everything after gets 1 (multiturn_sft_dataset.py:216-229). This is derived by string-length slicing of the rendered prefixes, so any template whose rendering is not a pure prefix-append per turn breaks the mask silently. validate_mixsft_chat_templates.py:135-138 is the guard: it asserts loss_mask.sum() > 0 for every row.

A per-message integer `loss_mask` field in the parquet overrides the derived mask for that entire turn, including its generation prompt (multiturn_sft_dataset.py:341-347). It must be a plain int 0 or 1; anything else asserts. Neither build_weighted_mix.py nor shard_sft_parquet.py emits this field, so it is only reachable with hand-built data.

The loss mask is left-shifted by one over the FLATTENED concatenation of all sequences in the micro-batch (losses.py:43), with no per-sequence boundary zeroing (upstream 0.6.0 had `loss_mask_flatten[cu_seqlens[1:] - 1] = 0`; both this snapshot and 0.7.0 dropped it). The last position of sequence i therefore inherits the first mask value of sequence i+1. It is benign for MixSFT data because every conversation starts with a system/user turn whose mask is 0, but it would leak if a sequence ever began with a trained token.

`trainer.save_freq` defaults to -1 and sft.sh does not override it, so a run writes exactly ONE checkpoint, at the final step (sft_trainer.py:351). Use `--extra trainer.save_freq=N` or the literal `trainer.save_freq=after_each_epoch` (:132-133) for intermediate checkpoints.

Setting `trainer.test_freq>0` without `data.val_files` crashes: fit() enters the validation block on `(self.test_freq > 0 and is_valid_step)` and then iterates `for val_data in self.val_dataloader` where val_dataloader is None (sft_trainer.py:327-330). This is upstream behavior, not an Open-MOPD change.

No consolidated HF weights are written. `checkpoint.save_contents` omits 'hf_model' (sft_trainer_engine.yaml:44), so global_step_N/ contains only per-rank sharded .pt files plus huggingface/ metadata (config + tokenizer + generation_config, no weights). The next pipeline stage needs `bash training/scripts/sft/merge_model.sh <global_step_N>`, which requires fsdp_config.json to be present and refuses remote URIs.

Checkpoints are world-size-bound: shard filenames embed the world size (`model_world_size_{W}_rank_{R}.pt`, fsdp_checkpoint_manager.py:225-227) and dataloader state is per-dp-rank (`data_{dp_rank}.pt`, checkpoint_handler.py:89). Resuming with a different --gpus will not find its shards.

Every path must be local. copy_to_local/copy_local_path raise ValueError on any string containing '://' (local_fs.py:11-14), and the launcher pre-checks the same (common.sh:190-194). There is no HDFS/S3 fallback anywhere on this path.

prepare_posttrain_tokenizer.py fails loudly by design: each --qwen-*/--smollm3-*/--fixed-date rewrite raises ValueError if its exact expected Jinja block is not found in the template (:84-85, :97-99, :113, :119), --eos-token/--pad-token must already exist in the Base vocab (:160-163), generation token ids must not resolve to unk (:129-130), and after save it reloads and raises if get_vocab() changed or the chat template was lost (:176-179).

build_weighted_mix.py refuses partial targets: either every --source has a --target or none does (:172-173); with no targets, --total-rows is mandatory (:176-177). sample_rows raises if a source has fewer rows than requested (:114-115). A non-empty --output-dir raises FileExistsError unless --overwrite (:166-167). The final source absorbs the rounding remainder (:183-185).

build_weighted_mix.py loads every source fully into Python memory as dicts before sampling (:52-76, :190-197). The released mix is ~1.15M rows (run_full_mix_debug.sh:22-24: 459646 + 459646 + 229823), so this is a large-RAM operation, and run_full_mix_debug.sh `rm -rf`s the output dir first (:13).

normalize_record str()-coerces everything and drops unknown columns: only messages/domain/source/dataset/split/difficulty/sample_id survive, role and content are forced to str, and a missing id falls back through sample_id/source_row_index/key to '' (build_weighted_mix.py:79-110, shard_sft_parquet.py:40-74). Any other metadata in the source parquet is lost.

validate_mixsft_chat_templates.py must be run with training/verl on PYTHONPATH (it imports verl.utils.dataset.*) and it iterates EVERY row of --data building the dataset item for each (:115-140), so point it at one small shard, not the full mix.

open_mopd_specific.what: The whole scripts/local/ launcher family, including sft.sh
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Not part of verl. Dry-run-by-default design, local-path-only validation (common.sh:190-194 rejects '://'), and TEACHER_DOMAINS/LOCAL_DOMAINS plumbing shared with mt_opd.sh (common.sh:31).

open_mopd_specific.what: training/scripts/sft/: the MixSFT data-prep and tokenizer-preparation toolchain
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: No upstream verl counterpart. The Jinja rewrites are named for this project: prepare_posttrain_tokenizer.py:82 '# OpenOPD data already contains the complete <think>...</think> block.' and :95 '# Preserve literal <think>...</think> instructions from OpenOPD data.'

open_mopd_specific.location: /data/ycfeng/Open-MOPD/training/verl/verl/utils/local_fs.py:1 (docstring 'Local path helpers for the OpenOPD trainer.'), :11-14 (_local raises on '://'); import sites multiturn_sft_dataset.py:31, sft_dataset.py:29, checkpoint_handler.py:24, fsdp_checkpoint_manager.py:32
open_mopd_specific.what: verl.utils.local_fs / verl.utils.local_io replacing verl.utils.fs / verl.utils.hdfs_io; all HDFS support stripped from the SFT path
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Upstream verl 0.6.0 and 0.7.0 both ship verl/utils/fs.py + verl/utils/hdfs_io.py; this repo ships local_fs.py + local_io.py and deletes every hdfs_io call. Concretely: trainer.default_hdfs_dir was removed from sft_trainer_engine.yaml and sft_trainer.yaml, removed from CheckpointHandler.__init__, and the HDFS copy blocks were deleted from CheckpointHandler.save_checkpoint and FSDPSFTTrainer.save_checkpoint.

open_mopd_specific.what: Resume actually takes effect: resume_global_step is taken from the CheckpointHandler return value
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Upstream verl 0.6.0 sets self.resume_global_step = 0 and then calls self.ckpt_handler.load_checkpoint() discarding the return value, so a resumed run restarted its step counter at 0. This snapshot assigns the returned step, which also fixes start_epoch (:237) and the total-steps early exit.

open_mopd_specific.what: Per-micro-batch losses are SUMmed, not MEANed, before the DP all-reduce
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Upstream 0.6.0 used torch.mean here. Because sft_loss already divides each micro-batch loss by the GLOBAL batch_num_tokens (losses.py:48), summing is the correct reconstruction of the global token-mean; mean under-reports by the micro-batch count.

open_mopd_specific.what: Per-rank traceback printed before distributed teardown
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Upstream 0.6.0 calls trainer.fit() then destroy_global_process_group() with no try/except. The added comment states the motivation: a failed rank otherwise blocks in destroy_process_group while its peers only report a secondary NCCL watchdog timeout.

open_mopd_specific.location: /data/ycfeng/Open-MOPD/training/verl/verl/utils/dataset/multiturn_sft_dataset.py:133-164, with all 4 call sites rewritten at :189, :197, :208, :290
open_mopd_specific.what: MultiTurnSFTDataset._apply_chat_template helper that forwards enable_thinking only when the row supplies it
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Absent from verl 0.6.0, which splatted **self.apply_chat_template_kwargs and always passed enable_thinking=enable_thinking. The docstring names SmolLM3 and the exact failure mode (an empty <think> block injected in front of responses that already contain a complete thinking block), matching prepare_posttrain_tokenizer.py's --smollm3-* flags. verl 0.7.0 later adopted the same conditional idea in a different, inline form, so this particular helper is this repo's own implementation.

open_mopd_specific.what: Checkpoint generation_config is sourced from the post-training tokenizer package first
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Absent from both verl 0.6.0 and 0.7.0, which only tried GenerationConfig.from_pretrained(model_config.name_or_path) and silently skipped on failure. Here the tokenizer's name_or_path is tried first, the model config second, and GenerationConfig.from_model_config is a guaranteed fallback, with the comment 'A separate post-training tokenizer package may define turn-end stop IDs that differ from the Base model EOS.' Without it a MixSFT checkpoint would inherit the Base model's pretraining EOS/stop behavior.

open_mopd_specific.what: HFModelConfig prefers the tokenizer directory's generation_config.json
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Absent from verl 0.6.0 and 0.7.0. Same motivation, stated in the inline comment; this is what makes model.tokenizer_path a full generation-contract override rather than just a vocab source.

open_mopd_specific.what: SFTTensorCollator restricted to the tensor keys of batch[0]
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: verl 0.7.0 unions keys across the batch and wraps non-tensor values in NonTensorData; this snapshot keeps only tensor keys. Practical effect on the MixSFT path: any extra non-tensor field a custom dataset returns is silently dropped instead of stacked.

open_mopd_specific.what: NOT part of this subsystem despite the name signal: DomainWeightedSampler
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: This Open-MOPD addition consumes the `domain` column that build_weighted_mix.py writes, but it is wired into the RL trainer only. The SFT dataloader uses a plain DistributedSampler (sft_trainer.py:168-170), so domain weighting during MixSFT happens offline via row allocation in build_weighted_mix.py, not via a sampler.

open_mopd_specific.location: /data/ycfeng/Open-MOPD/training/verl/tests/ (20 test files, all RL/OPD: test_delta_opd_reward.py, test_exopd_*, test_mt_opd_*, test_domain_weighted_sampler.py, ...)
open_mopd_specific.what: The MixSFT stage has no unit test in the repo
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Grep over training/verl/tests finds no SFT trainer or MultiTurnSFTDataset test. The stage's only executable check is training/scripts/sft/validate_mixsft_chat_templates.py, which is a standalone CLI rather than a pytest module.

report.purpose: Stage 1 of the Open-MOPD pipeline: turn per-domain instruction datasets (math / code / instruction-following) into one normalized, weighted, sharded `messages`-schema parquet mix, then run multi-turn SFT on a Base model that has been given an official post-training chat template, producing the MixSFT initialization used by the 3 domain RL teachers and by the student in multi-teacher on-policy distillation. Training runs through `torchrun -m verl.trainer.sft_trainer` (the engine/BaseEngine SFT trainer, Hydra config `sft_trainer_engine.yaml`), which tokenizes each conversation turn-by-turn to build a token-level `loss_mask` that is 1 only on assistant content, then computes a globally token-normalized cross-entropy. Checkpoints are written as per-rank FSDP sharded `.pt` files plus HF metadata under `trainer.default_local_dir` and must be merged to HF format with `verl.model_merger` before the RL/OPD stages can consume them.
report.subsystem: sft_stage (MixSFT: weighted multi-domain SFT mix construction + engine-based SFT training)
uncertain: Exact provenance of the vendored snapshot. The repo declares verl 0.7.0.dev (training/verl/verl/version/version) and git history contains only 2 squashed commits, so no in-repo diff exists. I downloaded the released verl 0.6.0 and 0.7.0 wheels and diffed: 0.6.0 is the close ancestor, and everything I attributed to Open-MOPD is absent from BOTH wheels. For _apply_chat_template specifically, upstream 0.7.0 implements the same 'only forward enable_thinking when provided' idea in a different inline form, so I cannot rule out that an intermediate upstream dev commit introduced a similar helper; the SmolLM3-specific docstring and its alignment with prepare_posttrain_tokenizer.py make Open-MOPD authorship the strong reading.

Whether the released MixSFT checkpoint was produced by the engine trainer (verl.trainer.sft_trainer) or the legacy fsdp_sft_trainer.py. Only the engine path has a launcher in this repo, and README.md:70 reports 'MixSFT (epoch 4)' which matches sft_trainer_engine.yaml's total_epochs default of 4 rather than sft.sh's TOTAL_EPOCHS default of 1, so the published run did not use sft.sh's defaults verbatim. The production hyperparameters (lr, train_batch_size, max_length, save_freq) are not recorded anywhere in the repo.

The concrete source datasets behind MATH_SOURCE / CODE_SOURCE / IF_SOURCE in run_full_mix_debug.sh. The source names ('math_oda', 'code_ocr', 'instruction_nemotron') and build_ocr_shards.py imply OpenCodeReasoning for code and a Nemotron-derived set for instruction following, but the scripts require the operator to supply local paths and no download or manifest step exists in the repo.

Whether data.shuffle / data.seed are ever set in practice. They are read by both dataset classes but appear in no YAML under training/verl/verl/trainer/config/ and in no launcher, so max_samples subselection is head-of-file by default.

Whether `model.dtype` (workers/config/model.py:93, default 'bf16') affects the SFT path at all. The FSDP engine initializes the module from `engine.model_dtype` (transformer_impl.py:187-195, default fp32); I did not trace every other consumer of HFModelConfig.dtype.

The --prompt-style {plain,lcb} argument of build_ocr_shards.py is parsed (:17) and echoed into summary.json (:114) but I found no code that branches on it; build_messages (:25-26) always emits the raw input text as the user turn. It reads as dead/unimplemented config rather than a working switch.

I could not execute OmegaConf to prove that `config.get('multiturn', {})` returns the default under Hydra's struct mode (omegaconf is not importable in this environment). The dead-key conclusion rests on code reading plus the fact that the same constructor calls `config.get('shuffle', False)` and `config.get('seed')` for keys that also do not exist in sft_trainer_engine.yaml, so a raising `.get` would make the trainer unstartable.

corrections.claim: gotcha: "prepare_posttrain_tokenizer.py fails loudly by design: each --qwen-*/--smollm3-*/--fixed-date rewrite raises ValueError if its exact expected Jinja block is not found in the template (:84-85, :97-99, :113, :119)"
corrections.why_wrong: Three of the four flags raise unconditionally, but --smollm3-fix-system-boundary has an idempotency escape hatch: if the primary block is absent AND a second marker string is already present, it silently proceeds without raising.
corrections.correct_fact: --smollm3-fix-system-boundary is a silent no-op (not an error) when the template already carries the fixed form. The code is `if old in template: template = template.replace(old, new, 1)` / `elif '<|im_end|>\\n" -}}\n{%- endif -%}\n{#' not in template: raise ValueError(...)`. So the ValueError fires only when neither the un-fixed block nor the already-fixed marker is found. --qwen-preserve-assistant-content (:84-85), --smollm3-preserve-system-think-tags (:97-99) and --fixed-date (:118-120) do raise unconditionally.

corrections.claim: gotcha: "normalize_record ... a missing id falls back through sample_id/source_row_index/key to '' (build_weighted_mix.py:79-110, shard_sft_parquet.py:40-74)"
corrections.why_wrong: The two normalize_record implementations differ, and the report merged them. build_weighted_mix.py has no `sample_id` fallback step.
corrections.correct_fact: build_weighted_mix.py falls back id -> source_row_index -> key only (3 steps). shard_sft_parquet.py falls back id -> sample_id -> source_row_index -> key (4 steps). Practical consequence: re-running build_weighted_mix.py over an already-normalized MixSFT shard (which carries `sample_id`, not `id`) writes sample_id="" for every row, silently destroying provenance; shard_sft_parquet.py preserves it.

That it is an upstream intermediate is provable from build_weighted_mix.py's normalize_record reading `row.get("split", row.get("ocr_split", ""))` -- an explicit fallback for exactly this producer.

corrections.claim: call_chain step "log_probs computation": "attention_mask is rebuilt as ones over each real sequence"
corrections.why_wrong: It is rebuilt from loss_mask, not from input_ids. The report's phrasing hides a real coupling: the synthetic attention_mask's per-sequence lengths come from the loss_mask nested tensor.
corrections.correct_fact: `attention_mask_list = [torch.ones_like(t, dtype=torch.int32) for t in loss_mask]` -- the mask is derived by iterating the loss_mask nested tensor, so any dataset whose loss_mask length diverges from its input_ids length silently produces a wrong attention_mask instead of an error. MultiTurnSFTDataset keeps them equal (multiturn_sft_dataset.py:407-409 truncates both), so this is latent, not currently broken.

missed.what: `train_time` is a dead accumulator: the end-of-run summary always prints 0.00s. It is initialized to 0 and never incremented, even though the per-step Timer (`timer.last`) is captured and used for MFU.
missed.location: /data/ycfeng/Open-MOPD/training/verl/verl/trainer/sft_trainer.py:250 (`train_time = 0`), :315 (`delta_time = timer.last`, used only for MFU), :356 (`print(f"Total time for train steps: {train_time:.2f}s")`). grep for `train_time` in the file returns exactly those two lines.
missed.why_it_matters: The report enumerated every emitted metric and the final-step print block but did not flag that the only wall-clock number a MixSFT operator sees at the end of a run is hard-zero. Anyone reading the run log would conclude the timer is broken or the run did not train.

missed.what: A reachable path where the run ends WITHOUT writing any checkpoint. `total_training_steps` is used only for the `is_last_step` comparison, while the epoch loop bound is `config.trainer.total_epochs` read independently. If `trainer.total_training_steps` exceeds `len(train_dataloader) * total_epochs`, the epoch loop exhausts, `fit()` falls off the end, and neither the final `ckpt_handler.save_checkpoint` nor the summary print ever runs -- with `save_freq=-1` (the default, which sft.sh does not override) that means zero checkpoints on disk. The same shortfall occurs on resume: `start_epoch = global_step // steps_per_epoch` skips whole epochs while StatefulDataLoader resumes mid-epoch, so the resumed run yields fewer steps than `total_training_steps`.
missed.location: /data/ycfeng/Open-MOPD/training/verl/verl/trainer/sft_trainer.py:122-126 (total_training_steps), :237 (start_epoch), :252 (`for epoch in range(start_epoch, self.config.trainer.total_epochs)`), :322 (`is_last_step = global_step >= self.total_training_steps`), :351-358 (save + return gated on is_last_step)
missed.why_it_matters: The report states total_training_steps "triggers the early return + final checkpoint" as if unconditional. It is conditional on total_training_steps <= steps_per_epoch * total_epochs. Given the report's own gotcha that save_freq=-1 means "exactly ONE checkpoint, at the final step," the failure mode is losing the entire MixSFT run's weights.

call_chain.detail: Each builder emits the same 5-column verl RL schema (data_source, prompt, ability, reward_model, extra_info). Math re-wraps the DAPO-Math-17k user text with MATH_RL_THINK_TAG_SYSTEM_PROMPT + MATH_RL_USER_SUFFIX; code serializes DeepCoder tests into reward_model.ground_truth as a JSON string; IF stores instruction_id_list + instruction_kwargs_json inside extra_info.
call_chain.step: 1. Offline: build per-domain RL prompt parquet

call_chain.detail: Adds a 6th top-level column `domain` in {math,code,if} plus extra_info.domain / extra_info.index=f"{domain}-{mix_index}" / extra_info.source_index / extra_info.mix_index. extra_info is normalized to ONE union struct (13 fields) so Arrow can hold all three domains in one column. build_mix_rl_union.py:87-115 does the same for the legacy 24K selection restore.
call_chain.step: 2. Offline: fuse the three domains into one MT-OPD parquet with a top-level `domain` column

call_chain.detail: `prompt` (data.prompt_key) is popped and rendered with apply_chat_template; every other parquet column (data_source, ability, reward_model, extra_info, domain) stays in row_dict verbatim.
Non-tensor values become np.ndarray(dtype=object) of shape (batch,). This is exactly how `domain` reaches non_tensor_batch['domain'] with no extra plumbing.

Reads dataset.dataframe['domain'] directly (raises if the column is absent, :58-59), Hamilton-allocates per-batch quotas from data.domain_weights (:18-33), cycles+reshuffles each domain pool so small domains oversample rather than truncate. Wired via data.sampler.class_path/class_name -> main_ppo.create_rl_sampler:438-449.

reward_mode=mt_opd hard-requires non_tensor_batch['domain'] (raises ValueError at :2110-2114), then build_domain_weights(domains, domain_order=mt_opd.teacher_domains) selects each row's teacher log-probs.
call_chain.step: 5b. mt_opd teacher routing consumes the same domain labels

call_chain.detail: get_custom_reward_fn(config) loads custom_reward_function.path via spec_from_file_location('custom_module', ...) and partials in custom_reward_function.reward_kwargs; if absent, falls back to default_compute_score (optionally partial'd with sandbox_fusion url/semaphore). Manager class comes from reward_model.reward_manager through the registry; reward_fn_key=data.reward_fn_key; **reward_model.reward_kwargs go to the ctor.

Per row i: slice prompts/responses by attention_mask, decode both, read non_tensor_batch['reward_model']['ground_truth'] (:174), non_tensor_batch[reward_fn_key] (:175), non_tensor_batch['extra_info'] (:176), inject num_turns/rollout_reward_scores into extra_info (:179-180), call compute_score(data_source, solution_str, ground_truth, extra_info) (:182-187), then write the scalar at reward_tensor[i, valid_response_length-1] (:246). Every key of a dict score is appended to reward_extra_info (:255-258).
call_chain.step: 7. Reward manager turns rows+responses into a token-sparse reward tensor

call_chain.detail: A linear if/elif ladder on the data_source string; unmatched sources raise NotImplementedError (:127). Open-MOPD appended two branches: startswith('livecodebench') -> rllm_code_reward.compute_score(scoring_mode='official_lcb') (:110-118) and 'ifeval' in ds -> instruction_following.compute_score(scoring_mode='official_eval') (:119-124). Return value is coerced: dict passes through, scalar -> float, else float(res[0]) (:129-134).

reward_func routes IF (_is_if: 'ifeval' in ds or ds.startswith('ifbench') or ds in {nemotron_if,ifbench,instruction_following}) -> instruction_following official_eval; code (_is_code: startswith('livecodebench') or ds in {livecodebench,codecontests_lcb}) -> rllm_code_reward official_lcb; EVERYTHING ELSE (math + unknown) -> ttrl_math.reward_func. _normalize collapses all outputs to exactly {'score','acc'} because ray_trainer asserts every reward_extra_info key list covers all samples.

When compute_true_reward=False and rm_scores exist, the manager returns the teacher-KL rm_scores immediately and never runs a rule scorer. When compute_true_reward=True it still runs the full rule pass but returns rm_scores as reward_tensor and stashes the rule tensor under reward_extra_info['true_reward_score'] (:280) - diagnostic only.
call_chain.step: 10. rm_scores short-circuit (this is the MT-OPD training path)

config_keys.effect: Which parquet column holds the chat-message list; it is popped out of row_dict and rendered by apply_chat_template.
Which non_tensor_batch key the reward manager reads to pick the scorer. Every reward manager uses self.reward_fn_key, so changing this changes the whole routing input.
RL prompt parquet path(s). Must be local paths.
Set to verl/utils/dataset/domain_weighted_sampler.py + DomainWeightedSampler to enable exact per-batch domain mixtures. Forces data.dataloader_num_workers=0 (asserted).

config_keys.default: {math:1, code:1, if:1} (NOT declared in any yaml - must be added with +data.domain_weights.*)
config_keys.effect: Per-batch quota weights for DomainWeightedSampler; positive floats only.
The batch size over which domain quotas are computed by the weighted sampler.
Seed for the weighted sampler's per-epoch pool shuffles (seed + epoch).
When reward_model.reward_manager=='mixed', dynamic (DAPO-style) group filtering keeps this per-domain quota instead of taking the first k uids, so filtering cannot bias the batch toward one domain.
Registry name of the reward manager class. Available in this tree: naive, prime, batch, dapo, instruction_following, mixed.

Forwarded as ctor kwargs to the reward manager (after stripping the _DISTRIBUTED_REWARD_KWARGS set). This is how compute_true_reward / length_cap_cfg / overlong_buffer_cfg / max_workers / enable_format_reward reach NaiveRewardManager.
False makes NaiveRewardManager return rm_scores immediately when they exist, skipping the (expensive, code-sandbox-heavy) diagnostic rule pass entirely.
answer_length_cap: reward = think_score + min(answer_score, piecewise-linear cap(response_len)). Requires the scorer to return answer_score/think_score keys (ttrl_math and rllm_code_reward do).
DAPO soft overlong penalty; mutually exclusive with length_cap_cfg (alc wins, checked first).
ThreadPoolExecutor fan-out for NaiveRewardManager's per-row scoring.
When set AND no custom reward fn is configured, default_compute_score is partial'd with the sandbox URL so codecontests/apps/codeforces/taco route to sandbox_fusion instead of prime_code.
Lets an OPD run reuse an inline (async-rollout-computed) score for VALIDATION only; training rm_scores stay reserved for teacher distillation.
Which reward-loop manager scores validation trajectories inline. 'opd_validation' selects OPDValidationRewardLoopManager.
Runs the custom reward function in a Ray task during log_prob instead of inline.
Loads an arbitrary module as top-level module 'custom_module'. For MT-OPD validation set path=.../verl/utils/reward_score/opd_val_dispatch.py and name=reward_func.
Merged into every scorer call with precedence over call-time kwargs. Carries scoring_mode, all IF guard knobs, and GRM endpoints.

Code: official_lcb|livecodebench_official|eval_official switches to the official LCB harness reading extra_info.metadata. IF: official_eval|eval_official|standalone_eval switches to the official IFEval/IFBench strict+loose evaluator; 'legacy' uses the raw constraint ratio. It also flips is_code_reward_config -> forces the distributed code reward path.
Size of the spawn ProcessPoolExecutor that runs ttrl_math (needed because ttrl_math uses SIGALRM, which is unsafe off the main thread).

Auto-switches an IF row to the official evaluator when it looks like an aligned val row (has eval_prompt_for_scorer, or evaluator in {ifeval,ifbench}, or metadata + dataset in {ifeval,ifbench_test,ifbench_mt_ifbench,ifbench_mt_ifeval}).
IF reward-hacking guards that cap or penalize rule-passing but semantically empty answers. All read from reward_kwargs; each contributes its own reward_extra_info keys.

LLM-as-judge gate applied ONLY to training rows that already pass every verifiable constraint (content_ok>=1). A NO verdict caps the score to _semantic_fail_cap. Only reachable through compute_score_batch (BatchRewardManager) or mix_rl_dispatch's IF branch.
config_keys.key: custom_reward_function.reward_kwargs.grm_* (endpoints, model, families, fail_cap, fail_mode, keep_think_on_fail, max_concurrency*)

config_keys.effect: 'opd_kl' = single-teacher OPD; 'mt_opd' = multi-teacher routing, which hard-requires non_tensor_batch['domain'].
Ordered domain labels; its length must equal 1 + number of mt_teacher_* logprob tensors, and each row's domain string must match one of these labels.
How many mt_reward_model_N worker groups to spin up.
Each extra RL teacher's model config; teacher N's per-token log-probs land in batch['mt_teacher_N_on_student_log_probs'].

config_keys.default: grpo in rl.sh; token_reward_direct hard-coded in mt_opd.sh
config_keys.effect: Selects the advantage estimator; MT-OPD uses token_reward_direct so the dense per-token teacher reward is consumed directly.

entrypoints.signature: default_compute_score(data_source, solution_str, ground_truth, extra_info=None, sandbox_fusion_url=None, concurrent_semaphore=None, memory_limit_mb=None, **kwargs) -> float | dict
entrypoints.what_it_does: The single data_source -> scorer routing table. Returns the scorer's dict verbatim when it returns a dict, else float(res) or float(res[0]). Raises NotImplementedError for any unmatched data_source (:127).

entrypoints.signature: reward_func(data_source, solution_str, ground_truth, extra_info=None, sandbox_fusion_url=None, concurrent_semaphore=None, **kwargs) -> {'score': float, 'acc': float}
entrypoints.what_it_does: MT-OPD validation dispatcher wired through custom_reward_function.path/name. IF -> instruction_following(official_eval), code -> rllm_code_reward(official_lcb), math AND every unknown data_source -> ttrl_math. Output is force-normalized to exactly {score, acc}.

Resolves a mixed-RL row's domain with a strict precedence: extra_info['domain'] -> ability/extra_info['ability'] -> data_source patterns. Raises ValueError when nothing matches (:57). This is the closest thing to a declarative domain registry in the reward layer.

Mixed-RL non-code scorer: math -> ttrl_math.reward_func, if -> instruction_following.compute_score_batch([one row])[0]. Deliberately raises RuntimeError for code (:84) because code must go through the shared subprocess testcase pool.

IF scorer. ground_truth is discarded (:624) - all supervision lives in extra_info. Default 'tiered_think_format' mode returns 1.0/0.8/0.2/0.0 from (format_ok, content_ok), then applies four optional guard layers. Returns ~30 keys including score, base_score, constraint_ratio, tiered_score, think_format_ok, content_ok, num_constraints, num_failed_constraints, answer_text, family.

BatchRewardManager entry. Per-row compute_score, then fans out a generative-reward-model judge over rule-passing TRAINING rows only and caps their score on a NO verdict. Adds grm_called/grm_pass/grm_capped/grm_penalty/grm_error keys to every row.
Arg-order adapter so NaiveRewardManager / custom_reward_function.name=reward_func can call compute_score.

entrypoints.signature: compute_score(data_source, solution_str, ground_truth, extra_info=None, max_tests=15, timeout=6, testcase_max_workers=1, scoring_mode='rllm', lcb_lm_style='CodeQwenInstruct', lcb_worker_concurrency=24, **_) -> dict
entrypoints.what_it_does: Two modes. 'rllm': JSON-decodes ground_truth into testcases and runs the vendored rLLM RewardCodeFn. 'official_lcb': ignores ground_truth and rebuilds a CodeGenerationProblem from extra_info['metadata'], running the official LiveCodeBench harness. Both wrap the pass rate as score = 0.2*think_format + 0.8*pass (_with_think_format_score:66-89).

entrypoints.signature: compute_score(model_response, gt_answer, fast=False) -> dict ; reward_func(data_source, solution_str, ground_truth, extra_info=None, sandbox_fusion_url=None, concurrent_semaphore=None) -> dict
entrypoints.what_it_does: Math scorer used by every Open-MOPD math path. score = 0.2*has_closed_think_block + 0.8*boxed_answer_correct. Returns score, think_score, answer_score, final_score, base_score, format_score, think_format_score, boxed_format_score, acc, extracted_gt, pred. reward_func re-raises on failure rather than returning 0.

The dominant reward manager. Decodes each row, calls compute_score, writes the scalar at the last valid response position, and mirrors every scorer dict key into reward_extra_info. Under rm_scores it returns the teacher tensor and files the rule score as reward_extra_info['true_reward_score'].

Calls compute_score ONCE with plural kwargs (data_sources=, solution_strs=, ground_truths=, extra_infos=) plus **reward_kwargs. Mutates extras[i]['rollout_reward_scores'] in place (:67-68) and writes data.batch['acc'] (:127). This is the only manager compatible with instruction_following.compute_score_batch.

Per-row scoring like naive but strips a trailing eos_token from response_str (:87-89) and applies the DAPO overlong penalty unconditionally (:120). InstructionFollowingRewardManager is a bare subclass registered as 'instruction_following'.

A guard, not a scorer: raises RuntimeError if rm_scores is missing, otherwise passes rm_scores through. Exists so the trainer's startup contract is satisfied without silently re-scoring an async-scored mixed batch.
The single factory: resolves the custom reward fn, picks the manager class from the registry, and injects reward_fn_key + reward_model.reward_kwargs.

gotchas: The `domain` column is NOT produced by anything under training/scripts/rl/. All four per-domain builders emit exactly 5 columns and no `domain`. Only experiments/data/build_mix_rl_raw_union.py (OUTPUT_SCHEMA:57-66) and build_mix_rl_union.py (:108) add it. Feeding a single-domain parquet to reward_mode=mt_opd therefore dies at ray_trainer.py:2110-2114, and to DomainWeightedSampler at domain_weighted_sampler.py:58-59.

extra_info must be ONE Arrow struct type across all three domains. build_mix_rl_raw_union.py:40-56 declares a 13-field union (split, index, source_config, sample_id, raw_prompt, instruction_id_list, instruction_kwargs_json, dataset, agent_name, family, domain, source_index, mix_index) and nulls out fields a given domain lacks (:88-91). The per-domain builders each use a different, narrower extra_info struct (math: {index}; code: {split,index,source_config}; IF: 7 fields), so they cannot be concatenated without this normalization.

extra_info.index is retyped to a string in the mix. build_mix_rl_union.py:100-103 explains why: math source indices are UUIDs and code's are integers, so the union stores source_index as str and rewrites index to f"{domain}-{mix_index}". _template_rows_by_domain (:58-84) then requires that exact "<domain>-<int>" shape, contiguous 0..N-1 indices, and 1:1:1 counts.

data_source values that no scorer claims. The code builder emits data_source in {taco, primeintellect, livecodebench} (build_deepcoder_rl_dataset.py:26-30). default_compute_score handles 'taco' (:74) and 'livecodebench' (:110) but NOT 'primeintellect' -> NotImplementedError at :127. Likewise the math builder's fallback 'math_dapo_boxed' (build_dapo_math_rl_dataset.py:101) matches no branch. Code/math training rows are meant to be scored by the async reward loop / rm_scores, not by default_compute_score, but any driver-side call on them raises.

data_source 'nemotron_if_rl' (build_nemotron_if_rl_dataset.py:22) falls through EVERY IF predicate: 'ifeval' is not a substring, it does not start with 'ifbench', and it is not in {nemotron_if, ifbench, instruction_following}. So default_compute_score raises on it (__init__.py:119,127), and opd_val_dispatch._is_if (:27-32) returns False, so the row is scored by ttrl_math (:62-63), i.e. graded as a math problem. opd_validation._is_if_data_source (:53-58) has the same hole. The val parquet the IF builder writes at line 191 carries exactly this data_source.

The IF training rows and the IF official evaluator read DIFFERENT extra_info keys. The builder writes instruction_kwargs_json (a list of JSON strings, build_nemotron_if_rl_dataset.py:84) which only compute_score's rule path consumes (instruction_following.py:635-636). _official_eval_score instead reads metadata['kwargs'] or extra_info['kwargs'] (:235) and metadata['instruction_id_list'] (:234). Running scoring_mode=official_eval on a raw nemotron_if_rl training row yields an empty kwargs list.

instruction_following.compute_score deletes ground_truth on its first line (:624). The IF builder consequently writes reward_model.ground_truth = "" (build_nemotron_if_rl_dataset.py:79). Any manager or metric that assumes a non-empty ground_truth for IF rows is wrong by construction.

opd_val_dispatch._normalize (:67-87) must collapse every scorer's output to exactly {score, acc}, and the reason is a hard trainer invariant: the val reward manager appends every returned key to a per-key list and ray_trainer asserts each list length == #samples. In a mixed MT-OPD val batch a math-only key like think_score would only appear on math rows -> AssertionError. Adding aux keys to any domain scorer re-breaks mixed validation.

opd_val_dispatch.py imports absolutely (`from verl.utils.reward_score import ttrl_math`, :24) on purpose: verl loads it via spec_from_file_location('custom_module', ...) as a top-level module, not a package member, so a relative import would raise 'attempted relative import with no known parent package'. The same applies to any new dispatcher file.

DAPORewardManager (and therefore InstructionFollowingRewardManager) dereferences self.overlong_buffer_cfg.enable unconditionally at dapo.py:120. Passing overlong_buffer_cfg=None (the ctor default at :36) makes __call__ raise AttributeError. NaiveRewardManager guards this correctly (naive.py:214); DAPO does not.

Setting custom_reward_function.reward_kwargs.scoring_mode to official_lcb/livecodebench_official/eval_official, or pointing path at rllm_code_reward.py / official_lcb_reward.py, silently flips should_use_distributed_reward() and should_flatten_reward_tests() to True (reward.py:70-90). The scoring_mode knob thus changes the execution topology, not just the metric.

reward_model.reward_kwargs is filtered before reaching the manager: the 12 keys in _DISTRIBUTED_REWARD_KWARGS (reward.py:39-51) are popped out (:66-67). A reward manager can never see distributed*/testcase_* kwargs.

NaiveRewardManager mutates extra_info in place: extra_info['num_turns'] and extra_info['rollout_reward_scores'] are injected before every scorer call (naive.py:176-180); BatchRewardManager writes extras[i]['rollout_reward_scores'] into the shared non_tensor_batch array (batch.py:65-68). Scorers therefore see keys the parquet never contained.

answer_length_cap and the DAPO overlong penalty are mutually exclusive, and alc wins because it is tested first (naive.py:204-220). alc also silently requires the scorer to return answer_score and think_score; with any other scorer it computes 0.0 + min(0.0, cap) and destroys the reward.

reward_extra_info['true_reward_score'] is a full (batch, resp_len) TENSOR while every other reward_extra_info entry is a per-row list (naive.py:280 vs :258). Downstream aggregation must special-case it.

mix_rl_dispatch.infer_domain raises rather than defaulting (:57), and its precedence is extra_info['domain'] > ability > data_source patterns. Note reward_func calls it WITHOUT the ability argument (:69), so the top-level `ability` column is only consulted on the reward-loop path (experimental/reward/reward_loop/mixed.py:141-145).

DOMAIN_ORDER is hard-coded to ('math','code','if') in domain_weighted_sampler.py:15 and is duplicated as a literal tuple inside ray_trainer.py:1820 and as dict literals at :1791-1793 and :1862. Adding a fourth domain requires editing all of these, not one registry entry.

DomainWeightedSampler requires data.dataloader_num_workers == 0 (asserted in main_ppo.py:450-455) and reads data_source.dataframe directly, so it only works with a dataset that exposes an Arrow-backed .dataframe carrying a `domain` column.

The code builder's prompt-length filter and the IF filter tokenize differently: build_deepcoder_rl_dataset.prompt_token_length uses apply_chat_template(tokenize=True, enable_thinking=False) (:137-145) while filter_nemotron_if_rl_parquet uses apply_chat_template(tokenize=False) then tokenizer(add_special_tokens=False) (:33-40). The second path matches RLHFDataset's own tokenization (rl_dataset.py:406-410); the first can differ by special-token handling.

build_deepcoder_rl_dataset swallows every per-row exception into a filtered_errors counter (:221-223), as does build_livecodebench_rl_val_dataset (:180-182). A systematically malformed source silently produces a small output parquet; only the summary json reveals it.

build_mix_rl_raw_union excludes code data_source == 'livecodebench' by default (:216-220) - i.e. the lcbv5 training rows the code builder emitted - as source decontamination against the LCB val set. --allow-code-lcbv5 turns that off.

ttrl_math uses SIGALRM for its sympy timeout (math_utils.timeout_ours), which is only legal on a process's main thread. OPDValidationRewardLoopManager therefore runs it in a spawn ProcessPoolExecutor (opd_validation.py:142-152). Calling ttrl_math directly from a Ray async actor's event-loop thread is unsafe.

instruction_following._load_official_instruction_eval serializes its import under a module lock and eagerly primes langdetect (:164-219) because a first-call race makes langdetect raise 'Need to load profiles', which the official IFEval checker treats as a PASS - the race produced silent false-positive language checks.

rllm_code_reward and instruction_following both compute the repo root as Path(__file__).resolve().parents[5] (:94 and :28) and import from evals.verifier.*. Moving either file, or vendoring verl at a different depth, breaks official scoring at runtime, not at import time.

build_deepcoder_rl_dataset.py:150-151 has a dead conditional: `pattern = "train-*.parquet" if source_config == "lcbv5" else "train-*.parquet"` - both branches are identical. And the assert at :95-97 is a tautology (it only runs when func_name is not None, then asserts func_name is in metadata), so it cannot catch the lcbv5 rows missing func_name that it appears to target.

inputs.name: data_source
inputs.shape_or_schema: pa.string(), top-level parquet column -> non_tensor_batch['data_source'] (np object array, shape (batch,)). Observed values: math 'math_dapo' (input passthrough) or fallback 'math_dapo_boxed'; code 'taco' | 'primeintellect' | 'livecodebench'; IF 'nemotron_if_rl'; code val = caller-supplied SPLIT_NAME (e.g. 'livecodebench_v5', 'livecodebench_v6').

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.shape_or_schema: pa.list_(pa.struct([('role',string),('content',string)])). Always [system, user] in all three builders. Popped by RLHFDataset (data.prompt_key) and rendered via apply_chat_template(add_generation_prompt=True).
inputs.source: build_dapo_math_rl_dataset.py:48-53; build_deepcoder_rl_dataset.py:70-74; build_nemotron_if_rl_dataset.py:74-77; consumed at utils/dataset/rl_dataset.py:313, 406-410

inputs.name: ability
inputs.shape_or_schema: pa.string(). math: 'MATH' (input passthrough); code: 'code'; IF: 'instruction_following'. In the mix it defaults to the domain when absent.

inputs.name: reward_model
inputs.shape_or_schema: pa.struct([('style',string),('ground_truth',string)]). style is always 'rule'. ground_truth: math = the boxed answer string; code = json.dumps(list-or-dict of testcases, with metadata attached for lcbv5); IF = "" (empty, unused by the IF scorer).

inputs.name: extra_info (math)
inputs.shape_or_schema: pa.struct([('index', string)])

inputs.name: extra_info (code train)
inputs.shape_or_schema: pa.struct([('split',string),('index',string),('source_config',string)]); source_config in {taco, primeintellect, lcbv5}

inputs.name: extra_info (code val)
inputs.shape_or_schema: pa.struct([('split',string),('index',string),('sample_id',string),('dataset',string),('request_id',string)])

inputs.name: extra_info (IF)
inputs.shape_or_schema: pa.struct([('sample_id',int64),('raw_prompt',string),('instruction_id_list',list_(string)),('instruction_kwargs_json',list_(string)),('dataset',string),('agent_name',string),('family',string)]). instruction_kwargs_json holds json.dumps(kwargs, sort_keys=True) per instruction (or the literal 'null'); family comes from classify_family().

inputs.name: domain
inputs.shape_or_schema: pa.string() in {'math','code','if'}; top-level 6th column of the MT-OPD mix parquet -> non_tensor_batch['domain']. Also mirrored into extra_info.domain.
inputs.source: build_mix_rl_raw_union.py:64,108 and :92-98; build_mix_rl_union.py:105-108; consumed at ray_trainer.py:2109-2114 and domain_weighted_sampler.py:58-62

inputs.name: extra_info.metadata (code val, official LCB)
inputs.shape_or_schema: JSON string or dict carrying the full LiveCodeBench problem: question_id/question_title + public_test_cases + private_test_cases. Detected by is_official_lcb_metadata (needs an id key AND a tests key).

inputs.name: solution_str (derived)
inputs.shape_or_schema: str, decoded from data.batch['responses'][i][:attention_mask[prompt_len:].sum()] with skip_special_tokens=True. DAPO additionally strips a trailing eos_token.

inputs.name: data.batch['prompts'] / ['responses'] / ['attention_mask']
inputs.shape_or_schema: (batch, prompt_len), (batch, resp_len), (batch, prompt_len+resp_len) int64

inputs.name: data.batch['rm_scores']
inputs.shape_or_schema: (batch, resp_len) float - the dense teacher-KL signal in OPD/MT-OPD, or an async-rollout inline score in mixed RL. Its mere presence changes every reward manager's behavior.

inputs.name: data.meta_info['reward_extra_keys']
inputs.shape_or_schema: list[str]; each name must also be a key of non_tensor_batch. Used to rebuild reward_extra_info on the rm_scores short-circuit path.

inputs.name: MixSFT parquet row
inputs.shape_or_schema: 7 flat columns: messages list_(struct(role,content)), domain string, source string, dataset string, split string, difficulty string, sample_id string; zstd-compressed shards named train-{00000..}.parquet plus summary.json.

open_mopd_specific.what: Eight entries added to verl/utils/reward_score/ that do not exist in upstream verl 0.7.0: code_testcase_runners.py, if_grm.py, instruction_following.py, mix_rl_dispatch.py, opd_val_dispatch.py, rllm_code_reward.py, rllm_vendor/, ttrl_math/
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Verified by unpacking the official verl-0.7.0 wheel: its reward_score/ contains only geo3k, gsm8k, __init__, math_batch, math_dapo, math_reward, math_verify, prime_code, prime_math, sandbox_fusion, search_r1_like_qa_em. Every other entry in this tree is an addition.

open_mopd_specific.what: Two reward managers added: MixedRewardManager ('mixed') and InstructionFollowingRewardManager ('instruction_following')
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: The 0.7.0 wheel's reward_manager/ has only abstract, batch, dapo, __init__, naive, prime, registry. The __init__.py diff also shows Open-MOPD dropping the upstream try-import of RateLimitedRewardManager.

open_mopd_specific.what: Two routing branches appended to default_compute_score: livecodebench -> rllm_code_reward(official_lcb) and 'ifeval' in ds -> instruction_following(official_eval)
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: diff against the wheel shows exactly this 20-line insertion and nothing else; the comment block explicitly names MT-OPD and explains that training advantage is unaffected because the manager short-circuits to rm_scores.

open_mopd_specific.what: NaiveRewardManager extended with compute_true_reward, length_cap_cfg (answer_length_cap), overlong_buffer_cfg + max_resp_len, enable_format_reward, max_workers, and the true_reward_score logging path
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: The wheel's ctor is exactly `def __init__(self, tokenizer, num_examine, compute_score=None, reward_fn_key="data_source")`. All six extra parameters, the _ALC_* helpers, the ThreadPoolExecutor fan-out, and the rm_scores/true_reward_score block are new. report.purpose: rl_data_prep owns two things: (1) the offline builders that turn raw public corpora (DAPO-Math-17k, DeepCoder, Nemotron-IF, LiveCodeBench) into the verl RL prompt parquet the three domain RL teachers and the MT-OPD student consume, plus the MixSFT parquet the pipeline starts from; and (2) the runtime reward layer that turns a dataset row plus a sampled response into a scalar written into a token-sparse reward tensor. The bridge between the two halves is the `data_source` string, which is the sole routing key from a parquet row to a domain scorer, and the Open-MOPD-added `domain` column, which is the routing key from a row to its RL teacher. In MT-OPD training the reward layer is mostly bypassed: the learning signal is the teacher-KL `rm_scores`, and the rule scorers survive only as validation metrics and as a logged-only `true_reward_score`.
report.subsystem: rl_data_prep (domain-RL data preparation + reward functions + reward managers)
uncertain: No committed script sets custom_reward_function.path to opd_val_dispatch.py. Its module docstring says 'OPD jobs set custom_reward_function', and scripts/local/rl.sh:68-73 is the only committed launcher that wires custom_reward_function at all (via REWARD_FUNCTION_PATH/NAME env vars, defaulting name to 'compute_score', not 'reward_func'). scripts/local/opd.sh and mt_opd.sh do not set it. Likewise no committed script sets reward_model.reward_manager, data.sampler.class_path, data.domain_weights, or reward_model.reward_kwargs.compute_true_reward. All are reachable and self-consistent in code, but the actual per-stage values used for the paper's runs are not in any tracked yaml or shell script I found.

The MT-OPD validation parquet's actual data_source values. Which reward manager each of the three domain RL teachers actually used. 'instruction_following' is registered and is a DAPO subclass, but DAPO's __call__ raises AttributeError on a None overlong_buffer_cfg, so it must have been given one; the values are not in the repo.

numpy array -> list; a str starting with '[' is json-parsed into a chat list; a list goes through tokenizer.apply_chat_template(tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True, [enable_thinking=...]); a plain str passes through raw. So the `prompt` column may be a raw prompt string, a chat message list, or the JSON string of that list.

One output row per (input row x completion): original row dict + completion_index, completion, completion_tokens, finish_reason, stop_reason, generated_special_token_counts. An empty result.outputs emits one row with completion="" and completion_tokens=0 and NO finish_reason/stop_reason/generated_special_token_counts keys (l.279-285), so the schema is ragged in that case.

file_suffix = f"base{base}_offset{offset}_rank{rank}" when offset is truthy else f"base{base}_rank{rank}" (l.304). With a `dataset` column: groupby('dataset') and write {dataset}_rollouts_{suffix}.parquet, backfilling blank/NaN dataset values from `_input_name` else path.stem (l.306-320). Otherwise a single {path.stem}_rollouts_{suffix}.parquet (l.321-324).

Reads all --rollout paths through a ThreadPoolExecutor (--read-workers; 'scheme://' paths handed straight to pandas, is_remote_path:124) -> pd.concat -> groupby('dataset', sort=False) -> score_dataset per group -> payload {results, macro_official, macro_live} -> write --output JSON and print the results table with official_extra dropped.

EXACT set membership on the `dataset` value: MATH_DATASETS{aime24,aime25}->score_aime; IFEVAL_DATASETS{ifeval,ifbench_mt_ifeval}->score_ifeval; IFBENCH_DATASETS{ifbench_test,ifbench_mt_ifbench}->score_ifbench; EVALPLUS_DATASETS{humaneval_plus,mbpp_plus}->score_evalplus; LCB_DATASETS{livecodebench_v5,livecodebench_v6,livecodebench_full}->score_lcb; anything else -> build_unscored(note='unknown_dataset').

total = official_total(dataset, data_dir) (utils.py:69-73), then overridden: math total = result['total'] = len(df) (aime.py:40); LCB total = scored_rows (score.py:106-107). official = correct/total when correct is an int; live = correct/scored_rows when correct is an int; when correct is a float (LCB/EvalPlus pass@1) BOTH official and live are that same float with no division; when correct is None both are None.
macro_official and macro_live are unweighted arithmetic means over the per-dataset official / live values that are not None. build_unscored datasets contribute nothing.

load_lcb_official_modules() (needs a livecodebench checkout) -> optional subset filter -> prepare_lcb_groups groups rows by `sample_id` (fallback `request_id`) and builds CodeGenerationProblem(**parse_metadata(first_row)) per group plus extract_code(completion, LMStyle) per row (livecodebench_official.py:65-85) -> write {details}/{stem}_outputs.json -> score_lcb_multi_process when process_workers>1 and problems>1, else single-process batching by --lcb-progress-interval -> write {details}/{stem}_eval.json -> pass@1 = mean over problems of the fraction of that problem's graded completions that are truthy (l.90-95).

ifbench=False uses the vendored google_ifeval package and best-effort patches in the ifbench registry (try/except at l.106-118); ifbench=True hard-requires repo_path('ifbench') on sys.path (l.92, unguarded). Per row: key = metadata['key'] else `sample_id` else positional index; instruction_id_list and kwargs from metadata else top-level columns; kwargs normalized (json/ast, drop None, float->int) then filtered to each instruction's get_instruction_args_keys(); response = strip_think_tags(completion) (l.84-85). Builds a prompt->response dict, then runs test_instruction_following_strict and _loose over every row.

_load_with_src globs {--rollout-dir}/*.parquet excluding *_scored.parquet (l.39-49) and concats with a temporary `_src_file` column -> lowercased --dataset substring dispatch (l.190-216) -> df['score'] = per_row -> rewrites EVERY source parquet in place per _src_file group (l.224-226) -> writes the flat summary JSON to --out (l.236-237).

call_chain.detail: ds = dataset.lower(); ds.startswith('aime') -> _math_rows (delegates to score_aime_row); 'livecodebench' in ds or ds.startswith('lcb') -> _code_rows (official LCB metadata path); 'deepscaler'/'deepcoder'/'farm' in ds, or ('code' in ds and 'livecodebench' not in ds) -> _code_farming_rows (testcases from the flat metadata JSON); ds == 'ifeval' or 'ifbench' in ds or ds.startswith('if') -> IF, where fn = score_ifeval ONLY for the exact string 'ifeval' and every other IF name goes to score_ifbench (l.201); otherwise it prints 'no scorer' and returns WITHOUT writing --out (l.214-216).

entrypoints.signature: python -m evals.rollout_engine.vllm_rollout --model M --input P1 [P2 ...] --output-dir D [--base 0] [--offset N] [--tensor-parallel-size 1] [--data-parallel-size 1] [--pipeline-parallel-size 1] [--dtype bfloat16] [--max-model-len 32768] [--gpu-memory-utilization 0.93] [--trust-remote-code] [--enable-prefix-caching] [--max-num-seqs 1024] [--max-num-batched-tokens None] [--temperature 0.6] [--top-p 0.95] [--top-k 20] [--n 1] [--max-tokens 30000] [--stop-token-ids 151643,151645] [--enable-thinking true|false] [--node-size 1] [--node-rank 0]
entrypoints.what_it_does: Offline vLLM generation. Forks one process per data-parallel rank, hard-pins each to its own tp_size GPUs via CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, slices each input parquet by [--base, --base+--offset) then by rank, and writes one rollout parquet per (dataset x rank) into --output-dir.

entrypoints.signature: run_file_partition(llm, path: Path, output_dir: Path, temperature: float, top_p: float, top_k: int, n: int, max_tokens: int, stop_token_ids: list[int]|None, enable_thinking: bool|None, dp_size: int, global_dp_rank: int, base: int, offset: int|None) -> list[Path]
entrypoints.what_it_does: The only unit-testable core of stage 1 (tests/test_vllm_rollout.py:100-144). Returns the list of written parquet paths.

entrypoints.signature: resolve_stop_token_ids(model_path: str, explicit_stop_token_ids: Any) -> list[int] | None
entrypoints.what_it_does: Explicit --stop-token-ids wins ('[a,b]' JSON, 'a,b' CSV, or scalar); otherwise loads transformers GenerationConfig.from_pretrained(model_path).eos_token_id.

entrypoints.signature: python -m evals.verifier.score --rollout P1 [P2 ...] [--output scores.json] [--data-dir evals/data/parquet] [--details-dir D] [--workers 160] [--read-workers 8] [--lcb-progress-interval 500] [--lcb-lm-style CodeQwenInstruct] [--lcb-process-workers 160] [--lcb-worker-concurrency 24] [--lcb-timeout 6] [--lcb-subsets v5,v6]
entrypoints.what_it_does: The aggregate scorer. Groups all rollout rows by the `dataset` column, dispatches via exact-set registries, writes {results, macro_official, macro_live} JSON. Does NOT modify rollout parquets.

entrypoints.signature: score_dataset(df, data_dir: Path, details_root: Path|None, workers=160, lcb_progress_interval=500, lcb_lm_style='CodeQwenInstruct', lcb_process_workers=160, lcb_worker_concurrency=24, lcb_timeout=6, lcb_subsets=None) -> dict
entrypoints.what_it_does: Returns keys dataset, metric, scored_rows, correct, official_total, official, live, official_extra plus the six behavior keys. On an unknown dataset or a scorer returning {'error':...} it returns build_unscored(): dataset, scored_rows=0, correct=None, official_total, official=None, live=None, note.

entrypoints.signature: python -m evals.score_rollouts --rollout-dir DIR --dataset NAME --out scores.json [--workers max(8, ncpu-2)] [--lm-style CodeQwenInstruct] [--timeout 6] [--max-tokens 30000]
entrypoints.what_it_does: The in-place scorer for eval nodes: adds a per-row float `score` column (1.0/0.0/NaN) back INTO every rollout parquet under --rollout-dir and writes a flat summary JSON with a truncation rate. Routing is lowercase substring matching, not the score.py registry.

Sums score_rollouts-style scores_livecodebench_v*.json shards into a per-model LCB v5/v6 scorecard. Both the model list and the run-directory prefix 20260624_ are hardcoded, so it only works on that one historical run layout.

entrypoints.signature: score_aime(df, dataset) -> dict{correct:int, scored_rows:int, total:int, metric:'avg_at_k_rows', official_extra:{unique_samples:int|None}}; score_aime_row(row) -> bool; extract_aime_final_answer(text) -> str
entrypoints.what_it_does: Row scorer compares extract_aime_final_answer(row['completion']) with extract_aime_final_answer(row['answer']) as ints when both parse, else as strings. Extraction: last \boxed{...} then the last integer inside it; else the last line that is a bare 1-3 digit number or contains exactly one such number; else the last integer in the whole text.

entrypoints.signature: score_lcb(df, details_dir, workers, progress_interval=500, lm_style='CodeQwenInstruct', *, data_dir=None, subsets=None, process_workers=1, worker_concurrency=None, timeout=6) -> dict{correct:float, scored_rows:int, metric:'livecodebench_pass_at_1', official_extra:{...}} or {'error': 'dependency_missing_or_invalid_livecodebench: ...'}
entrypoints.what_it_does: Official LCB runner wrapper. `correct` is a FLOAT pass@1 in [0,1] and `scored_rows` is the PROBLEM count, not the row count. official_extra keys: metrics{pass@1}, outputs_path, eval_path, metadata_count, workers, process_workers, worker_concurrency, rollout_rows, generations_per_problem, lm_style, plus subset-filter keys.

entrypoints.signature: score_ifeval(df, details_dir) -> dict{correct:int, scored_rows:int, metric:'strict_prompt_level_accuracy', official_extra:{strict:{...}, loose:{...}}, per_row_strict:list[float]}
entrypoints.what_it_does: Strict plus loose Google-IFEval evaluation after stripping <think>...</think>. Each of strict/loose carries prompt_level_accuracy, instruction_level_accuracy, prompt_total, prompt_correct, instruction_total, instruction_correct. per_row_strict is aligned to df row order and is what score_rollouts writes into the parquet.

entrypoints.signature: score_evalplus(df, dataset, details_dir, workers) -> dict{correct:float|None, scored_rows:int, metric:'evalplus_pass_at_1', official_extra:{samples_path, result_path, pass_at_k, parallel, rollout_rows}} or {'error': 'dependency_missing: evalplus (...)'}
entrypoints.what_it_does: Writes a {task_id, solution} JSONL, calls evalplus.evaluate(base_only=False, i_just_wanna_run=True), reports pass_at_k['plus']['pass@1']. scored_rows is the number of DISTINCT task_ids. Numeric mbpp_plus task ids are rewritten to 'Mbpp/<n>'.

entrypoints.signature: compute_behavior_metrics(df) -> dict{trunc_rows, repeat_rows, trunc_repeat_rows, trunc_rate, repeat_rate, trunc_repeat_rate}
entrypoints.what_it_does: Truncation needs BOTH completion_tokens and max_tokens columns, otherwise all False. Repetition fires when repeated_phrase_score>=8 OR repeated 6-gram ratio>=0.18 OR trailing-40-line repeat ratio>=0.25.

entrypoints.signature: official_total(dataset: str, data_dir: Path) -> int | None
entrypoints.what_it_does: Denominator for the official rate: len(pd.read_parquet(data_dir/f'{dataset}.parquet', columns=['request_id'])) when that file exists, else the hardcoded DATASET_TOTALS table (utils.py:18-30), else None.

TWO scoring entrypoints with DIFFERENT dataset routing. score.py uses exact-set membership; score_rollouts.py uses lowercase substring matching. They disagree on ifbench_mt_ifeval: score.py routes it to score_ifeval (score.py:28) while score_rollouts.py sends anything not literally 'ifeval' to score_ifbench (score_rollouts.py:201). Same rollouts, different official evaluator.

score_rollouts.py's module docstring (l.13) says math scoring is 'boxed-match vs reward_model.ground_truth', but the real path (_math_rows -> score_aime_row, aime.py:27) reads the flat `answer` column and never touches reward_model. A rollout parquet with only reward_model and no `answer` scores 0 everywhere without erroring.

score_rollouts.py rewrites your rollout parquets IN PLACE (l.224-226) with no backup and no confirmation. The `*_scored.parquet` exclusion at l.41 is vestigial: no code in the repo ever writes that suffix.
score_rollouts.py exits WITHOUT writing --out when the dataset name matches no branch (l.214-216), so a downstream consumer sees a missing file rather than an error.

`correct` changes type per scorer, which silently changes the meaning of official/live: int for aime (row count) and IF (prompt count), float pass@1 for LCB and EvalPlus. score.py:117-118 divides only in the int case; in the float case official == live == that pass@1 with no division at all. EvalPlus can return correct=None (evalplus.py:67) when the result file is missing, which yields official=live=None.

official and live are identical by construction for math (score.py:78 sets total = result['total'] = len(df), aime.py:40) and for LCB (score.py:106-107 sets total = scored_rows). The two rates genuinely differ only for IFEval/IFBench, where official divides by the DATASET_TOTALS/parquet size and live divides by the rows actually present.
`scored_rows` denominators are not comparable across scorers: rollout rows for aime and IF, distinct LCB PROBLEMS for score_lcb (livecodebench.py:98), distinct task_ids for EvalPlus (evalplus.py:70).

build_unscored (utils.py:85-94) omits `metric` and all six behavior keys that the success path emits, so the printed DataFrame and the results JSON have a ragged schema and carry an extra `note` key instead.

vllm_rollout.py's --offset filename tagging uses a truthiness test (l.304), so `--offset 0` yields the same base{B}_rank{R} name as no offset at all. Two runs differing only by offset=0 vs offset=None collide.

--data-parallel-size is process-level only: llm_kwargs never passes data_parallel_size to vLLM (l.90 comment plus tests/test_vllm_rollout.py:56-71). Each worker overwrites CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, so pre-masking GPUs before launch is ignored, and dp_size*tp_size must be <= the visible GPU count.

A row whose vLLM result has no outputs emits a row lacking finish_reason / stop_reason / generated_special_token_counts (vllm_rollout.py:279-285). pd.DataFrame.from_records then yields NaN for those in mixed batches, and the columns vanish entirely if every row is empty.

compute_behavior_metrics needs BOTH completion_tokens and max_tokens columns to detect truncation (behavior.py:66-69). The rollout writer does stamp max_tokens (l.260), but any hand-built rollout parquet without it silently reports trunc_rate = 0.0 instead of failing.

LIVECODEBENCH_CODEGEN_LITE_DIR's computed default is depth-sensitive: repo_path('livecodebench').parents[2]/benchmark_assets/livecodebench/code_generation_lite (livecodebench_official.py:16-19). Verified with OPENOPD_LIVECODEBENCH_REPO=/data/ycfeng/tmp/fake_lcb it becomes /data/benchmark_assets/..., nowhere near the README's evals/data/benchmark_assets. Set it explicitly.

livecodebench_official.load_lcb_official_modules os.chdir()s into the LCB checkout during import (l.27-45) and injects a fake `anthropic` module into sys.modules (l.22-26). It is called once in score_lcb (l.44), AGAIN inside prepare_lcb_groups (l.66), and once per parallel worker (livecodebench_parallel.py:13): repeated, un-cached, cwd-mutating imports.

The LCB model alias is hardcoded to 'Qwen/Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct' in both parallel paths (livecodebench_parallel.py:96,144) purely to satisfy the official LanguageModelStore lookup. It has nothing to do with the model under evaluation and is not exposed as a flag.

aggregate_lcb_scorecard.py is effectively dead for anyone outside the original run: MODELS (l.11-17) and the glob prefix 20260624_{model}_lcb_sharded (l.31) are hardcoded. It also reads TOP-LEVEL 'correct'/'scored_rows' with int(), which matches score_rollouts.py output but would truncate score.py's float LCB pass@1 to 0.

evals/rollout_engine/ and evals/verifier/scripts/ have no __init__.py; they work only as implicit namespace subpackages (verified importable via find_spec with origin=None). `python -m ...` works from the repo root, but a pip-install-style packaging of `evals` may drop them.

score_rollouts.py mutates sys.path at import time (l.34-36), inserting the repo root and training/verl. It is therefore usable only from a checkout, and it creates a dependency cycle: evals.score_rollouts -> verl.utils.reward_score.code_testcase_runners -> evals.verifier.score_functions.code.livecodebench_official.

vllm_rollout.py reads `_input_name` (l.311-313) as a dataset-name fallback, but nothing in this release ever writes that column (repo-wide grep: only those two lines). Dead code whose producer, build_data.py, was not released.

lcb_generation_passed (livecodebench.py:22-27) is exported and unit-tested (test_score.py:42-47) but never called by score_lcb, whose pass@1 loop uses plain bool(item) at l.91. Dead-but-tested helper.

inputs.name: input eval parquet (--input, stage 1)
inputs.shape_or_schema: Parquet, one row per generation request (already expanded by repeat). REQUIRED column: `prompt` (str, or list[{role,content}], or the JSON string of such a list; vllm_rollout.py:275,152-171). OPTIONAL but load-bearing downstream: `dataset` (str; controls the output file split at l.306-320), `answer` (str; AIME reference), `metadata` (dict or JSON str; LCB problem, IFEval constraints, or EvalPlus task_id+entry_point), `sample_id` (LCB/EvalPlus grouping key), `request_id` (LCB fallback grouping key and the column official_total counts in the full dataset parquet). Every other column is carried through verbatim into the rollout parquet via row.to_dict() (l.280).
inputs.source: Not produced by any shipped code: the documented builder evals/rollout_engine/build_data.py is absent from this release.

inputs.source: vllm_rollout.py:57-65; resolve_stop_token_ids:109-119; parse_optional_bool:122-125 (any value other than 'true' becomes False, and None omits the kwarg entirely)

inputs.name: rollout parquet (--rollout for score.py, --rollout-dir for score_rollouts.py)

open_mopd_specific.why_specific: The docstring describes an Open-MOPD operational pattern: grade on the eval node's hundreds of CPUs and write a `score` column back into the rollout parquet, plus a code-data-farming branch (_code_farming_rows) for DeepScaleR/DeepCoder-style training-data generation. open_mopd_specific.why_specific: aime24/aime25 (30 problems x 32 repeats), humaneval_plus, mbpp_plus, livecodebench_v5/v6/full, ifeval, ifbench_test, ifbench_mt_ifbench, ifbench_mt_ifeval: exactly the math/code/if three-domain split the MOPD pipeline distills, hardcoded as the eval matrix.

open_mopd_specific.what: official vs live dual reporting plus behavior counters
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Reporting a full-dataset-denominator rate and a submitted-rows rate side by side, with truncation/repetition counters on every result, is an Open-MOPD convention for judging partially-completed distillation checkpoints.

open_mopd_specific.what: Vendored Google IFEval instead of a pip dependency, with cross-registry patching
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: Google's IFEval is copied into the repo (its README is the upstream Google text) and its INSTRUCTION_DICT is cross-patched with the IFBench registry via setdefault, so IFEval-only and IFBench-only instruction ids both resolve. That patching logic is Open-MOPD's.

open_mopd_specific.what: No mt_opd / opd_kl / delta_opd / exopd / token_reward_direct / teacher_domains / mt_reward_model_N / domain_weighting / target_gradient_shares anywhere under evals/
open_mopd_specific.why_specific: The eval layer is fully decoupled from the distillation trainer: it consumes only model checkpoints and parquet files. The distillation-specific naming lives under training/, and the only shared surface is the scoring code reused by RL validation via code_testcase_runners.

report.purpose: The evals layer is a self-contained, Hydra-free two-stage offline benchmark harness for Open-MOPD checkpoints, deliberately decoupled from the distillation trainer: stage 1 (evals/rollout_engine/vllm_rollout.py) does multi-process data-parallel vLLM generation from eval parquet files, and stage 2 grades those rollouts with the official third-party verifiers for math (AIME), code (EvalPlus, LiveCodeBench) and instruction following (Google IFEval, AllenAI IFBench). There are two competing stage-2 entrypoints with different dataset routing: evals/verifier/score.py (exact-name registry sets, aggregate JSON only, reports both an official and a live rate) and evals/score_rollouts.py (lowercase substring matching, writes a per-row score column back into the rollout parquet in place, plus a flat summary with a truncation rate). The same scoring primitives are reused by RL validation through verl/utils/reward_score/code_testcase_runners.py so eval numbers and in-training val numbers line up. This release ships the code but not the data-building, asset-fetching, third-party-lockfile, or run-all-shell pieces its README documents.
uncertain: The exact on-disk schema of the eval input parquets cannot be recovered from source, only inferred from readers, because the producer (evals/rollout_engine/build_data.py) is not in this release. In particular the metadata column's per-dataset content (LCB CodeGenerationProblem field names, IFEval key/instruction_id_list/kwargs, EvalPlus task_id/entry_point) is inferred from how the scorers unpack it, and the README's claimed repeat_idx expansion column is never read by any shipped eval code.

Whether evals/verifier/score_functions/instruction_following/google_ifeval/ was modified relative to upstream Google IFEval. The vendored README is the upstream text and no patch or diff ships, so I cannot tell whether instructions.py or evaluation_lib.py carry local edits.

The pinned commits and repo URLs for evalplus / ifbench / livecodebench, and the content of the LiveCodeBench offline-asset patch. repos.lock.json and third_party/patches/ do not ship, so the exact third-party versions the reported numbers were produced with are unrecoverable from this repo.

End-to-end verification of the code and IF scoring paths. I confirmed the aime/behavior/dispatch paths empirically (7/7 verifier tests pass) and confirmed the failure modes for IF (absl missing) and third-party resolution (no lockfile), but I could not execute score_lcb / score_evalplus / score_ifbench against real assets, so their output shapes are read off the source rather than observed.

Whether --lcb-subsets was ever exercised: filter_lcb_subsets silently returns the unfiltered frame with a filter_note when data_dir is missing or yields no ids, and no shipped data-dir exists to test it against.

Whether score_rollouts.py or score.py is the intended production path for the numbers in the Open-MOPD paper/README. Both exist, they disagree on ifbench_mt_ifeval routing and on the type of `correct` for LCB, and aggregate_lcb_scorecard.py only consumes the score_rollouts.py shape.
